chapters.label: Prologue
chapters.title: To Question
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A belief that rejects the official teachings of a religion.
In a slow, relaxed, unhurried way.
Unpleasantly cold and damp, especially of skin.
A personal charm that draws people's attention.
Showing the separated colours of a rainbow, like light through a prism.
A nickname or extra name by which someone is known.
The crime of betraying one's own ruler or country.
A voice that rises and falls in a regular, musical way.
A senior Alethi servant, dressed in black and white, who oversees others.
An Alethi woman's left hand, which modesty requires her to keep covered.
King of Alethkar, murdered by a Shin assassin on the night he signed a treaty with the Parshendi. His death started the war on the Shattered Plains.
Gavilar's daughter: a famous scholar, an open atheist, and the woman who took Shallan as her ward in the last book.
The Shin assassin in white, who fights with a Shardblade and can make people and things fall in any direction.
The name Jasnah gave, at the end of the last book, to the strange place of glass beads and a dark sky that Shallan glimpsed.

quiz.q: What unsettling thing does Jasnah notice as she crosses the feast hall?
o: A Parshendi drummer staring at her
Her wine cup has been tampered with
Her shadow pointing the wrong way
A crack spreading up the hall wall
quiz.e: Her shadow points toward a sphere lamp instead of away from it, something that has happened to her before.

quiz.q: Whom does Jasnah find her father talking with privately in the servants' hallway?
o: Brightlord Meridas Amaram
Highprince Torol Sadeas
Her uncle Dalinar Kholin
The Parshendi elder Klade
quiz.e: Gavilar is speaking quietly and harshly with Amaram, whom he has long hoped Jasnah might marry.

quiz.q: Why is Tearim, captain of the King's Guard, wearing Shardplate?
o: He had won it in a duel that week
Dalinar lent it to him for the feast
It was a gift from the Parshendi
Gavilar has begun letting him wear it
quiz.e: Gavilar has stopped wearing his own Plate and entrusts it to Tearim, a renowned duelist.

quiz.q: What happens when the dark, oily figure glances at the wall?
o: The lamps explode in a burst of light
The palace shatters into glass beads
Jasnah faints and wakes in her rooms
A highstorm tears through the hallway
quiz.e: The palace breaks into countless glass beads and Jasnah falls into a sea of them under a dark sky.

quiz.q: How does Jasnah keep from drowning in the sea of beads?
o: She grabs a floating door and climbs on
She commands the palace's bead to rise
The dark figure lifts her from the sea
She calls out the name of a Herald
quiz.e: Each bead holds the pattern of an object. She pours her power into the bead of the palace, and a hallway of beads rises beneath her.

quiz.q: What does Jasnah finally hire Liss to do?
o: Kill the Shin servant from the feast
Guard Gavilar for the rest of the night
Steal letters from Amaram's rooms
Spy on her brother Elhokar's wife
quiz.e: She swaps the first envelope for a second one: Liss is to become a maid to Aesudan and only watch, for now.

quiz.q: Why did Liss get rid of her Shin servant?
o: He was too good a servant, and creepy
He kept trying to run back home
He refused to ever touch a weapon
He was caught stealing from her
quiz.e: Liss sold him to a slaver because he was “too good a servant” and unnerved her. He is the assassin who kills Gavilar.

quiz.q: What reason does Gangnah give for the Parshendi having Gavilar killed?
o: He had insulted the Parshendi drummers
He had refused to sign their treaty
He was about to do something dangerous
Their gods demanded a royal sacrifice
quiz.e: Gangnah admits the Parshendi hired the assassin because Gavilar “was about to do something very dangerous,” and says nothing more.

chapters.title: Santhid
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Extra items of equipment or clothing that go along with an activity.
To hold something out for someone to take.
Of a sailing ship, to change course by turning its front through the wind.
Rather stout and round in the body.
Bold in a reckless, unwise way.
A person or thing that is puzzling and hard to understand.
A heavy club; also anything used to overpower others by force.
A pole that sticks out forward from the front of a sailing ship.
The raised side of a ship’s deck; also any protective wall.
A dizzy feeling, often from looking down from a height.
The hard case in which a caterpillar changes into a butterfly or moth.
Willing to agree or go along with something.
A paired writing device: what is written with one pen is copied by its twin far away.
Shallan became Jasnah’s ward secretly planning to steal her Soulcaster. She swapped it for a fake, only to learn Jasnah’s was itself a fake, and the theft was discovered.
The young ardent who courted Shallan in Kharbranth. He was really an assassin sent to poison Jasnah, and nearly killed Shallan as well.
Shallan’s brothers in Jah Keved are buried in debt after their father’s death, and the family’s own Soulcaster is broken.
Jasnah’s name for the strange place of glass beads and a dark sky that Shallan glimpsed during her first Soulcasting.
Jasnah believes the parshmen are the Voidbringers of legend, and has set out for the Shattered Plains to search for the lost city of Urithiru.

quiz.q: What startles Shallan as she sketches her memory of Shadesmar?
o: A raised pattern slides across her page
Her charcoal starts to move all by itself
Tiny glass beads roll across the paper
A face appears among the drawn clouds
quiz.e: A pattern rises from the paper like an embossing, then slides across it “like an axehound pup under a bedsheet.”

quiz.q: Why does Shallan want to be lowered over the side of the ship?
o: To prove to Yalb that she is not timid
To pry a crystal loose from its shell
To see if it is a fish or a tortoise
Nobody has ever drawn a live santhid
quiz.e: Every santhid scholars have examined washed up badly decomposed; she wants the first drawing of a living one.

quiz.q: What answer makes Jasnah spin around when she asks what spren are?
o: They’re fragments of storms
They’re living ideas
They’re souls of the dead
They’re servants of God
quiz.e: Shallan says spren are “living ideas,” and Jasnah tells her she is right.

quiz.q: How does Jasnah plan to deal with the broken Soulcaster?
o: She will buy its owners a new one
Shallan will take it back herself
Navani will try to repair it
She will Soulcast a copy of it
quiz.e: Navani, a renowned artifabrian, thinks she can fix it; it can then go to Shallan’s brothers to return to its owners.

quiz.q: Whom has Jasnah begun arranging for Shallan to marry?
o: Renarin, Dalinar’s younger son
Adolin, Dalinar’s elder son
A nephew of Highprince Sadeas
A wealthy Thaylen shipowner
quiz.e: Jasnah has started a betrothal to Adolin Kholin, and Shallan is delighted by the idea.

quiz.q: What secret does Jasnah call more important than Shadesmar and spren?
o: Fear is stronger than any loyalty
Wealth is the root of all authority
Power is an illusion of perception
Truth is whatever scholars write
quiz.e: She says most authority exists only as others perceive it, and that Shallan can create that illusion too.

quiz.q: How does Shallan finally get the captain to stop the ship?
o: She orders him as if he can’t refuse
She offers to double his fee
She has Jasnah order it for her
She threatens to jump in anyway
quiz.e: Copying Jasnah, she tells Tozbek it isn’t his to allow or disallow: “That is your order.”

quiz.q: What does Shallan see under the santhid’s shell?
o: A great fish with armored fins and teeth
A tortoise-like head on a very long neck
A swarm of crabs clinging to its flesh
A grey-blue mass with tendrils, one huge eye
quiz.e: Beneath the shell is a knotted grey-blue body trailing thick blue tendrils, with an eye as big as her head.

chapters.title: Bridge Four
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: The calm, rainy tail end of a highstorm.
To force someone to serve in an army.
A soldier who fights for pay rather than for a country or cause.
An officer in charge of supplies, food and equipment.
A junior officer ranking below a captain.
To choose not to do something.
To conquer and bring under control.
A badge or emblem showing rank or membership.
To shock or stir people into action.
Holding together well as a unit.
Grey-haired, often with a rough, weathered look.
A large body of troops made up of several companies.
A formal written document giving an order or a right.
At the Tower, Sadeas pulled his troops back and left Dalinar’s army to be slaughtered. Bridge Four went back and helped Dalinar escape.
Afterwards, Dalinar gave Sadeas his Shardblade in exchange for every bridgeman in Sadeas’s camp, and freed them.
Kaladin can draw Stormlight into himself, which heals him and makes him glow faintly. His men know; Syl, the spren at his side, is invisible to almost everyone else.
Amaram murdered Kaladin’s squad to take a Shardblade, then had Kaladin branded a slave. His forehead also bears the shash glyph, meaning “dangerous.”
Among Kaladin’s crew: old Teft, the Horneater cook Rock, Sigzil (who can read glyphs), one-armed Lopen, Moash, Skar, Hobber, and Shen, a parshman.

quiz.q: About how many former bridgemen are now Kaladin’s responsibility?
o: Nearly a thousand
Just over two hundred
Roughly five thousand
Barely a hundred
quiz.e: Kaladin counts nearly a thousand men across the barracks, to be combined into twenty crews of about fifty.

quiz.q: What job does Kaladin give Teft?
o: Guarding Dalinar’s two sons
Choosing and training forty leaders
Paying the men from Dalinar’s purse
Keeping the battalion’s records
quiz.e: Teft is to combine the crews and train two men from each team, forty in all, who will then train the rest.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin insist they keep Dalinar alive?
o: Syl has warned him of an assassin
He has sworn an oath to the king
His heir might sell them back to Sadeas
Dalinar owes them their back pay
quiz.e: Dalinar is the only one who has shown bridgemen compassion; Kaladin fears a successor would sell them back to Sadeas.

quiz.q: What rank does Kaladin plan to give Moash, Skar, Teft, Sigzil and Rock?
o: Sergeant
Squadleader
Captain
Lieutenant
quiz.e: He makes the five lieutenants, to fill the gap between sergeant and his own rank of captain.

quiz.q: What does Hobber ask the tattooist to add under his freedom glyph?
o: The name Dalinar Kholin
The date he was branded
The words “Bridge Four”
The glyph for his home town
quiz.e: He says he was not freed from Bridge Four but by it, and wants “Freedom, Bridge Four.”

quiz.q: Why does the tattooist at first refuse to tattoo Shen?
o: He is a parshman, so he’s property
His skin is too dark to show ink
He has no slave brand to cover
He cannot pay her in spheres
quiz.e: She says, “He’s property.” The bridgemen insist he is one of them, and she gives in.

quiz.q: What happens to Kaladin’s own tattoo?
o: Syl changes the glyph it shows
The tattooist refuses to finish it
He has it put on his arm instead
Stormlight pushes the ink back out
quiz.e: Stormlight in his body forces the ink out, and the tattoo melts away, leaving the shash brand visible.

quiz.q: What do the bridgemen do with their Cobalt Guard patches?
o: Sew them on their spear hafts
Cut them off: they’re Bridge Four
Give them to the guards’ widows
Burn them in the barrack’s firepit
quiz.e: Lopen points out the Cobalt Guard are dead; Skar cuts his patch off, saying “We’re Bridge Four,” and the rest follow.

chapters.title: Pattern
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Rule by priests; in Roshar’s history, a past era when the Vorin church governed.
Beliefs that an authority declares to be true beyond question.
A split or contrast between two opposed things.
To keep something going, often something false or harmful.
An old book made of bound pages (plural: codices).
A small round window in the side of a ship.
A design raised up from a flat surface.
Decoration made of curling, spiral lines.
A typical or perfect example of a kind of person or thing.
A sudden change of subject away from the main point.
A prayer written in glyphs, used for protection.
In the last book, strange figures with symbols for heads appeared in Shallan’s drawings and seemed to follow her, frightening her badly.
Shallan once turned a goblet into blood without any device, and Jasnah, it turned out, Soulcasts the same way; her “Soulcaster” is a fake.
The Knights Radiant once abandoned their oaths and Shardblades. The Vorin church remembers them as the Lost Radiants, traitors to mankind.
Jasnah openly does not worship the Almighty, which shocks devout Vorins like Shallan.

quiz.q: According to Jasnah’s book, what did the Hierocracy do to ancient texts?
o: Burned every copy it could find
Made altered copies to fit its dogma
Locked them away in Kharbranth’s vaults
Sold them to Thaylen merchants
quiz.e: It made modified copies of ancient texts, aligning history to match Hierocratic dogma.

quiz.q: How did Jasnah respond when Shallan asked for a copy of this book?
o: She refused and Shallan took it
She assigned it on the very first day
She was hesitant, then dug it out
She said it was full of errors
quiz.e: Jasnah hadn’t assigned it and was reluctant, having to dig it out of a trunk in the hold.

quiz.q: What does Shallan switch to partway through drawing the pattern?
o: Pen and ink, for crisper lines
A larger sheet of sketch paper
Coloured chalk from her trunk
A brush with diluted ink
quiz.e: Pencil suits soft, living things; this needed sharper lines, so she switches to pen and ink.

quiz.q: What happens as the last line of ink dries?
o: The pattern sighs and leaves the page
The page bursts into a spray of light
The creationspren swarm onto the paper
The drawing fades as if never there
quiz.e: The pattern rises with what sounds like a sigh of relief and moves from the paper onto the floor.

quiz.q: What is standing in Jasnah’s palm when Shallan opens the door?
o: A tiny ribbon of glowing white light
A small symbol-headed creature
A little inky man in a long coat
A sphere glowing a deep violet
quiz.e: A small figure of inky blackness in a fashionable long-coated suit; it melts into shadow when it sees Shallan.

quiz.q: By Jasnah’s reading, for each Radiant devoted to battle, how many served in other ways?
o: One
Two
Ten
Three
quiz.e: She says for every battle-focused Radiant, another three worked in diplomacy, scholarship or other service.

quiz.q: What do the pattern’s kind call themselves?
o: Honorspren
Mazespren
Voidspren
Cryptics
quiz.e: They call themselves Cryptics, though people would likely name them liespren, a term they dislike.

quiz.q: What does Jasnah assign Shallan for the next few days?
o: Copying out Jasnah’s old book by hand
Studying and recording the pattern
Practising her Soulcasting
Reading about Alethi court life
quiz.e: She is relieved of other study to observe the Cryptic and record her experiences in detail.

chapters.title: Taker of Secrets
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: In a way meant to fend something off.
A hard, glassy black stone formed from cooled lava.
A piece of armour protecting the forearm.
A rocklike plant that grows in layered, stony mounds.
A written copy of spoken words.
A long speech by one person.
Someone who holds beliefs that go against a religion’s teachings.
As a verb: to take something for your own use, often without permission.
To measure or express in numbers.
Not noticing what is happening around you.
The person who held a job or position before the current one.
During highstorms Dalinar lives through scenes from the distant past, raving aloud as he does. Each one tends to end with a voice he takes for the Almighty.
In his last vision of the previous book, the voice told Dalinar it had been killed. Saying so in public could brand him a heretic.
Navani now writes down his words during the visions. She found he speaks ancient languages in them, which proves the visions are not just madness.
Navani, his brother’s widow, and Dalinar have begun a romance. Alethi custom frowns on it, and many would call it improper.
Kaladin and Bridge Four have just become Dalinar’s bodyguard, with Kaladin as their captain.

quiz.q: Where does Dalinar think his vision is taking place?
o: On the Shattered Plains
In Longbrow’s Straits
In the Frostlands
In the Purelake
quiz.e: Warm, knee-deep water with no land in sight makes him guess the Purelake.

quiz.q: What tells Dalinar the vision is set before the Recreance?
o: The soldiers all speak modern Alethi
The fortress is made of obsidian
The knight’s Shardplate is glowing
The men carry steel weapons
quiz.e: Shardplate glowed in the shadowdays, so a knight in glowing Plate means a time before the Recreance.

quiz.q: What are the knights and soldiers searching for?
o: A Parshendi scout spying at night
A lost knight’s fallen Shardblade
A gemheart buried in the lakebed
A spren that Sja-anat has touched
quiz.e: A soldier says they want a spren that doesn’t act as it should, because Sja-anat has touched it.

quiz.q: What rises out of the lakebed?
o: A huge shelled beast like a chasmfiend
A great serpent made of water and light
A skeletal creature of stone, thirty feet tall
A whole fortress pushing up from beneath
quiz.e: A thirty-foot stone creature with red eyes tears itself free of the rock; the soldiers call it a thunderclast.

quiz.q: What task does the Almighty give Dalinar?
o: Find the lost city of Urithiru
Refound the Knights Radiant
Make peace with the Parshendi
Recover the Honorblades
quiz.e: He says the Radiants were a solution to the Desolations and Dalinar must refound and unite them.

quiz.q: Why was transcribing this vision harder for Navani?
o: He was whispering far too quietly
He changed languages at the end
Her pen ran out of ink halfway
Adolin kept interrupting her
quiz.e: He spoke an ancient Selay, then switched languages at the end, and spoke too fast.

quiz.q: What does Navani propose that Dalinar refuses?
o: Moving her things into his quarters
Showing the visions to the ardents
Inviting more scholars to the visions
Delaying the king’s proclamation
quiz.e: She suggests moving into his quarters to save travel; he says no, since it would be wrong whatever the Almighty’s fate.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar find scratched on his wall after napping?
o: “Sixty-two days. Death follows.”
“Unite them before the storm comes”
“The Blackthorn will fall”
“Life before death”
quiz.e: White scratches form glyphs reading “Sixty-two days. Death follows.”

chapters.title: Ideals
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A formal written order or document issued by an authority.
A person whose job is to read public announcements aloud.
Working together side by side; “in tandem” means jointly.
Eager, quick readiness to do something.
An official demand for supplies, or the right to make one.
The officer in charge of an army's food, clothing and equipment.
A substance that kills germs and stops wounds becoming infected.
A path that zigzags back and forth up a steep slope.
A badge or mark that shows someone's rank.
A soldier's standing position: feet apart, hands clasped behind the back.
To cancel or take back an order or law.
An alliance of separate groups joining for a common purpose.
Skill at judging situations and making good decisions.
To copy someone you admire, trying to equal them.
Sadeas abandoned Dalinar's army on the Tower plateau. Kaladin and Bridge Four came back to rescue them, and Dalinar traded his Shardblade, Oathbringer, to Sadeas to free the bridgemen.
Earlier in this book, someone scratched glyphs into the wall of Dalinar's quarters while Kaladin's men stood guard: a countdown of sixty-two days, warning that death follows.
During the chasmfiend hunt in the last book, the king's saddle girth was found cut, and Dalinar began investigating who might want Elhokar dead.
Syl, Kaladin's spren, is an honorspren. Only Bridge Four knows that Kaladin can draw in Stormlight.
At the end of the last book, Dalinar stopped resisting Navani, the king's mother, and the two began a relationship that many Alethi consider improper.

quiz.q: What change does Dalinar’s proclamation make to the hunt for gemhearts?
o: Each highprince may keep every gemheart he wins
Gemhearts go to whichever army reaches them first
Pairs of highprinces will hunt each one together
Only the king’s own army may hunt them from now on
quiz.e: Each gemheart will be collected by two highprinces working in tandem; the spoils go to the king, who decides each share.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin ask Rock to do for the bridge crews?
o: Stock a storeroom and train cooks for the barracks
Teach the newest bridgemen to fight with a spear
Lead patrols out into the hills around the camps
Guard Dalinar’s sons while Kaladin is on duty
quiz.e: Rock gets a storeroom to fill from the quartermaster and must train cooks for the other barracks, so the bridgemen start by eating well.

quiz.q: What does Sigzil want from Kaladin?
o: Command of one of the new bridge crews
Leave to travel home to Azir for a season
Lessons in reading the king’s writs
A chance to measure and test his powers
quiz.e: Sigzil wants to run experiments on Kaladin’s abilities and how long Stormlight stays in him; Kaladin gives him a couple of days to prepare.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin tell Syl he is waiting for?
o: The next highstorm, to refill his spheres
The thunder that always follows lightning
Word from his parents back in Hearthstone
Sadeas to be punished for his betrayal
quiz.e: Things are going well, so he expects something bad to follow, “the thunder” after the lightning.

quiz.q: What does Sadeas tell Ialai he truly wants?
o: Real war and conquest, not plateau skirmishes
A peace treaty with the Parshendi at last
To return home and rule his lands in Alethkar
Dalinar’s Shardplate to go with his Blade
quiz.e: He has come to loathe the plateau game; he wants war and plans to forge a new Alethkar, then conquer Jah Keved.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin post a man on the balcony that Dalinar calls unreachable?
o: The king had ordered that every door be guarded
He had seen someone climbing there that morning
It is the way he would choose to break in himself
Moash needed a second man to relieve him there
quiz.e: Kaladin says that if he wanted to get in, the “unreachable” way is the one he would try. The king approves.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin call Dalinar “sir” rather than “Brightlord”?
o: He was never taught the proper forms of address
Every man he has called Brightlord betrayed him
Dalinar asked him to use it on his first day
Bridge Four voted to drop all lighteyed titles
quiz.e: He says every “Brightlord” has betrayed him, while some men he called “sir” still have his trust.

quiz.q: How does Dalinar plan to “disarm” the highprinces?
o: Confiscate the spears of their soldiers
Ban them from going on plateau runs
Buy up their Shards with gemheart wealth
Have Adolin duel them for their Shards
quiz.e: He lifts his ban on Adolin’s serious duels: Adolin will challenge other Shardbearers with their Shards as the prize.

quiz.q: What goal of Dalinar’s makes everyone in the room leap to their feet?
o: To refound the Knights Radiant
To make peace with the Parshendi
To march the armies home at once
To take the throne from Elhokar
quiz.e: He says he will refound the Knights Radiant. Teshav calls the Radiants traitors, and Kaladin nearly drops his spear.

quiz.q: What larger duty does Dalinar give Kaladin after the meeting?
o: Running the medical corps of the warcamp
Slowly taking over the King’s Guard too
Training all of Dalinar’s new recruits
Leading Bridge Four on plateau assaults
quiz.e: Dalinar needs the King’s Guard officers for his army, so Kaladin’s men will merge with the guard and he will command it.

chapters.title: Terrible Destruction
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: An Alethi woman's right hand, which she may leave uncovered.
An idea or quality rather than a physical thing.
The group of servants or attendants who accompany an important person.
Without enough people to do the work.
To agree to something, often reluctantly.
Friendly and easy to talk to.
A narrow passage or stairway inside a ship.
Of a sphere: dull and empty, with no Stormlight left inside.
To calm someone down or soothe their worries.
Something that does not fit the usual pattern; an odd exception.
To put forward an idea as the basis for an argument.
Quiet, obedient and easy to control.
The strange spren of shifting lines that has followed Shallan, whom she has named Pattern. Jasnah calls his kind Cryptics, or liespren.
Shallan joined Jasnah to steal her Soulcaster and save her bankrupt family in Jah Keved. The fabrial she has is broken, and her brothers are waiting at home.
In the last book Shallan Soulcast without a fabrial, turning a goblet into blood after a voice demanded a truth from her.
At the end of the last book, Jasnah concluded that the parshmen, the docile servants everyone owns, are the Voidbringers of legend.
An ancient city, linked to the Knights Radiant, that Jasnah has been researching. Shallan first learned of it by secretly reading Jasnah's notes.

quiz.q: How does Pattern react when Shallan explains that people eat food?
o: He asks to taste one of the limafruit
He calls eating a terrible destruction
He says that spren eat Stormlight too
He hums happily and calls it a good lie
quiz.e: Moving over the bowl of fruit, he is aghast: “Terrible destruction to eat!”

quiz.q: Where does Pattern say he first remembers being with Shallan?
o: Aboard Tozbek’s ship, the Wind’s Pleasure
In the Palanaeum, in Kharbranth
Somewhere green, with many plants
Inside the pouch of Jasnah’s spheres
quiz.e: Not on the ship, he says, but somewhere green with “many plants,” which brings back a glimpse of her father’s gardens that terrifies her.

quiz.q: What did Yalb see while Shallan was talking to Pattern?
o: The deck around her turned green
Pattern wrote words on the deck
Her eyes glowed with bright light
The fruit bowl rose into the air
quiz.e: Yalb swears the deck turned green. Shallan brushes it off as a scholarly matter.

quiz.q: What kind of lies does Pattern say are good ones?
o: Small lies
Kind lies
Old lies
True lies
quiz.e: He likes Yalb’s lie and says good lies are “true lies”: “Light makes shadow. Truth makes lies.”

quiz.q: What does Shallan realize about Jasnah when she sees a fearspren on her desk?
o: Jasnah is not worried; she is terrified
Jasnah has been Soulcasting in secret
Jasnah is angry at being interrupted
Jasnah has heard news of a new attack
quiz.e: Jasnah tries to hide a fearspren under a book, and Shallan sees past her mask: “You’re terrified.”

quiz.q: Why does Jasnah think parshmen might revolt without hearing any call to action?
o: They secretly read the letters of their owners
They have been trained to obey a single signal
Like the Parshendi, they may share a hidden link
Their spren have been whispering orders to them
quiz.e: Parshendi can sing in time across any distance, so their cousins the parshmen may have the same unexplained ability.

quiz.q: Why does Jasnah say they must find the city of Urithiru?
o: Legend says the Heralds are waiting inside it
It is the one place safe from every highstorm
Her brother has promised to fund the search
Its records may be the proof she needs
quiz.e: Urithiru may hold untouched records from before the Hierocracy, evidence strong enough to convince people about the parshmen.

quiz.q: What book does Jasnah give Shallan to read?
o: The Way of Kings
Words of Radiance
Ideals of the Ten
The Last Desolation
quiz.e: Jasnah hands her Words of Radiance, the source with the most about the Lightweavers, an order of the Knights Radiant.

chapters.title: Open Flame
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Untidy, with clothes and hair in disorder.
Small spren that dance in and around fires.
To breathe too fast and too deeply, usually from panic.
Sharp, backward-pointing hooks, like those on a fishhook.
Mist or steam rising into the air.
