Floating mats of living vines
Drifting mountains of pumice
quiz.e: A leg of rock lifts and crashes down: the Tai-na, the gods of the Reshi Isles, are greatshells.

quiz.q: What advice does the hanging Aimian give Rysn before she meets the king?
o: Never step onto the king’s shelf
Bring the king a gift of fruit
Speak only through an interpreter
Don’t ask about their god’s soul
quiz.e: He tells her not to ask about the soul of their god, since the Reshi don’t like to speak of it.

quiz.q: What surprises Rysn about the Reshi king?
o: The king is a child
The king is a woman
The king is a foreigner
The king is blind
quiz.e: The king is a greying woman. Talik insists they are led by a king and that gender is irrelevant.

quiz.q: What does the king reveal Vstim once did on the island?
o: Won a duel of boasts with Talik
Slew a coracot with their hunters
Swam beneath the god’s great head
Brought them their first medicines
quiz.e: Vstim once killed a coracot alongside the island’s hunters, which astonishes both Talik and Rysn.

quiz.q: How does Rysn appeal to “someone with more authority” than the king?
o: She sends a boat to bring Vstim up
She leaps from the shelf into the sea
She offers all her goods to Talik
She climbs down a rope to plead to Relu-na
quiz.e: She climbs down a fruit rope beside the god’s head and begs Relu-na itself for the trade.

quiz.q: What does Rysn realize after she wakes?
o: Vstim had staged it as her test
Talik had cheated Vstim for years
The king had cut the rope herself
Vstim had sold her to the Reshi
quiz.e: Vstim had been Talik’s babsk and set up a controlled first trade for her; the trade was never in danger.

quiz.q: What is the winged creature that crawls on Rysn’s arm?
o: A cremling the healers keep
A newly hatched chasmfiend
A larkin, thought extinct
A spren in a living body
quiz.e: It is a larkin, believed to have died with Aimia. Vstim says the island itself gave it to her.

chapters.label: Interlude I-4
chapters.title: Last Legion
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Made of chitin, the tough material of shells and insect armour.
Metal bands used to chain someone’s wrists or ankles.
Refusal to obey or respect a superior.
The state of being unknown or hidden away.
Trimming a plant to control how it grows.
A stony, plantlike growth that spreads in ridges and mounds.
The division of people into higher and lower ranks.
Wearing down an enemy, or being worn down, through steady losses.
Meddling in something casually, without full understanding.
Deep, full and rich in sound.
General of the listeners (the Parshendi’s own name for themselves) and their last Shardbearer. She is nursing a wounded leg and longs to talk peace with Dalinar.
Eshonai’s sister, a scholar in nimbleform, who has announced the secret of stormform and wants to bring it before the Five.
Listeners take different forms that shape body and mind: warform, workform, mateform, nimbleform and dullform. The old songs speak of hundreds more, some tied to their gods.
Listeners hear rhythms such as Peace, Resolve and Mourning, and hum or speak to them to show what they feel.
Eshonai was one of six listeners who decided to have King Gavilar killed, hoping to stop their gods from returning.

quiz.q: What kind of spren is trapped in the gemstone?
o: Windspren
Fearspren
Gloryspren
Stormspren
quiz.e: Eshonai says her sister calls it a stormspren, the key to stormform.

quiz.q: What is Thude’s answer to every disagreement?
o: Singing it out to Peace
Suggesting they go eat
Settling it with a spar
Taking it to the Five
quiz.e: Thude suggests food: it is hard to argue with your mouth full, and everyone ends up full.

quiz.q: How did listeners traditionally change form, before trapping spren in gems?
o: They bonded a spren in a highstorm
They drank a mix of crem and sap
They fasted for a whole stormpause
They sang to the Five on the tower
quiz.e: They went into a highstorm singing the proper song to attract the proper spren, and bonded it there.

quiz.q: Why have the three listeners Eshonai meets taken dullform?
o: They bonded the wrong spren by mistake
They were sent to spy on the humans
They think humans won’t kill them
They wish to remember the old days
quiz.e: The malen says they chose it themselves: humans won’t kill them when they come.

quiz.q: Whom does Eshonai’s mother mistake her for?
o: Her sister Venli
The warrior Bila
Her own mother
A house owner
quiz.e: She calls Eshonai “Venli” and praises her for staying home, unlike her wandering sister.

quiz.q: According to Mother’s song, how did the Last Legion win its freedom?
o: They slew their gods in a highstorm
They hid among the Alethi as slaves
They fled across the Origin
They took dullform, giving up thought
quiz.e: Warriors touched by the gods chose dullness of mind, a crippling that brought freedom, and made songs to remember.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai find in the sack her mother returns?
o: Her old warform armour
Her childhood playthings
Her old hand-drawn maps
Venli’s first song notes
quiz.e: Her maps from the early days, when she explored the wilds the humans call Natanatan.

quiz.q: What do the Five agree to about the stormform test?
o: Venli will try it at the next storm
Eshonai will try the form first
Zuln will test it as a dullform
They will wait a year to try it
quiz.e: Eshonai insists on trying it first and will leave her Blade and Plate with Thude; the Five agree over Venli’s objection.

chapters.title: The Day’s Masterpiece
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: The side of something that is sheltered from the wind.
Shaped like a tube: long, round and hollow.
Without being asked for or invited.
To complete something or make up for what it lacks.
Lowly and needing little skill, like routine labour.
Harmful in a quiet, gradual way.
An improvement; the act of making something bad better.
A substance that keeps a wound from becoming infected.
Calm and detached; not swayed by feelings.
The rise and fall of the voice when speaking.
The end of the world, or a catastrophe on that scale.

The slaver whose wagons Shallan found after the shipwreck. Acting like an important lady, she insisted that he take her to the Shattered Plains. In the last book, he was the slaver who sold Kaladin to Sadeas’s army.
On the Wind’s Pleasure, Shallan saw men stab Jasnah. She sank the ship by Soulcasting it, and washed ashore with only Jasnah’s trunk of books and notes.
Jasnah believed the parshmen might be the Voidbringers about to return, and hoped the lost city of Urithiru held records old enough to prove it.
The young ardent who courted Shallan in Kharbranth in the last book. He was secretly trying to poison Jasnah, and died of his own poison.
Shallan’s family’s broken Soulcaster, which she was carrying so that Navani could repair it and her brothers could return it to its owners.

quiz.q: What puzzles Shallan about the spindly shrubs beside the wagon?
o: Their leaves smell strongly of spice
They look too fragile for highstorms
They grow only where water pools
Their roots split the rocks apart
quiz.e: Their branches are brittle tubes; she asks Bluth how such a plant survives highstorms, and he only grunts.

quiz.q: What example does Shallan give Bluth of her own stupidity?
o: She couldn’t make a fire after the wreck
She got lost in her father’s gardens
She can’t drive a chull without help
She was seasick on her first voyage
quiz.e: Everyone is stupid in some situations, she says: ashore after the wreck, she couldn’t even make a fire to warm herself.

quiz.q: What are the two parshmen doing in Tag’s wagon at the midday halt?
o: Mending a chull harness
Grinding grain for bread
Carving bowls from shrubs
Weaving hats from reeds
quiz.e: They weave hats from reeds gathered that morning, which Tvlakv will sell for a few chips.

quiz.q: Once settled in the empty slave wagon, what does Shallan hold out her hand for?
o: A pair of spare boots
Her share of the meal
The key to the cage
Tvlakv’s map of the route
quiz.e: She asks for the key; Tvlakv regards it a moment too long before handing it over.

quiz.q: Why does Pattern say he was sent to Shallan in particular?
o: Because of the lies
Because of her drawings
Because Jasnah called him
Because her brothers prayed
quiz.e: Patterns worried about the Voidbringers and sent one; he says it was “because of lies,” the lies that saved her and drew him.

quiz.q: What does Pattern say about his real name?
o: It was taken from him long ago
It is made of many numbers
Only Jasnah ever learned it
It is a song humans can’t hear
quiz.e: “Name is numbers,” he says, hard to say; Pattern is fine.

quiz.q: What does Shallan find at the very bottom of Jasnah’s trunk?
o: A letter from Navani to Jasnah
A map of the way to Urithiru
Jasnah’s own working Soulcaster
A sketch she drew of Jasnah
quiz.e: It is her first drawing of Jasnah, from the day they met. Jasnah kept it among her most precious things.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan think the killers struck at Jasnah?
o: To claim a reward from the Parshendi
To take revenge for Gavilar’s murder
To control knowledge and profit from it
To steal her Soulcaster for themselves
quiz.e: She decides they want to control the knowledge so they can profit from the apocalypse itself.

chapters.title: Ironstance
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Overstepping what is proper; too bold.
In a plain, severe way, without decoration.
A carving whose figures stand out from a flat surface.
A prayer written in glyphs on cloth or paper, then burned to send it to the Almighty.
A metal stand or pan for holding burning coals.
A piece of armour covering the shoulder.
Letting light through, so that you can partly see through it.
To calm someone or ease their anger.
A belief that certain actions bring good or bad luck, without reason behind it.
To give something up as the penalty for losing.
A striking public show or display.
Dalinar has lifted his ban on Adolin’s serious duels. Adolin is to challenge other Shardbearers with their Shards at stake, to put pressure on the highprinces who work against the king.
Jasnah and Navani arranged a causal, a provisional engagement, between Adolin and Shallan. Jasnah and Shallan were sailing on the Wind’s Pleasure.
At the Tower, Sadeas abandoned Dalinar’s army to the Parshendi. Kaladin and his bridgemen went back for them, saving Dalinar and Adolin. Kaladin now commands the guard protecting Dalinar’s family.
The battle-hunger many Alethi feel in combat: a rush of eagerness and power while fighting.

quiz.q: What does Navani’s glyphward actually say?
o: “Safety and glory”
“Victory and honour”
“Strength and calm”
“Courage and luck”
quiz.e: Adolin guesses “Victory”; Navani tells him it says “safety and glory” and that it wouldn’t kill him to learn some glyphs.

quiz.q: What news about the Wind’s Pleasure concerns Adolin?
o: It was seen sinking near the coast
Its captain reported a pirate attack
It is a week overdue at its port
Jasnah left it at an earlier stop
quiz.e: Navani checked with the harbormaster at the Shallow Crypts: the ship hasn’t arrived. She assumes Jasnah is up to something.

quiz.q: Which of these is one of the good-luck rituals Renarin checks?
o: A glyphward tucked inside his helm
A night spent without sleep
A cup of wine with Father
Mother’s chain in his pocket
quiz.e: Renarin checks that Adolin ate chicken, talked to his sword, and has their mother’s chain in his pocket. Navani calls it foolishness.

quiz.q: What does Adolin finally admit is the reason he dislikes his guards?
o: They report everything to Navani
He doesn’t like their captain
They once let an assassin pass
They are too slow to keep up
quiz.e: Something about the captain seems “off” to him; Renarin suspects it’s because the man ordered him around on the battlefield.

quiz.q: What did Adolin have to wager to get Salinor to agree to the duel?
o: Both his Plate and his Blade
His Blade and a sack of spheres
His Plate and his father’s horse
His rank as battlefield commander
quiz.e: He had to bet Plate and Blade against only Salinor’s Blade, as though he had to offer more to be worth the bother.

quiz.q: Which stance does Adolin switch into as Salinor closes in?
o: Windstance
Flamestance
Stonestance
Ironstance
quiz.e: He opens in his familiar Windstance, then shifts to Ironstance, sword two-handed by his head, and batters Salinor’s helm.

quiz.q: How does Adolin respond when the highjudge says he has broken only two pieces?
o: He shatters Salinor’s left gauntlet
He demands a second bout at once
He rips off a pauldron and crushes it
He asks the king to rule on it
quiz.e: The duel was to three broken pieces of Plate; he tears off Salinor’s pauldron, smashes it between his fists, and says “Done.”

quiz.q: What does Adolin do with the Shardblade he wins?
o: Presents it to the king Elhokar
Gives it to Renarin as a gift
Keeps it for himself as a spare
Returns it to Salinor
quiz.e: He hands it to Renarin so his brother has the full set; Renarin, hesitant, grimaces as he takes it.

chapters.title: A Hand with the Tower
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: In an irregular way, starting and stopping.
Treatment that makes someone feel humiliated.
Worn out and messy, as if frayed.
To speak of something as having little worth.
Using charm or attraction to tempt someone.
A symbol or emblem that stands for a person or group.
Carefully and cautiously, to avoid pain or damage.
Of eyes: small, round and glittering.
A plant whose sap can be used to keep wounds from becoming infected.
The slaver Tvlakv and his hired guards, Bluth and Tag, are carrying Shallan toward the Shattered Plains, along with a wagon of slaves and two parshmen.
She lost her shoes in the wreck and has cut her feet badly walking on stone. She fears rotspren, the spren drawn to infected wounds.
Before the attack at sea, Jasnah arranged for Shallan to be engaged to Adolin Kholin, son of Highprince Dalinar.
The Alethi highprinces and their armies have been camped at the Shattered Plains for years, fighting the Parshendi.

quiz.q: What lie does Shallan catch Tvlakv telling?
o: That he has never sold a free woman
That he owns only one pair of shoes
That the Plains are a month away
That his slaves are all criminals
quiz.e: He wears different shoes than on the first day but claims he lost a trunk to a storm. He doesn’t much mind being caught.

quiz.q: What does Shallan send Pattern to do?
o: Listen to Tvlakv and repeat his words
Scout the area for any other travellers
Search Tvlakv’s wagon for her shoes
Count the spheres in Tvlakv’s purse
quiz.e: Pattern comes back and reproduces Tvlakv’s and Tag’s voices perfectly, even the crackle of the fire.

quiz.q: In the overheard talk, what does Tvlakv hope to do with Shallan?
o: Sell her at the slave markets of Thaylenah
Marry her to a wealthy Thaylen trader
Trade her to some passing soldiers
Sell her back to whoever is missing her
quiz.e: Someone rich must be missing her, he says; selling her back could be what “finally digs us out.” Tag wants to leave her.

quiz.q: What does Shallan promise Tvlakv if he does as she says?
o: To give him a lighteyed title
To buy all of his slaves
To see his debts canceled
To pay him in Jasnah’s spheres
quiz.e: She claims a fortune awaits her through a betrothal and promises to see his debts canceled, making him a free man. He’s shocked she knows.

quiz.q: Why does Tvlakv shrink back from Shallan beside the fire?
o: She draws a hidden knife from her sleeve
Her voice suddenly sounds just like Tag’s
A strange pattern crawls across the ground
She glows, and her dress looks whole
quiz.e: She is glowing with the light of spheres, and her torn dress looks majestic. She lets the glow fade, hoping he’ll blame the firelight.

quiz.q: Why is Bluth sure the armed men camped nearby are deserters?
o: No banners, yet good gear and tight guard
They wear the colours of Sadeas’s army
He recognized one of them from his past
They had many horses but no supplies
quiz.e: They fly no banners and show no sigils, but have good equipment and keep a tight guard. He’d bet the chulls on it.

chapters.title: Swordmaster
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: The outer edge or boundary of an area.
The muddy sediment left by highstorms, which slowly hardens into stone.
A title or form of address that shows respect.
To provoke hostility in someone; to annoy.
Harmless; not likely to draw suspicion.
One of the ranks into which Alethi lighteyes are sorted by birth.
The shape and build of a person’s body.
Something that weighs a person down or hinders movement.
In a light, carefree, dismissive way.
A sense of threat or danger.
Kaladin’s former commander, admired as an honourable hero. He killed Kaladin’s men, took the Shardblade Kaladin had won, branded him and sold him as a slave. He has just arrived at the warcamps.
To free Bridge Four and the other bridgemen from Sadeas, Dalinar traded away his own Shardblade.
During a highstorm, glyphs appeared scratched into Dalinar’s wall: “Sixty-two days. Death follows.” No one saw who made them.
Kaladin is now captain of the guard protecting Dalinar and his family, with Bridge Four at its core.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin know there must be a way up onto the wall?
o: Fresh crem stains show an old ladder there
A guard is already posted up there
The rockbuds up there are cultivated
Drehy spots a rope over the edge
quiz.e: Cultivated rockbuds mean someone tends them; the ardent has the key to the stairwell in the northwestern corner.

quiz.q: Why can men who aren’t Shardbearers spar with Shardblades here?
o: The king lends his Blades for practice
They rent them from Thanadal’s camp
The ardents keep the Blades in trust
Adolin lends his own Blade as a favour
quiz.e: They use the King’s Blades, a grand tradition; one is his father’s, kept for training Shardbearers.

quiz.q: What does Moash point out after the ardent stalks off?
o: Kaladin left the main gate unguarded
Kaladin was staring at the Shardblades
Kaladin had spoken Amaram’s name aloud
Kaladin used no honorific for the king
quiz.e: Kaladin skipped the king’s honorific and implied lighteyes had to be tricked into training; he thanks Moash for the reminder.

quiz.q: What happened in Dalinar’s rooms during the highstorm last week?
o: An assassin was caught beside his bed
A second number was scrawled on the wall
Navani’s new fabrial was smashed apart
Red spren were seen circling his door
quiz.e: Someone again wrote a number counting down to the same date, a little over a month away, though Kaladin is sure no one got past him.

quiz.q: When Syl confronts him like a storm, what does Kaladin admit?
o: Amaram once saved him
He fears the Weeping
Dalinar is a good man
He misses his family
quiz.e: She demands “No lies. Ever.” He admits Dalinar gave up his Blade for them and is a good man, fooled by Amaram.

quiz.q: What does Adolin tell Kaladin his job is?
o: To keep the ardents out of the way
To fetch water between his bouts
To stay well out of Adolin’s sight
To watch over Adolin’s brother
quiz.e: Adolin says he can keep himself alive; Kaladin should watch Renarin. He owes Kaladin his life but tells him to remember his place.

quiz.q: According to Syl, why weren’t the Shards abominations in the Radiants’ time?
o: The knights hadn’t yet changed
The Heralds had blessed them
No spren had been harmed yet
They were never used in wars
quiz.e: She says the Shards weren’t abominations back then; what changed was the knights.

quiz.q: Why, according to Zahel, was Renarin never chosen by a sword master?
o: His father forbade him to train
He had health problems of some sort
Every master had refused to teach him
He wished to become an ardent
quiz.e: Most lighteyed boys of rank are chosen by ten; Renarin never practiced much, due to health problems. Adolin then calls Zahel over.

chapters.title: A Pattern
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Of land: poor, and unable to grow much.
A drawing that exaggerates someone's features, often unkindly.
Shown as better or more perfect than in real life.
A short, thick club used as a weapon.
In a silent, bad-tempered, resentful way.
Annoyed and frustrated, having run out of patience.
Shrivelled and wrinkled with age or drying.
Describing a partnership in which two different living things each benefit from the other.
The capacity for thought, reason and wisdom.
A reed-like plant whose sap is used to clean wounds and keep infection away.
Small red spren that gather around infected wounds.
The slaver who once sold Kaladin into Sadeas’s army. His hired guards are Bluth and Tag, and he is now carrying Shallan toward the Shattered Plains.
Shallan has no shoes, and her feet are cut and bandaged with cloths from Jasnah’s trunk. She has been treating them with knobweed sap to keep rotspren away.
By the fire, Shallan faced Tvlakv down and briefly glowed, her torn dress looking whole. Then Bluth ran in with news of several dozen deserters nearby, and the wagons fled in the dark.
The spren that follows Shallan as a shifting pattern on surfaces. He hums “Mmm,” and is fascinated by lies.
Jasnah believed the parshmen are the Voidbringers of legend, and that the lighteyes must be persuaded to get rid of them.

quiz.q: After her first, unflattering sketch of Bluth, what does Shallan draw?
o: Bluth asleep in the wagon, his hat over his eyes
Bluth as a soldier, uniformed and with a spear
Bluth beating the chull with his long reed
Bluth and Tag arguing over a game of dice
quiz.e: She draws him again, idealized: in uniform, a spear planted at his side, eyes on the horizon.

quiz.q: How does Shallan learn that the deserters are following them?
o: Bluth finds their bootprints on a ridge
A parshman points out the men far behind them
A thin trail of smoke rises to the south
Tag hears their shouting on the wind
quiz.e: Tvlakv spots smoke to the south: the deserters have stopped to cook their midday meal, not caring if they’re seen.

quiz.q: What do Tvlakv’s parshmen answer when Shallan asks their names?
o: They give no answer
“One” and “Two”
“Slave” and “Worker”
They name their owner
quiz.e: One says “One,” points at his companion and says “Two,” then goes back to weaving.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan insist they head for the second column of smoke?
o: The deserters would run down slow wagons fleeing east
Tvlakv’s list says the storm will pass to the east
The ground to the east is too broken for the wagons
She hopes to find the sailors from her lost ship
quiz.e: She reasons the deserters would take the easy kill of slow wagons rather than the larger group ahead, so cutting east won’t work.

quiz.q: Which drawing does Shallan feel she finally gets exactly right?
o: Yalb with a spark of mischief in his eyes
The santhid as it swam beside the ship
Herself at the edge of the Shattered Plains
Jasnah at her desk, worried and exhausted
quiz.e: Her picture of Jasnah on the ship captures the worried, terrified face she saw: Jasnah’s burden.

quiz.q: How does Shallan finally draw the Stormlight out of a sphere?
o: She swallows the sphere
She crushes it in her fist
She breathes it in sharply
She asks Pattern to help
quiz.e: Pattern suggests eating it; she instead sucks in a sharp breath, and the Light streams into her chest.

quiz.q: What does Shallan notice after the Stormlight has left her?
o: A cut on her foot has shrunk
Her dress has mended itself
Pattern has grown much larger
The sphere is glowing again
quiz.e: The wound is noticeably smaller: the Stormlight has been healing her feet.

quiz.q: What does Pattern reluctantly admit he expects to happen?
o: Shallan will leave him behind in the Frostlands
Losing Jasnah will make him forget everything
His kind will force him to go back to them soon
Shallan will one day kill him, as the knights did
quiz.e: He says the Knights Radiant killed their spren through their oaths, and he will learn what he can before she kills him.

chapters.title: Bruises
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Messy and careless in habits or appearance.
Grand and impressive in a way that commands respect.
To give a false idea of something; to hide what is really there.
A phrase whose meaning can't be worked out from its separate words.
Present from birth rather than learned.
Too unpleasant or arrogant to bear.
The top layer of stone along a wall or roof edge.
The bar between a sword's blade and its grip that protects the hand.
Acting as though one is better than others.
Stubborn determination; refusal to give up.
A tough cord of tissue joining muscle to bone.
Dalinar’s bodyguard, now led by Kaladin. Bridge Four and the surviving members of the old guard protect Dalinar and his sons.
Dalinar’s younger son, who wears spectacles and has hardly trained with a sword. He has been given Dalinar’s old Shardplate, and a Blade his brother won in a duel.
The scarred ardent swordmaster at the practice grounds, who was asked to take Renarin as his student.
During a recent highstorm, someone scratched glyphs on the wall of Dalinar’s rooms, and Kaladin still can’t work out how they got in.
In the last book, Kaladin killed a Shardbearer to save Amaram’s life and refused the Shards. Amaram killed Kaladin’s men to keep them for himself and branded Kaladin a slave.

quiz.q: What is the chouta that Lopen is eating?
o: A Horneater stew served in a hollow shell
Meat in a dark sauce wrapped in thick bread
Fried tallew grain rolled into small balls
Dried chull meat strung on a wooden stick
quiz.e: Chouta is Herdazian food: chunks of meat slathered in dark liquid, wrapped in thick flatbread. Kaladin calls it disgusting.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin plan for the highstorm that night?
o: Moving Dalinar to the king’s palace for safety
Leaving Moash and Drehy at Dalinar’s door all night
Guarding Dalinar himself, with his family together
Hiding Bridge Four men inside Dalinar’s rooms
quiz.e: The mysterious numbers came during storms before, so he’ll guard Dalinar himself and suggest the family stay together.

quiz.q: What is Zahel’s first exercise for Renarin?
o: Climbing onto the roof and jumping off
Running laps of the practice grounds
Holding a stance without moving for an hour
Dismissing and summoning his Blade
quiz.e: Zahel sends him up onto the roof of the dueling grounds to jump off, then to do it headfirst.

quiz.q: What does Zahel mean when he says repeating himself makes him “eat the wrong flower”?
o: It makes him feel tired
It makes him feel old
It makes him want to sleep
It makes him get angry
quiz.e: He explains that the idiom means he gets angry, and complains that nobody here has proper idioms.

quiz.q: Who was Niter?
o: Zahel’s student before Adolin
The ardent who made the Blade guards
Head of the Cobalt Guard before Kaladin
A Shardbearer who had betrayed the Kholins
quiz.e: Niter led the Cobalt Guard and was Zahel’s friend. He died keeping the men of the Kholin house alive.

quiz.q: How does Zahel land his first blows on Kaladin?
o: He drops the Blade and gets in close with his fists
He lures Kaladin onto the sand Renarin landed in
He swings the blunted Blade at Kaladin’s knees
He has another ardent trip Kaladin from behind
quiz.e: Kaladin is focused on the Shardblade; Zahel drops it, gets inside his reach, and punches him in the stomach and face.

quiz.q: What happens when Kaladin, healed by Stormlight, charges Adolin again?
o: Adolin throws him a second time
The Stormlight suddenly drains away
Moash pulls him back from the fight
Renarin crashes into him from the roof
quiz.e: The tempest inside him flees without warning; he stumbles, Adolin catches him, and Zahel puts a Blade to his neck.

quiz.q: What does Syl ask when Kaladin wonders why his Stormlight failed?
o: Why he was angry with Adolin
Whether he had eaten that day
What he had sworn to Dalinar
Who he had been protecting
quiz.e: She asks “Who were you protecting?” and whether he was really just practicing. He doesn’t know.

chapters.title: Safe Things
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A raised platform at one end of a hall, for a high table or seat of honour.
A bag with a shoulder strap.
Going from place to place in search of fun or adventure.
To come together and form one thing.
The rounded knob at the end of a sword's handle.
A thin, loosely woven fabric, often used for bandages.
The person who will inherit a title or property.
A large, dog-like animal of Roshar, kept as a pet or hunting beast.
Shallan’s family, a minor lighteyed house of Jah Keved. In the last book her brothers Balat, Wikim and Jushu were at home struggling to save it.
At eleven, Shallan was carried by her father through a room where her mother lay facedown on the floor, past a strongbox with light streaming from its cracks.
Vorin custom has women keep the left hand covered, and a girl starts to do so as she grows up.

quiz.q: Why do the maids gossip so freely in front of Shallan?
o: She has been away from the house for months
She hasn’t spoken in five months
They think she is asleep in her chair
They are speaking a language she lacks
quiz.e: She hasn’t said a word in five months, and the maids seem to think that because she doesn’t speak, she doesn’t hear.

quiz.q: What gift does Helaran bring Shallan?
o: A new blue silk dress with a clipped cuff
A young axehound pup from the kennels
Drawing paper and charcoal pencils
A book of Veden poems from Northgrip
quiz.e: He ordered a leather satchel from Northgrip holding thick, expensive drawing paper and a set of charcoal pencils.

quiz.q: What does Helaran tell her to draw after crumpling her sketch?
o: Plants and animals: “safe things”
Portraits of their whole family
The gardens outside the window
Fanciful creatures from stories
quiz.e: Seeing bodies on the page, he tells her to draw plants and animals, “safe things,” and not dwell on what happened.

quiz.q: What does Helaran summon when their father threatens him?
o: A troop of armed guards
A writ from the highprince
A clutch of glowing spheres
A six-foot Shardblade
quiz.e: Mist coalesces into a curved Shardblade, and he levels its point at his father’s chest. Shallan had no idea he was a Shardbearer.

quiz.q: What does Shallan do when Helaran holds the Blade to their father?
o: She runs to fetch the maids
She speaks, begging him not to
She throws her pencils at him
She hides beneath the high table
quiz.e: She whispers “No” and “please,” her first words in months. Helaran laughs that she speaks only to defend their father.

chapters.title: The Coldness of Clarity
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Burning slowly with smoke but little flame.
The state of being gone or forgotten completely.
A burning stick or piece of wood.
A close-fitting, sleeveless jacket, often of leather.
Rough-looking, with grey or greying hair.
Untidy and uncared for, especially of hair.
Of nails: neatly trimmed and cared for.
Deserving or calling out for pity.
A badge or emblem showing rank or membership.
A leather bag for holding wine or water.
Some thirty well-armed deserters have been following the tracks of Tvlakv’s three wagons all day, so Shallan had the caravan make for a column of smoke rising ahead of them.
Shallan has learned to breathe in Stormlight from spheres; it makes her glow faintly and has been healing her feet.
Tvlakv’s hired guards: Bluth, the hulking, gruff man who drives Shallan’s wagon, and Tag.
Vorin prayers are written as glyphs and burned as an offering to the Almighty.

quiz.q: What does Shallan see from the top of the last hill?
o: A bandit camp sharing out stolen goods
A caravan that has survived an attack
An empty campsite with its fires still lit
An army patrol camped for the night
quiz.e: Three wagons smolder among signs of battle, but caravan workers and guards are alive, with five more wagons intact.

quiz.q: Who is Yix?
o: One of Tvlakv’s parshmen
The deserters’ lookout
The caravan’s wounded leader
A golden-haired foreigner
quiz.e: Dressed in stone-coloured clothing, he stands up so close Shallan jumps. The woman scout speaks to him in a foreign tongue.

quiz.q: According to the woman scout, how did the caravan’s wagons catch fire?
o: The bandits used flaming brands to scare them
A lantern was knocked over during the fighting
The guards set them alight to block the road
Lightning from a passing storm struck them
quiz.e: She thinks it was an accident: the bandits used flaming brands to scare them, then pulled back so as not to lose more goods.

quiz.q: What does Shallan offer the woman scout?
o: A share of Tvlakv’s spheres
A place in her wagon
Her protection that night
A Brightlord’s reward
quiz.e: She offers her protection, in return for being conveyed to the Shattered Plains. The woman laughs that she’s gutsy.

quiz.q: Where does Shallan have Bluth drive her wagon?
o: North, into the burning camp
East, away from both groups
South, toward the deserters
West, back toward the coast
quiz.e: She sends Tvlakv and Tag to help the caravan, then has Bluth turn the wagon around and head south into the deserters.

quiz.q: What does Shallan glimpse reflected in a deserter’s breastplate?
o: Her own face, ragged and terrified
Jasnah standing just behind her
Pattern’s shape upon the metal
A stately, richly gowned woman
quiz.e: The woman she sees is tall and stately, with flowing red hair, a gold-embroidered gown, a necklace and manicured nails.

quiz.q: Who is first to say he will go and help the caravan?
o: A short man with an eye patch
Vathah, the band’s leader
A balding man in his forties
A deserter with a crossbow
quiz.e: The scarred man with the eye patch says starting over would be nice and runs up the hill; nearly the whole band follows.

quiz.q: Besides Lightweaving, what power does Pattern say Shallan has?
o: The power of command
The power of transformation
The power of foresight
The power of persuasion
quiz.e: Pattern says she has the power of transformation too: she didn’t Soulcast anyone, and yet she transformed the deserters.

chapters.title: Ashes
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: To rescue goods or materials from damage or ruin.
Looking exhausted and worn, as from worry or hardship.
Out of place; not fitting the surroundings.
A wanderer with no home or steady work.
A formal agreement between two sides.
A flat voice that never rises or falls.
To free someone from blame or guilt.
Payment given to make up for a loss or for effort.
A formal complaint about being wronged.
A fake document made to pass as genuine.
A written legal order or document.
A large, slow crustacean used on Roshar to pull wagons.
The largest size of sphere, the glass-and-gem beads used as money.
The slaver who sold Kaladin to Sadeas’s army in the last book. Earlier in this book he took Shallan along in his wagons, with his hired men Bluth and Tag.
In the last chapter, Shallan talked a band of army deserters, led by the grim Vathah, into charging to the aid of a caravan under attack. She promised their crimes would be erased.
A lighteyed woman in a long coat who wears a sword. Before the fighting, Shallan offered her protection in exchange for passage to the Shattered Plains.
Shallan’s spren, a shape of shifting lines that can slide across surfaces and speak, though people rarely notice him.

quiz.q: What does Shallan find tucked inside Bluth’s jacket?
o: Her sketch of him as a proud soldier
A pardon written for the deserters
A purse of spheres taken from bandits
A prayer of mourning for his old squad
quiz.e: It is the picture she drew of him not as he was but as he might have been: a soldier in a crisp uniform. A hero.

quiz.q: What reason does Shallan give Macob for wanting his caravan along?
o: She needs his maps of the route east
Soldiers can’t convey a lady in comfort
His guards know the roads better
She owes his family an old debt
quiz.e: She says the soldiers don’t know how to convey a lighteyed woman in comfort. Privately, she wants the caravan to remind the deserters of civilization.

quiz.q: What makes Vathah let go of Shallan’s arm?
o: Tyn draws her sword and orders him off
Shallan threatens to have him hanged
A voice he can’t place tells him to
His men call him away to the fires
quiz.e: Pattern, clinging to the back of Vathah’s uniform, says “You should let her go.” Vathah can’t find the speaker, and Shallan claims she heard nothing.

quiz.q: What does Tvlakv suggest about Bluth?
o: He was in league with the deserters
He had stolen spheres from the wagons
He meant to run off with the caravan
He was secretly a spy for Sadeas
quiz.e: Tvlakv guesses Bluth promised the deserters a share of the loot, then admits the theory makes no sense.

quiz.q: What wages does Shallan offer the slaves she takes from Tvlakv?
o: Two firemarks a week, plus food and boots
Nothing until they reach the Plains
A broam each once their writs are burned
Six firemarks a week, five toward debt
quiz.e: Six firemarks a week if five go toward their slave debt, one if not. A slave notes they take home the same either way.

quiz.q: What is written on the paper a caravan woman gives the deserters?
o: A list of the guards who fell
A prayer of thanks for the rescue
A prayer of mourning for the dead
A promise of pay from Macob
quiz.e: It is a prayer of thanks, not of mourning. The deserters see the tearful, watching caravan workers, then burn it.

chapters.title: Lights in the Storm
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Held motionless by wonder, fear or fascination.
To walk in a slow, relaxed way.
Showing no feeling; enduring hardship without complaint.
Tall and dignified, like a statue.
Violent, uncontrollable shaking of the body.
To formally withdraw from a group or state.
Fame, especially for something bold or bad.
Refusing to obey or respect those in authority.
Involved with others in a wrongdoing.
Impossible to see into or understand.
A device that uses gemstones and Stormlight to work, such as a spanreed.
A scholar who studies and predicts highstorms.
A small crablike creature common on Roshar.

In the last book, Kaladin killed a Shardbearer to save Amaram. Amaram had Kaladin’s squad murdered to keep the Shards, and branded Kaladin a slave. At the end of Part One he arrived at the warcamps as Dalinar’s old friend.
During highstorms Dalinar lives through scenes from the distant past, and Navani writes down what he says.
Someone scratched a countdown, “Sixty-two days,” into the wall of Dalinar’s rooms, and nobody knows how they got in.
Dalinar lifted his ban, so Adolin now duels other Shardbearers with their Shards as the prize. Earlier in this book he beat Salinor.
The quiet parshman placed in Bridge Four in the last book, who worked alongside the men.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin glimpse outside the rattling shutter?
o: A white spren shaped like a young woman
Faint red lights, like a pair of eyes
A Shardblade flashing through the slats
A shadowy man clinging to the sill
quiz.e: A steady, faintly red light appears and Kaladin has the impression of eyes. The king’s complaint about the shutter breaks the moment.

quiz.q: What is heating the king’s room during the storm?
o: Logs brought all the way from Alethkar
Hot stones Soulcast inside the hearth
Braziers of burning coal and oil
A huge ruby in a fabrial Navani built
quiz.e: The hearth holds a ruby the size of Kaladin’s fist; Renarin explains that his aunt built the heating fabrial herself.

quiz.q: What is Adolin looking at in his book?
o: Sketches of men in fine clothing
Diagrams of the classic stances
Maps of plateaus near the camps
Notes on each Shardbearer in camp
quiz.e: The book is full of fashion sketches. Adolin snaps it shut when Kaladin asks about it.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin say a highstorm is a good time for an assassin?
o: Guards drink to pass the long hours
Lightning hides the glow of a Blade
Winds cover shouts; help comes slowly
The king always sleeps through storms
quiz.e: The winds would cover shouts and help would be slow while everyone sheltered. The king agrees it makes sense.

quiz.q: What goal does Dalinar set for Adolin’s duels?
o: Undermining Sadeas, even killing him
Testing every Shardbearer in the camps
Winning Shards for the king’s own army
Restoring Adolin’s standing at court
quiz.e: Dalinar agrees with Kaladin that the duels must be narrowed: the aim is to undermine Sadeas, killing him in a duel if they have to.

quiz.q: How does Dalinar respond when Kaladin accuses Amaram?
o: He orders Amaram arrested that night
He calls Kaladin a liar and leaves
He promises to tell the king at once
He asks for proof and says to keep quiet
quiz.e: Dalinar calls Amaram one of the best men he knows, asks for proof, and tells Kaladin to hold his tongue while he talks to Amaram.

quiz.q: Who is Punio?
o: A bridgeman from one of Sadeas’s crews
A Horneater cook hired to help Rock
Lopen’s cousin, who left Roion’s army
A guard Idrin sent to Bridge Four
quiz.e: Punio, a Herdazian soldier from Roion’s army, joined because Lopen’s mother said they needed guards. Kaladin lets him stay.

quiz.q: What does Shen ask Kaladin?
o: If he may go home to his family
If he is really part of Bridge Four
If parshmen can see spren as well
If he will be sold back to Sadeas
quiz.e: Shen asks if he is really Bridge Four and where his spear is. Told Kaladin can’t arm parshmen, he concludes he is Bridge Four’s slave.

chapters.title: Assassin
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A flat walkway or platform, often cut into a slope or a building.
In an unsteady way that looks likely to fall.
A paste of lime, sand and water that sets hard to bind stones.
The base on which a structure rests.
Overly complicated and hard to follow.
Planned in a forced, unnatural way.
In Vorin belief, the life’s work a person chooses in order to serve the Almighty.
To transform one substance into another, as Soulcasters do.
In the last book the king’s saddle girth was found cut during a chasmfiend hunt, and gemstones in his Shardplate had been swapped for flawed ones.
The king is convinced people are trying to kill him, and many in camp dismiss him as paranoid.
Idrin captains the king’s own guard. Dalinar plans for Kaladin and his bridgemen to take over guarding the king.
Szeth, the Shin assassin in white, killed King Gavilar six years ago, and the Alethi never caught him.

quiz.q: How was the king nearly killed?
o: A knife was thrown from a dark window
Poison was slipped into his wine
A balcony railing gave way under him
A stone fell from the roof above him
quiz.e: A section of the balcony railing pulled free while he leaned on it; one bar held, and he clung there until rescued.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin call whoever did it an idiot?
o: No one could know where the king would lean
They left their tools behind on the balcony
They struck while his guards stood watching
They chose a night with a highstorm passing
quiz.e: The trap could easily have caught someone else, exposing the plotters for nothing. Dalinar notes the king has a favourite spot at the rail.

quiz.q: What do Dalinar and Kaladin conclude about the plotters?
o: They are foreigners unused to Alethi ways
They meant only to frighten the king
They wanted Dalinar blamed for the death
They are cowards who want an accident
quiz.e: They prefer nonconfrontational methods and want the death to look like an accident: they are cowards.

quiz.q: What cut the iron of the railing so cleanly?
o: A saw hidden in the mortar dust
A Shardblade through the joint
A Soulcaster turning iron to smoke
Rust eating through the old joints
quiz.e: The pieces were sheared smoothly at a joint. Dalinar agrees: “That was a Shardblade.”

quiz.q: What does Dalinar want to keep from everyone else?
o: That the railing was sabotaged
That the king was hurt at all
That they spotted the Blade cut
That Idrin is under suspicion
quiz.e: It’s too late to pretend it was an accident, but they will hide that they noticed the Shardblade cut, to gain an edge.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar eventually want for the king’s protection?
o: Guards drawn only from the bridge crews
Idrin punished and stripped of his rank
The Cobalt Guard posted in his rooms
Adolin and Renarin guarding in turns
quiz.e: He will move Idrin to a command in his army, not as punishment, and wants the king guarded only by trusted bridgemen outside warcamp politics.

chapters.title: Tyn
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Friendly and easy to talk to.
A vehicle for carrying people or goods.
Someone who lends money and collects debts, often harshly.
Having a sharp, strong smell or taste.
To hunt around for something, often by begging or borrowing.
The state of being a slave or bound servant.
A very small amount of money.
The outer boundary of an area.
A descendant of a notable family.
A go-between who acts on behalf of others.
One of the ranks that sort Alethi darkeyes by social standing.
A paired pen fabrial that writes whatever its twin writes, far away.
Shallan promised the deserters their crimes would be forgiven if they followed her to the Shattered Plains. Their leader, Vathah, doubts her and expects to hang.
The lighteyed woman in a long coat, wearing a sword, who leads the caravan’s few remaining guards.
Jasnah arranged a causal, a conditional betrothal, between Shallan and Dalinar’s son Adolin, to give Shallan’s indebted house a powerful ally.
The group that wants back the Soulcaster Shallan’s family held, which Shallan broke.
Jasnah believed the Voidbringers would return and sought Urithiru, a city linked to the Knights Radiant. Shallan saved her trunk of books and notes.

quiz.q: Why do Gaz and Red say the deserters left the war?
o: They were never paid their wages
It became about spheres, not winning
Their highprince sent them home
They feared the Parshendi Shardbearers
quiz.e: The lighteyes stopped fighting to win and fought for gemhearts, while soldiers bled to make them rich. Red adds that Gaz also owed debtmongers.

quiz.q: What does Gaz add to Shallan’s wagon?
o: A lock to keep her books safe inside
A padded seat on the driver’s bench
A canvas cover against highstorms
A small window that lowers on a latch
quiz.e: He folds up the side and lowers a little window so she can see out, and offers to make another for the other side.

quiz.q: Where does Shallan tell Vathah most change begins?
o: In words
In battle
In prayer
In shame
quiz.e: Vathah says words won’t change the men; Shallan answers that, in her experience, words are where most change begins.

quiz.q: Which highprince do Jasnah’s notes call fond of games of chance?
o: Hatham
Sebarial
Aladar
Thanadal
quiz.e: Aladar is powerful, a brilliant political player and fond of games of chance; Shallan thinks he might risk an expedition to Urithiru.

quiz.q: How much does Gaz say he owes?
o: Twenty sapphire broams
Fifty emerald marks
A hundred diamond chips
Eighty ruby broams
quiz.e: Eighty ruby broams, though he says it may be his head they want now. He walks off rather than tell the truth about it.

quiz.q: Why, according to Pattern, is a table a table?
o: People have thought of it as one so long
Its wood remembers the tree it came from
Spren hold its legs in their proper shape
Its maker named it when it was finished
quiz.e: Without a perspective there is only wood; people considered it a table long enough that it became truth to the table.

quiz.q: Pattern says spren are fragments of power. Which name does he force out last?
o: Honor
Cultivation
Odium
Nightwatcher
quiz.e: He lists Honor, Cultivation and “another,” then, in a high whine, forces out “Odium.”

quiz.q: What does Tyn conclude Shallan is?
o: A spy sent by the Alethi king
A talented but new con artist
A runaway hiding from a marriage
A thief after the caravan’s goods
quiz.e: Tyn is impressed by her “con” and wants in. Shallan claims to know something important about Dalinar, which Tyn takes for blackmail.

chapters.title: Monsters
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: In a way that unsettles or confuses.
A great abundance; a lavish amount.
Drawn out; lasting longer than expected or wanted.
Acting as if you are better than others.
A loop hanging from each side of a saddle, to hold a rider’s foot.
The side of an animal between its ribs and hip.
To eat or drink far more than needed; to gorge.
The raised front part of a saddle.
Thrilling; making you feel very happy and excited.
An official written request for supplies or permission.
Rising and sinking in the saddle in time with a horse’s trot.

On the night of a highstorm a section of Elhokar’s balcony railing gave way, leaving him hanging over a long drop. Kaladin and Dalinar found it had been cut with a Shardblade, and agreed to keep that quiet.
Kaladin has seen Amaram arrive at the warcamps carrying a Shardblade: the man who took Kaladin’s Blade, branded him and sold him as a slave.
The gruff ardent swordmaster at Dalinar’s practice grounds. After sparring with Kaladin, he warned him he would need far more training to face Shardbearers.
Rare, huge horses that choose their own riders. Adolin rides a white one, Sureblood.

quiz.q: Why does Dalinar say Kaladin needs to learn to ride?
o: The king insists every guard be mounted
It took him so long to reach the palace
Bridge Four will soon serve as scouts
He must race Adolin on plateau runs
quiz.e: It took Kaladin almost three-quarters of an hour to reach the palace on the night of the king’s accident; riding would have been far faster.

quiz.q: How does Jenet respond to Adolin’s compliment on her riding dress?
o: She throws a stone at him
She ignores him completely
She thanks him very coolly
She orders him off her field
quiz.e: Without looking, she picks up a stone and throws it at him, then another, and Adolin rides off hunched over.

quiz.q: What is Kaladin’s horse, Spray, doing when he first tries to make her move?
o: Trotting back toward her stable
Rolling on her back in the dirt
Nudging his boot for a treat
Licking rocks to lure out grass
quiz.e: Licking fools the grass into thinking rain has come, so it pokes out of its holes. “Clever beast. Lazy. But clever.”

quiz.q: What does Kaladin realize about the railing while talking with Syl?
o: The highstorm alone tore it loose
The cut was made with a common saw
It must have been cut after the storm
The king must have been pushed onto it
quiz.e: The storm’s winds would have pushed on the railing as hard as the king did, so the sabotage must have happened after the storm.

quiz.q: What reason does Kaladin give Syl for trying to ride Dreamstorm?
o: Dalinar has ordered him to try it
He wants to impress Jenet’s grooms
He is scared of these animals
He hopes to win a bet with Moash
quiz.e: He tells Syl it isn’t because of Adolin: “Because I’m scared of these things.”

quiz.q: How does Kaladin stay on Dreamstorm while she bucks?
o: Two grooms grab hold of her bridle
He ties himself on with the reins
Syl calms her by whispering to her
He sticks himself on with Stormlight
quiz.e: He pours Stormlight onto the saddle and sticks himself in place, until it runs out and Dreamstorm throws him.

quiz.q: What does Natam remember about the balcony after Kaladin left that night?
o: Moash stayed late and went out to watch it
A servant he didn’t know swept it clean
The king went out there alone for an hour
Captain Idrin inspected the railing twice
quiz.e: Moash stayed past his shift, saying he wanted to see the king settled, and went out to watch the balcony.

quiz.q: Whom does Dalinar go to meet at the end of the lesson?
o: Highprince Sadeas
Brightlord Amaram
King Elhokar
Captain Idrin
quiz.e: It is Amaram. Kaladin’s sudden hatred surprises him, and he looks forward to getting away on patrol.

chapters.title: The Feather
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A hard protective case in which a creature changes from one stage of life to the next.
A hard shell or shell-like armour on an animal’s body.
Quickly spreading from one person to others, like laughter.
A thin, watery fluid that oozes from a wound.
Impossible to get through, or to understand.
Remarkably great in size or degree.
To stop having a physical form; to vanish.
A large open tent used for shade or shelter.
Something offered to persuade someone to act.
Dwelling gloomily on worries or resentments.
An Alethi term for a provisional betrothal agreement that may lead to marriage.
Under Dalinar’s new orders as Highprince of War, two highprinces go after each gemheart together, and the spoils go to the king to divide.
Dalinar lifted his ban on Adolin’s serious duels: Adolin is to challenge other Shardbearers with their Shards as the prize. His first such bout, against Salinor, was a brutal, unpolished win.
Jasnah began arranging a causal between Adolin and her ward, Shallan Davar, who was sailing with Jasnah toward the Shattered Plains.
Dalinar’s younger son has a “blood weakness” that brings on fits. He has recently begun training in Shardplate under the swordmaster Zahel.

quiz.q: Whom does Adolin rescue from being surrounded on the second tier?
o: Eranniv
Salinor
Jakamav
Ruthar
quiz.e: Jakamav, a Shardbearer under Highprince Roion who fights with a hammer, had been cut off up there.

quiz.q: How does Adolin get onto the top tier of the plateau?
o: He climbs a bridge propped on the cliff
Jakamav hoists him up onto his shoulders
He leaps off his Blade stuck in the rock
He fights his way up the clogged slope
quiz.e: He drives his Shardblade into the cliff flat side up, stands on it, and leaps up with his Plate’s strength.

quiz.q: What does Adolin find when he reaches the chrysalis?
o: It has already been opened and emptied
It is still sealed and far too thick
Its gemheart is cracked and worthless
The Parshendi have built a wall round it
quiz.e: The chrysalis is already open, with a gap where the gemheart should be; the Parshendi Shardbearer holds it.

quiz.q: How do the fleeing Parshendi escape with the gemheart?
o: They climb down ropes into the chasm
They leap to the hill’s other half
They hide in caves under the top tier
They cross a bridge and then pull it up
quiz.e: They jump the gap where the hill was split down the middle; to them it is just another chasm.

quiz.q: What does the Parshendi Shardbearer want from Adolin?
o: She wants to speak with Dalinar
She wants to duel him for Shards
She asks for a truce over the dead
She demands Sadeas be handed over
quiz.e: In accented Alethi she asks where his father is: she must speak to Dalinar, whom she met once long ago.

quiz.q: According to the bridgeman guard, what happened to Renarin?
o: He was knocked off a bridge into a chasm
He summoned his Blade and just stood there
He charged off alone and had to be rescued
He lost his Blade to a Parshendi warrior
quiz.e: Renarin insisted on helping defend a bridge, then froze once he summoned his Blade; the guards got him away.

quiz.q: Why does Jakamav put off meeting Adolin at the winehouse?
o: He has promised the night to Inkima
He has promised to dine with Sadeas
Adolin keeps refusing to drink with him
Adolin is bad for one’s reputation now
quiz.e: He says Dalinar and the king aren’t popular, so they should wait until it all blows over. The words hit Adolin hard.

quiz.q: What did the new scratched message outside Dalinar’s room say?
o: “Sixty days. The king will fall.”
“Fifty days. Trust no Shardbearer.”
“Forty days. The Heralds return.”
“Forty-nine days. A new storm comes.”

Inside a chest in the garden shed
On a shelf in Jushu’s bedroom

The listener (Parshendi) Shardbearer who nearly killed Dalinar, the Blackthorn, at the Tower. One of the Five who lead her people, she hopes to sue for peace with the Alethi.
Venli, Eshonai’s sister, believes that enough listeners in this ancient form could control or even summon a highstorm. She has trapped in a gemstone a spren she calls a stormspren.
Over Venli’s objection, the Five ruled that Eshonai, not Venli, would be the first to try stormform. Venli then set out to train her in the proper mindset.
A listener takes a new form by going out into a highstorm with the right spren and bonding it there.
Listeners attune inner rhythms that match moods, such as Resolve, Joy and Awe, and often speak “to” one of them.

quiz.q: What has Thude just arranged with the Alethi?
o: A duel with the Blackthorn on the next plateau run
A parley in seven days on a neutral plateau
A prisoner exchange right after the next highstorm
A truce covering every gemheart run this season
quiz.e: Thude has returned from the Alethi: the meeting to discuss peace will happen in seven days on a neutral plateau.

quiz.q: How do the listener songs describe the Rider of Storms?
o: A traitor spren who chose to protect humans
The eldest and greatest listener god
A judge who weighs each listener’s worth
The guardian spren of all warforms
quiz.e: The Rider, whom humans call the Stormfather, is not a listener god; the songs name him a traitor who protected humans instead.

quiz.q: Why does Eshonai face the storm without her Shardplate?
o: The storm’s lightning would be drawn to it
Venli had borrowed it to study while she was away
It was too damaged from her last battle
Wearing it interferes with the transformation
quiz.e: She would have preferred to wear it, but for some reason having it on interferes with the transformation.

quiz.q: What tells Eshonai that the moment of transformation has come?
o: The storm’s winds suddenly double in their strength
A crowd of windspren gathers around her head
Every rhythm becomes one steady, heartlike beat
The stormwall passes and the rain grows warm
quiz.e: All the rhythms align into the same single, steady beat, like a heart. Then the storm vanishes and the face appears.

quiz.q: What does the Rider of Storms say after the red spren strikes her?
o: That he cannot stop this, and is sorry
That she has chosen well and should rejoice
That she must flee back to Narak at once
That her people have betrayed him again
quiz.e: He says he cannot stop it and would shelter her if he had the power, then repeats, “I am sorry.”

chapters.label: Interlude I-6

During a highstorm, the Assassin in White attacked the Kholins at the Pinnacle. Kaladin fought him and fell from the palace with him, surviving on Stormlight.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin tell Zahel has happened?
o: Bridge Four was ambushed down in the chasms
Adolin was badly wounded in a duel
There was an attempt on the king’s life
A highstorm wrecked the practice grounds
quiz.e: Bloodied and missing a sleeve, Kaladin says there was an attempt on the king’s life not two hours ago.

quiz.q: How does Zahel explain why Kaladin should come back later?
o: A far grouchier swordsman takes over the room by night
He trains no one without Dalinar’s written leave
He refuses to teach anyone who is still bleeding
His lessons are only given in the morning light
quiz.e: Two people live in the room: a grouchy day swordsman with a soft spot for kids, and a far grouchier one who comes out at night.

quiz.q: What does Zahel mean by “don’t be green from the ground”?
o: Don’t come back until your wounds have healed
Don’t bring any of your bridgemen with you
Don’t arrive tired or before the sun is up
Leave your attitude behind and come to learn
quiz.e: Grumbling that the language has no proper metaphors, he explains: leave your attitude and come to learn.

quiz.q: What does Zahel expect, but not get, as he falls asleep?
o: Kaladin knocking at his door again
A voice speaking inside his mind
A second blanket from the monks
Thunder from yet another storm
quiz.e: He expects a voice to speak in his mind, but there isn’t one; there hasn’t been for years.

quiz.q: What did Wit do on the second day of the journey?
o: Struck himself on the head with a rock
Tried to hold a conversation with the madman
Took the madman’s Shardblade for himself
Sang rude songs about the driver all day
quiz.e: He hit himself on the head with a rock three or four times, to judge the driver’s company: between four and five blows.

quiz.q: What does the madman say is near at hand?
o: The death of the last Alethi king
A highstorm stronger than any before
The fall of the Shattered Plains
The Return, the time of the Desolation
quiz.e: Calling himself Talenel’Elin, Herald of War, he warns that the Return, the Desolation, is near and they must prepare.

quiz.q: What surprises one of the nobles about how the madman speaks?
o: He speaks an old, forgotten tongue
He has a northern Alethi accent
He speaks only in rhyming verse
He uses a Thaylen merchant’s accent
quiz.e: It is Alethi with a northern accent, not what the speaker expected from someone with such dark skin.

quiz.q: How do they know the Shardblade is not bonded to the madman?
o: Its gemstone has gone completely dark
He cannot recall where he found it
It did not vanish when he dropped it
Bordin was able to lift it with ease
quiz.e: Bordin says the madman simply dropped it, and it didn’t vanish, so it can’t be bonded to him.

quiz.q: What is suggested be done with the madman?
o: Send him to the ardents to heal his mind
Lock him away in the cells beneath the palace
Return him to his home village
Put him to work in the bridge crews
quiz.e: One of the lighteyes suggests sending him to the ardents in case they can help his mind recover.

chapters.label: Interlude I-8

Streaked with swirling patterns of colour, like marble stone.
The listeners’ word for the hair that some of their forms grow.
Rescue from harm, ruin or loss.

Eshonai’s sister, a scholar who spent years recording the old songs. She claims enough listeners in stormform could control or even summon a highstorm.
Eshonai’s friend, a warform soldier who wears a long coat. He arranged the coming parley with the Alethi.
Chosen by the Five to try stormform first, Eshonai went out alone into a highstorm with the spren Venli had captured.

quiz.q: What has Eshonai lost in her new form?
o: Her marbled black and red skin
The strength to leap chasms
Her ability to hear rhythms
The bulky armour of warform
quiz.e: Her skin tone is unchanged, but the bulky warform armour is gone; small, durable ridges show through her skin instead.

quiz.q: What does Thude point out about Eshonai?
o: Her skin has turned pale
Her eyes have turned red
Her hairstrands are white
Her voice has lost its rhythm
quiz.e: Thude tells her that her eyes are red. She says they represent what she has become.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai say she feels brewing beyond the rhythms?
o: An angry highstorm they could bring down on enemies
The return of the old listener gods from exile
An Alethi army gathering to march on Narak
A new form waiting for Venli to discover it
quiz.e: She feels a powerful, angry highstorm; with enough of them in this form, they could bring it down upon their enemies.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai pointedly ignore at the end?
o: Venli’s jealous humming to Irritation
Thude walking away from the crowd
A voice inside her screaming in horror
The pain spreading along her new ridges
quiz.e: As the crowd sings, she ignores the voice deep within her that is screaming in horror.

chapters.title: The Multiplied Strain of Simultaneous Infusion

On Roshar, a scholar who studies the winds and predicts highstorms.

Fabrials, mostly worked by ardents, that turn one substance into another. They make the grain that feeds the armies on the Shattered Plains.
Gavilar’s widow and Jasnah’s mother, a renowned artifabrian. At the end of the last book she and Dalinar began a courtship many consider improper, since she was his brother’s wife.

quiz.q: What keeps going wrong as Adolin practises throwing his Shardblade?
o: It drops point-first at his feet
It swerves off toward his guards
It turns to mist before it lands
It spins back toward his own hand
quiz.e: Again and again the Blade dissolves into white mist moments after leaving his fingers, until he finally sinks one into the rock.

quiz.q: Why are the Soulcasters working in daylight now, according to Kadash?
o: Demand is so high they must work shifts
The fabrials work better in sunlight
The assassin has made the nights unsafe
The king wants the camps to watch them
quiz.e: Buildings, food and waste removal make too many demands; Dalinar approved training several ardents per fabrial to work in shifts.

quiz.q: What do the five Soulcasters create on the plateau?
o: A stone bridge over a chasm
A row of new stone barracks
A great heap of fresh grain
A wedge-shaped windbreak
quiz.e: A stone wall, flat on the camp side and sloped on the other, springs into being: a windbreak Dalinar had considered for months.

quiz.q: What does Adolin ask Kadash to look into?
o: Where the assassin might be hiding
What the Radiants were able to do
Which highprince hired the assassin
How to protect the Soulcasters
quiz.e: To learn how to fight a man who walks on walls, he asks what powers the Radiants had. Kadash realises the Radiants may not be dead.

quiz.q: How does Navani regard reports that Jasnah’s ship was lost with all hands?
o: She has already gone into mourning
She blames the ship’s captain for it
She has sent ships out to search
She trusts Jasnah will come through
quiz.e: This isn’t the first supposed disaster to strike Jasnah, who plays with danger and always comes through, Navani thinks.

quiz.q: What happens when the workers crank the floating wooden square down?
o: The archers’ parapet rises into the air
The square snaps its ropes and falls
The wooden tower topples off its rollers
The gemstones flare and then shatter
quiz.e: The parapet with its dummy archers wobbles upward, opposite to the square’s motion, and hangs in the air. It does not fall.

quiz.q: What about Navani’s safehand startles Adolin?
o: It is wrapped in a bandage
It holds a glowing fabrial
It is covered by a glove
It is stained with ink
quiz.e: She wears a glove instead of a sleeve: more practical, she says, and as dowager queen nobody cares what she does.

quiz.q: How does Navani hope the device might be used on the Shattered Plains?
o: To lay bridges across chasms
To raise archers fifty feet up
To carry wounded off plateaus
To lift spheres into storms
quiz.e: Roll one out, engage it and send word by spanreed: pulling the platform down in camp would lift archers fifty feet into a perfect position.

chapters.title: A New Woman
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

Vague and hard to pin down.

Grey-haired and weathered by age or hardship.

Shyness and a lack of courage.
Someone who takes advantage of situations for personal gain.

A large, slow crustacean that Rosharans use to pull wagons.
The con woman who took Shallan under her wing turned out to have run the attack on Jasnah. When Tyn moved to kill her, Shallan killed her with her Shardblade.
Shallan persuaded these deserters to save a caravan from bandits by promising that their crimes would be erased. Bluth died in that fight, carrying her heroic sketch of him.
Jasnah and Navani arranged a provisional betrothal, a “causal,” between Shallan and Dalinar’s son Adolin.
A message on Tyn’s spanreed said her backers, the Ghostbloods, wanted to meet in the warcamps. Shallan answered “Yes.”

quiz.q: How does Shallan get into Tyn’s locked trunk?
o: Vathah prises the lid off with an axe
Pattern slips in and opens the lock
She finds the key in Tyn’s satchel
She cuts the lock with her Shardblade
quiz.e: Pattern shrinks through the keyhole, sees “a pattern” in the lock by her sphere’s light, and pushes until it clicks.

quiz.q: What did Pattern find so fascinating about the men’s talk last night?
o: How often they talked about money
How they boasted of their battles
How they lied about their pasts
How much they talked about death
quiz.e: They kept wondering whether she would “come for them,” and Pattern marvels at how long humans can talk about nonexistence.

quiz.q: What does Vathah quietly ask when Shallan says to take her to the king?
o: Whether she means to kill the king
Whether she has met the king before
Whether the king owes her family
Whether the men should wait below
quiz.e: He supposes a woman with a Shardblade might get close and strike. He wouldn’t mind, but his men would struggle to escape.

quiz.q: What does Shallan draw in the lurching palanquin?
o: Jasnah studying among her books
Adolin in his blue Shardplate
Herself facing Dalinar, confident
The warcamps spread below the hill
quiz.e: She draws herself standing strong before Dalinar in Shardplate: the woman she would have been without a household of fear.

quiz.q: What happens when Shallan strides past the guards at the palace gates?
o: They demand to search her trunks
They let her by without challenge
They send a runner to fetch Dalinar
They refuse to admit her soldiers
quiz.e: Acting as if she belongs, she walks past sixteen guards. Only once she’s by does one call out to ask who she is.

quiz.q: What does the captain of Dalinar’s guard demand from Shallan?
o: Her name and her family’s house
A letter of introduction
Payment for safe passage
To know where his boots are
quiz.e: He recognises the “Horneater” from the road and asks, “Where are my boots?” He is Kaladin, captain of Dalinar’s guard.

quiz.q: What does Shallan ask Kaladin to show Navani?
o: A spanreed letter about the causal
A sketch she made of Jasnah’s ship
A ring bearing the Davar family seal
A list of the men in her service
quiz.e: It is one of Jasnah’s spanreed messages with Navani arranging the causal. Kaladin looks it over holding it upside down.

quiz.q: How does Gaz say he knows Kaladin?
o: They served in the same army
Kaladin once guarded his caravan
Kaladin was a slave where he worked
They grew up in the same town
quiz.e: Gaz says Kaladin was a slave at the lumberyards where he used to work, and calls him dangerous. Kaladin says Gaz tried to get him killed.

quiz.q: Who wears Adolin’s Shardplate during the meeting?
o: Renarin, seated behind Dalinar
Captain Kaladin, at the door
General Khal, in a side room
King Elhokar, as a precaution
quiz.e: Dalinar wanted Adolin to project confidence, not fear, so General Khal wears the Plate, hidden in a side room with a strike force.

quiz.q: What does Adolin offer to wager if Relis will duel him?

His Blade and a year’s income
His father’s Shardplate alone
His own Plate for Relis’s Blade

quiz.q: Asked whether his fear or his greed is stronger, what does Relis answer?

His fear
His honour
His pride

quiz.q: Who accepts Adolin’s challenge instead?

Relis’s cousin Elit
Highprince Ruthar
Brightlord Jakamav
quiz.e: Elit, who has only the Plate his cousin gave him, takes the same five-to-one offer and sets the duel seven days away.

Elit steps between the two of them
A swing could void his duel with Elit
Relis is still wearing his Shardplate

quiz.q: How does Sadeas describe his betrayal of Dalinar?
o: As a kindness to an old ally
As a mistake he now regrets
As following the king’s order
As revenge for an old insult
quiz.e: He calls it a kindness, “a tip of the sword” to an old ally, like holding the sword for a man as he falls on it.

quiz.q: Why does Amaram say he stays with Sadeas?
o: He disagrees with Dalinar’s Codes
Sadeas commands the largest army
Adolin’s duels have offended him
To bridge the gaps between them
quiz.e: Trusted by both Sadeas and Dalinar, he says he can bridge gaps and help keep the kingdom together; leaving would create a divide.

quiz.q: What does Amaram guess about the red-haired young woman?
o: That she’s Shin, by her pale skin
That she’s Veden, of Horneater blood
That she’s Thaylen, by her eyebrows
That she’s Herdazian, by her build
quiz.e: “Veden, I’d warrant,” he says, with Horneater blood. The word makes Adolin wonder, and he pushes through to his father.

She meant to write their history

A reward of a broam each
A fair trial before the king

His dueling
His hair
His manners

A post among his clerks
A seat at the king’s council
Funds to hire more guards

Highprince Hatham’s
Highprince Aladar’s
Highprince Sebarial’s

He will hunt the assassin himself
He will take his men back home

The royal armory in Kholinar
Adolin will win them in duels
Shards seized in Jah Keved

To win the highprince’s favour

A book by Jasnah Kholin

Helaran is coming home

A bracelet set with rubies
A necklace of silver links

To arrest Helaran for treason
To summon Davar’s men to war
