quiz.q: What joke is hidden in the talk Shallan claims to overhear?
o: Father is called a stubborn tree
The messenger’s cousin is a shrub
The trees beat Father for once
A pun on “relieved” and “re-leafed”
quiz.e: She invents a talk about disobedient trees that regrow leaves when sung to, ending with Father being “relieved.” Jushu works out the pun.

quiz.q: Why does Wikim say Shallan should be the one to testify?
o: She is the eldest child at home
Only a woman can write it down
Father won’t dare hurt her, and she saw it
The highprince is fond of her
quiz.e: Wikim hisses that Father won’t dare hurt her and that she actually saw what happened. She insists she doesn’t remember.

chapters.title: Palona
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: To understand something after thinking hard about it.
Punishment or revenge for a wrong.
A large building divided into rooms or flats for many families.
An old word for a factory or workshop.
Grown or made for decoration rather than use.
Something, such as a wall or row of trees, that shelters against wind.
A bad-tempered, grumpy person, usually old.
Constantly nagged and bossed about by one's partner.
In a way that weighs something up with curiosity.
Lurking out of sight, often with a sly purpose.
A fixed regular payment, such as an allowance or salary.
A uniformed male servant who opens doors and helps guests.
The fine mud that highstorm rains carry and leave everywhere.
A plump, bearded highprince whom Jasnah’s notes dismissed as obnoxious and useless. At the meeting of highprinces, Shallan announced she would stay with him, and he went along with it.
Dalinar agreed to keep the provisional betrothal between Shallan and Adolin in place for now, and offered her a clerk’s stipend.
Vathah and his band of former deserters followed Shallan to the Shattered Plains and now serve as her soldiers.

quiz.q: What does Sebarial remark on when he wakes in the carriage?
o: Her accent sounds Thaylen
She looks younger than before
She has her mother’s eyes
She is far too clever for Adolin
quiz.e: He says she looked twenty or more at the meeting, but now can’t be older than fourteen. She tells him she is seventeen.

quiz.q: What has Sebarial been doing while others hunt gemhearts?
o: Hoarding gemhearts in secret
Training a secret army out in the hills
Buying up all the Soulcasters
Building mills, farms and workshops
quiz.e: He has built an economy: textile mills, manufactories, glassblowers, farms, aiming to sell to the other camps.

quiz.q: Why does Sebarial say he tries to hate everyone?
o: So no one deserving is left out
So no one can ever betray him
Because the Alethi all expect it of him
Because he once lost a duel
quiz.e: He hates everyone so that he doesn’t risk leaving out anyone who is particularly deserving.

quiz.q: What proves to Shallan that Palona is Herdazian?
o: Her dark and very curly hair
Her fine, modern dress
Her rocklike fingernails
Her bright green eyes
quiz.e: Her curly hair first suggests northern Alethkar, but her accent and her fingernails, with a rocklike cast, mark her as Herdazian.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan say she chose not to stay with the Kholins?
o: Navani had already refused her a room
It might leave her too restricted
Adolin had asked her not to
Their camp was too far away
quiz.e: She explains she is to marry Adolin, but feared staying in the Kholin household would leave her too restricted.

quiz.q: What does Palona warn about the running water?
o: Never drink it before boiling
It runs only during a storm
The cook guards it jealously
Wait until midday after a storm
quiz.e: The cistern fills each highstorm and sifts out the crem, but used before midday after a storm the water runs brown.

chapters.title: Scars
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Made up of many different, ill-matched kinds.
A hard-shelled creature such as a crab or lobster.
In a way that seems out of place.
Fearful of or hostile to foreigners.
A soldier who fights for whoever pays.
Basic and original, from the very beginning.
Lacking solid form; not able to be touched.
Remade by heating and hammering again, like metal.
A deep groove or scrape cut into a surface.
A person or thing that causes trouble or puts others at risk.
Having epilepsy, a condition that causes repeated seizures.
So unreasonable as to be laughable.
Unfair dislike of a group of people, held without good reason.
Dalinar freed Sadeas’s bridgemen. Kaladin organised them into twenty crews, and Teft is training sergeants and men from each crew.
Someone cut the railing of the king’s balcony with a Shardblade, and Elhokar nearly fell to his death. Kaladin has been looking into it.
After the Assassin in White’s attack on the palace, glyphs were found on the wall: “Thirty-eight days. The end of all nations.”
The Highlord who killed Kaladin’s men, took the Shardblade Kaladin won, branded him and sold him as a slave. He has arrived in the warcamps, and is a friend of Dalinar’s.

quiz.q: Where does Teft say he was during the highstorm the other night?
o: Drilling the Bridge Seventeen men
Off duty, visiting the market
Asleep in the Bridge Four barrack
Guarding Brightness Navani
quiz.e: Teft claims he went to the market and time got away from him. Kaladin doubts it, but lets him keep his privacy.

quiz.q: What does Sigzil say about the Shin?
o: They often hire out as mercenaries
They trade Shardblades to foreigners
They serve as bodyguards to kings
They are wary of outsiders and stay home
quiz.e: The Shin are extremely xenophobic, rarely leave their lands and never work as mercenaries, so a Shin assassin puzzles him.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin finally get onto the chasm wall?
o: He makes the wall become “down”
He sticks his boots to it with Light
Syl lifts him up on a gust of wind
He climbs a rope Rock lowers
quiz.e: After glimpsing another place, he makes the wall’s direction become down, then walks and runs up it.

quiz.q: What will Kaladin do if he learns he can trust Dalinar?
o: Challenge Amaram to a duel
Leave the army with Bridge Four
Tell Dalinar what he can do
Join the King’s Guard himself
quiz.e: He must know whether Dalinar is what he seems. If so, he will tell him what he can do and maybe give him his Knights Radiant.

quiz.q: Why must the railing have been cut after that night’s highstorm?
o: The cut was still fresh and bright
Guards were posted before the storm
Rain would have washed out the dust
The wind would have bent it out of shape
quiz.e: Kaladin reasons that the storm would have blown the cut railing out of shape, so a Shardbearer cut it afterwards.

quiz.q: Why is the chasm floor so clear of debris?
o: Bridge Four cleared it for training
A chasmfiend scraped through it
A flood washed the bones away
Sadeas’s men salvaged it all
quiz.e: Deep gouges in the wall show that a chasmfiend passed through, scraping everything away, closer to the camps than expected.

quiz.q: What first task does Kaladin give Renarin?
o: Washing the dirty stew bowls
Patrolling outside the barrack
Running laps around the camp
Carrying a bridge with the men
quiz.e: He sends Renarin to wash the stew bowls and help Rock clean up, which Renarin does with surprising enthusiasm.

quiz.q: What does Moash say Kaladin should do about Amaram?
o: Report him to the authorities
Ask Dalinar to dismiss him
Get him into a duel
Forget him and move on
quiz.e: Moash laughs at going to the authorities; Kaladin must bring Amaram down man against man in a duel.

chapters.title: Mere Vapors
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A statement that makes something seem bigger or better than it is.
A go-between who passes messages between two sides.
To prove that something or someone is genuine.
To secretly join a group in order to spy on it.
Having sharp corners or bony, pointed features.
A bold, sweeping movement or stroke, as of a pen.
To wrap up or surround completely.
The value of a coin or note.
Demanding something firmly and refusing to give up.
Cutting off, or ending a connection.
Of a sphere: drained of its Stormlight, so it no longer glows.
A pair of linked pens: what one writes, the other copies far away.
After Shallan killed Tyn, Tyn’s distant contact wrote that the Ghostbloods wanted to meet her. Shallan, writing as Tyn, answered “Yes.”
The secret group that hired Tyn for the attack at sea on Jasnah’s ship.
Tyn taught Shallan the tricks of a con artist, and told her she was a natural at forging signatures.
The lost city Jasnah was searching for. Shallan means to carry on that search.

quiz.q: How does Shallan try to explain taste to Pattern?
o: Like colour you see with your mouth
Like music that you hear with your nose
Like patterns drawn on the tongue
Like Light you breathe into you
quiz.e: She calls it “like color . . . you see with your mouth,” then apologises for the awful metaphor.

quiz.q: What does Pattern spot in Tyn’s old spanreed messages?
o: Jasnah’s handwriting in the margins
A route marked to Urithiru
A code in their first words
Pages cut out and destroyed
quiz.e: The first words follow a code of letter quintets, used to prove the right person is writing. Without it, Shallan would have exposed herself.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan make her new face darkeyed?
o: Tyn’s apprentices were always darkeyed
A darkeyed woman draws less notice
Lighteyes are banned from that tenement
The Ghostbloods meet only darkeyes
quiz.e: An unknown lighteyes moving through camp would be remarked upon; a darkeyes is more invisible. She can hint at eyedrops if needed.

quiz.q: What flaw does Shallan find in her new face?
o: Her hair stays red at the roots
Her eyes keep flickering back to blue
Her shadow keeps its old shape
A fuzzy gap at the side of the nose
quiz.e: She left a spot unfinished on the side of the nose in her sketch, so the image has a gap there.

quiz.q: What excuse does Shallan, writing as Tyn, give for not going herself?
o: She is on a ship far away
She is hiding from Dalinar
The ward betrayed her, and she is unwell
She refuses to meet with strangers
quiz.e: She writes that she thought she had Jasnah’s ward captive but the girl betrayed her, and she will send her apprentice.

quiz.q: Why does the meeting take place in Sebarial’s warcamp?
o: Its gates are open all night
The Ghostbloods own a house there
Sebarial pays the Ghostbloods
It has no soldiers at all
quiz.e: The messenger says it is one of the few camps with gates open all night, and draws a map to a tenement there.

chapters.title: The Ghostbloods
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Easily noticed; standing out from the crowd.
Quick, neat and skilful, especially with the hands.
In a way that seems out of place with its surroundings.
Grand and richly furnished, like a palace.
A person or thing that is mysterious and hard to understand.
Careful and sensible about the future.
A go-between who passes messages or deals between two parties.
Objects kept as reminders of people, places or events.
A pipe or passage that carries smoke away from a fire.
One of the ranks into which Vorin darkeyes are sorted; the first and second are the highest.
A device powered by gemstones that produces some special effect.
A large, tusked and dangerous predator.
The con woman who trained Shallan on the road to the Shattered Plains. She had organised the attack on Jasnah at sea, and Shallan killed her with a Shardblade when Tyn turned on her.
Tyn’s employers. They want back the broken Soulcaster Shallan’s family held.
In her last chapter, writing as Tyn on Tyn’s spanreed, Shallan agreed that Tyn’s “apprentice” would meet the Ghostbloods that very night in Sebarial’s warcamp.
She sketched a darkeyed, dark-haired face and Lightwove it over her own, then dressed in Tyn’s long white coat, trousers and Bluth’s hat.
In the last book Jasnah walked the city with wealth on show to lure thieves into an alley, where she destroyed them with Soulcasting.

quiz.q: Why does the fruit seller freeze when Shallan holds out a sphere?
o: The sphere’s light is flickering and weak
Foreign Veden coins aren’t accepted here
An emerald mark is far too much to change
Darkeyes are forbidden to carry spheres
quiz.e: A stick of fruit costs a single clearchip; her emerald mark is worth 250 times that, far beyond a street vendor’s change.

quiz.q: What weapon does the scarred man in white keep firing at the wall?
o: A long reed blowgun that shoots darts
A small crossbow resting on the mantel
A sling loaded with polished stones
A set of slim, balanced throwing knives
quiz.e: He loads dart after dart into a long reed and blows them into a tapestry target, once while it is aimed right past her.

quiz.q: Why, Shallan argues, would he not want her to sell out Tyn for money?
o: Tyn would hunt him down for the insult
The sack holds less than Tyn pays her
Tyn has already left the Shattered Plains
She’d betray him too for a bigger bounty
quiz.e: If she betrayed Tyn for a price, she says, he would know she’d do the same to him if offered enough.

quiz.q: What name does Shallan give when the scarred man asks who she is?
o: Shara
Veil
Kesha
Mira
quiz.e: She calls herself Veil, a name she had been toying with. He tells her to call him Mraize.

quiz.q: What does Mraize want Tyn to do next?
o: Learn what secrets Amaram’s manor hides
Kill Brightlord Amaram before Chachel
Steal a Shardblade from Sadeas’s palace
Spy on Dalinar Kholin’s war councils
quiz.e: Amaram is his “prey.” Tyn is to investigate the manor near Sadeas’s palace and report, without harming Amaram or raising suspicion.

quiz.q: What does Shallan spot on Mraize’s scarred right hand?
o: A tattoo of the Kholin glyphpair
A brand marking him a former slave
A ring bearing the symbol Jasnah drew
A spanreed strapped to his wrist
quiz.e: His signet ring bears the symbol Jasnah drew, the one Kabsal had tattooed on his body. Shallan decides there is no backing out.

quiz.q: Why does her first try at a new illusion in the alley fail?
o: Her spheres have all gone completely dun
Pattern is off watching the masked woman
A drunk in the alley is staring right at her
She has no detailed sketch to work from
quiz.e: The Stormlight just puffs out. The only difference from her rooms is that there she had drawn a detailed picture first.

quiz.q: How does Shallan shake off the masked woman tailing her?
o: She ducks into a crowded tavern and waits
She hides in a doorway behind a false wall
She doubles back through the busy market
She climbs onto a rooftop and lies flat
quiz.e: She draws a stone wall while walking, ducks into a doorway recess and covers it with the image; the woman passes by.

chapters.title: One Form of Justice
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Rich, costly and generous in amount.
The point at which something starts to take effect; a limit.
Something close to, but not exactly, the real thing.
An earlier action used as an example or rule for later ones.
Too annoying or arrogant to bear.
Looking at someone in an unpleasant, suggestive way.
Clashing; not in harmony with something else.
An official inquiry to find out the facts of a case.
An official who judges cases under the law.
Overly suspicious and distrustful of others.
In Vorin belief, the life’s work through which a person improves and serves.
A religious order of ardents that a Vorin believer joins.
The ardent swordmaster who trains Renarin. After the attack on the king, Kaladin knocked on his door late at night and was told to come back by day.
Dalinar’s younger son, who now trains with Zahel in Shardplate. He has asked Kaladin to let him serve in Bridge Four.
Someone cut the railing of Elhokar’s balcony with a Shardblade. Kaladin worked out that it must have been done after the highstorm that night.
On the road to the warcamps, posing as a Horneater princess, Shallan demanded a soldier’s boots as an apology. The soldier was Kaladin, who later confronted her at the palace.
The commander who made Kaladin a slave and killed his men. He is now at the Shattered Plains, serving with Highprince Sadeas.

quiz.q: What does Zahel mean when he says Kaladin has “red on his ears”?
o: He is embarrassed before his betters
He is angry and spoiling for a fight
He is too worn out to train properly
He is new and untested in real battle
quiz.e: Zahel calls it a “damnation language” idiom: feeling you have something to prove, angry at everything and everyone.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin decline to hold the Shardblade himself?
o: Zahel has forbidden him to touch it
He worries the king would object to it
He fears it might bond to him by mistake
Those things have killed too many friends
quiz.e: He says Shardblades have killed too many of his friends. Instead he asks Zahel to swing one at him, with no guard.

quiz.q: What worry about Shallan does Teft raise?
o: She’d make a good assassin for Adolin
She might be a spy for Highprince Sadeas
She might be after the Kholin fortune
She might have sabotaged the balcony
quiz.e: A foreign woman nobody knows, suddenly Adolin’s betrothed: Teft says she’d make a good assassin, and Kaladin wishes he’d seen it.

quiz.q: What reason does Shallan give Nall for coming to the grounds?
o: To watch Adolin spar for the first time
To ask the ardents to choose her devotary
To sketch the king’s Shardplate and Blades
To hand Kaladin back his boots in person
quiz.e: She shows Nall a portfolio: the royal record of Shards has only rough sketches, and she wants to make detailed new ones.

quiz.q: How, according to Moash, did his grandparents die?
o: Beheaded in public by the king’s order
In a fire set at their silversmith shop
Waiting in the dungeons for an inquest
Struck down by a lighteyed rival’s men
quiz.e: Elhokar, favouring a rival silversmith, had them jailed on some charge; they died months later, still waiting for a hearing.

quiz.q: What does Moash ask of Kaladin in return for stopping?
o: To meet and listen to the others involved
To keep Elhokar out of Bridge Four’s care
To help him win a Shardblade of his own
To leave the king’s guard duty to others
quiz.e: The plan wasn’t his idea. He wants Kaladin to hear the others out, and swears on his grandparents’ honour to do nothing until then.

quiz.q: Why, Syl says, is killing Amaram not the same as justice?
o: Amaram is protected by the king’s law
Thinking about him is twisting Kaladin
Amaram has already been punished enough
Only the Heralds may judge a Shardbearer
quiz.e: It is about what it does to him: thinking of Amaram changes and twists him, and he is supposed to protect, not kill.

quiz.q: What does Zahel think of catching a Shardblade between the palms?
o: A rare skill that is worth years of practice
A trick that only works in Shardplate
An old Radiant technique, long lost now
A stupid move that usually gets you killed
quiz.e: He calls the “lastclap” stupid: it only works because Shardbearers swing softly, and usually it fails. Kaladin accepts the logic.

chapters.title: Middlefest
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Departing from what is normal or accepted.
Tall, thin and awkward in movement.
Sounding far grander or more important than it really is.
Being well known, often for something bad.
A bundle of papers held together.
Holding false beliefs despite clear evidence.
Dull and lacking in thought or liveliness.
Shocking to people’s sense of what is proper.
Polite respect shown to someone of higher rank.
Cut off from receiving an inheritance.
A large container for serving wine or other drink.
One of the ranks into which Vorin lighteyes are sorted; the lower the number, the higher the rank.
Helaran, the eldest, carries a Shardblade and has left home. Below him come Balat and then the twins, Wikim and Jushu.
Rumours say Brightlord Davar killed his wife. He insists her lover killed her and then himself.
At a gloomy Davar feast, Father announced he would remarry. The highprince’s bastard, Redin, then came seeking testimony about their mother’s death, and none of the children would speak.
A neighbouring lighteyed family who were guests at that feast. Their daughter and Balat traded glances across the room.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan call the merchant’s “chicken” a Voidbringer?
o: It hatched in the middle of a storm
Its eyes glow a deep red in shadow
It grew back a leg it had lost
It can speak its own name aloud
quiz.e: It says “Jeksonofnone,” and she fears a talking animal will draw the eyes of the Unmade. The merchant says they live all over Shinovar.

quiz.q: Why does Father give in to Revilar’s lopsided trade deal?
o: Revilar holds most of Father’s debts
Revilar now has the highprince’s favour
Revilar threatens to expose Helaran
Revilar’s son beat Balat in a duel
quiz.e: The highprince visited Revilar and invited him to Vedenar. Father’s house is declining and his reputation is in shambles; he needs allies.

quiz.q: Where does Shallan find her brother Balat?
o: Drinking with tenners beside the duels
Playing cards with the waiting coachmen
Watching axehound fights in a gambling tent
Sparring on the sand of the dueling ring
quiz.e: In the ragged gambling pavilion he sits alone, fixed on two axehounds fighting. She gives him Eylita’s note inviting him to walk by the stream.

quiz.q: What does Father declare after the black-clad visitor leaves?
o: Helaran is disinherited; Balat is heir
Shallan will be married within the year
The family will leave the fair at once
Balat is banned from the gambling tent
quiz.e: The visitor brought word from Helaran. Father forbids his name: Tet Balat is now Nan Balat, and he has “only three sons.”

quiz.q: What has Shallan prepared for Wikim?
o: A book of Azish grammar to study
Math problems for timing highstorms
A sketch of the family in the gardens
A letter from the ardents inviting him
quiz.e: She copied highstorm-timing equations from Father’s books into glyphs. He calls it stupid, but later she sees him smiling as he works them.

quiz.q: What, Shallan suggests, would beauty be to a man who knows only pain?
o: The memory of what he once saw
Nothing; it has been taken away
The kindness of those who tend him
The times when the pain lessens
quiz.e: She asks whether the pain changes day by day; told it does, she says beauty would be the times it eases.

quiz.q: What happens as Shallan describes her most beautiful scene?
o: Stormlight rises from the man’s spheres
The jella trees nearby burst into bloom
Her satchel’s sketches start to glow
Wikim and Balat come looking for her
quiz.e: The messenger holds out spheres and Stormlight rises between them, the image wrapping around her, until she pulls back and it fades.

quiz.q: Where, the messenger finally says, is Helaran?
o: In Kharbranth
In Thaylenah
In Alethkar
In Vedenar
quiz.e: Helaran is in Alethkar, “where he feels he is needed.” His message to Father was that he has eyes nearby and is watching.

chapters.title: Patriots
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A small unit of soldiers under one leader.
Not in harmony; quarrelsome and at odds.
A small, tight group of people who keep others out.
Gloomy, sullen and low in spirits.
A point that is argued over; a complaint.
Someone who calls out news or announcements in public.
On the side sheltered from the wind.
Seen as a dark outline against a brighter background.
The state of being unable or unwilling to believe something.
To coax someone into doing something by flattery or persistence.
Someone who rules on behalf of a monarch who is too young or unable to rule.
A sudden seizure of power from a government, often by force.
Of a wound: becoming infected and growing worse.

Moash told Kaladin that King Elhokar left his grandparents to die in the palace dungeons. He admitted a part in the plot against the king, and Kaladin agreed to hear out the others involved if Moash stopped in the meantime.
Someone cut the railing of the king’s balcony with a Shardblade, hoping his fall would look like an accident.
Glyphs scratched into walls during highstorms have been counting down the days to some coming event: “Death follows,” and later “A new storm comes.”
Bridge Four’s Horneater cook, from the distant Horneater Peaks. Unlike the other bridgemen, he could see Syl when she was hidden from them.

quiz.q: What problem does Kaladin find with Bridge Eighteen?
o: Their sergeant drills them much too harshly
They have split into cliques that don’t mingle
They have been selling off their uniforms
They refuse to patrol beyond the warcamp
quiz.e: The men sit in isolated bunches with no camaraderie, and their weak sergeant, Vet, begs rather than orders.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin tell Syl he must keep working so hard?
o: Dalinar has ordered an inspection of the crews
Sadeas’s soldiers keep testing the camp’s guard
He thinks something is coming at the Weeping
The king wants twice as many guards by the Weeping
quiz.e: The countdowns on the walls point right toward the Weeping, and he wants the bridgemen ready for whatever comes.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin give Shen in the storeroom?
o: A Bridge Four patch for his uniform
Papers granting the parshman his freedom
A sergeant’s rank within Bridge Four
His spear, after speaking to Dalinar
quiz.e: Kaladin asked Dalinar about arming Shen, says “Bridge Four doesn’t have slaves,” and hands him his own spear.

quiz.q: In Rock’s story, which gods did the tana’kai ask for help first?
o: The gods of the trees
The gods of the waters
The gods of the mountains
The gods of the winds
quiz.e: He went first to the gods of the trees, then the waters, and last to the mountains, who withdrew their peaks to make room for the waters of life.

quiz.q: How does Rock describe Lunu’anaki, the god he says he met?
o: An old man with a long grey beard
A Horneater woman dressed in green
A tall figure made of flowing water
A young man with white hair
quiz.e: He looked like a person, perhaps Alethi but paler, young but with white hair; he mocked Rock’s beard. Sigzil looks up sharply at this.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin recognize Danlan, the woman at the table?
o: She reads Sadeas’s letters to him
She is one of Dalinar’s clerks
She serves wine at the king’s feasts
She sold him a map in the market
quiz.e: He recognizes her as one of Dalinar’s clerks; Graves says she is part of the highprince’s retinue.

quiz.q: What comparison does Graves use to persuade Kaladin?
o: A festering hand that threatens the body
A storm that must be left to blow itself out
A lame horse that has to be put down
A cracked bridge that has to be replaced
quiz.e: Knowing Kaladin trained as a surgeon, Graves asks whether you wait or act when a festering hand threatens the whole body.

quiz.q: What does Moash point out about Graves afterward?
o: He once carried bridges for Sadeas
He paid off Moash’s caravan debts
He married a darkeyed woman
He fought beside Dalinar at the Tower
quiz.e: Moash says Graves treats all men the same: he married a darkeyed woman, and one of his sons is a one-eye.

chapters.title: Feminine Wiles
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: The science and craft of making maps.
A note added to a text to explain or comment on it.
A title or name given as a mark of respect.
A small sign added to a letter to show how it is pronounced.
To put forward an idea as a likely possibility.
Showing too much satisfaction with oneself.
In a figurative way, rather than a literal one.
A tap that controls the flow of liquid from a pipe or container.
Someone who designs and builds fabrials, devices powered by gemstones.
A fixed, regular payment, often to cover living costs.
Someone who eats or indulges far too much.
A tall stand with a sloping top, for holding a book while reading aloud.
A servant who attends a carriage, opening doors and helping passengers.
The act of adding to or enhancing something.
Clever tricks used to charm or persuade.
The blunt, bearded highprince who took Shallan into his household, claiming her as a distant relation. Palona, who shares his manor, helped settle her in.
Two of the deserters who followed Shallan out of the wilderness. They now serve as her guards.
Dalinar has kept Shallan’s provisional betrothal to Adolin for now, but she must win over Dalinar, Navani and Adolin himself.
The legendary city of the Knights Radiant. Jasnah hoped its untouched records would support her warnings, and Shallan has taken up her search.
The old book about the Knights Radiant that Jasnah gave Shallan aboard ship. It was lost to the sea.

quiz.q: What puzzles Shallan about the old maps of the Silver Kingdoms?
o: None of them show Alethkar at all
They show the Plains as a great sea
Each puts Urithiru somewhere else
All are written in the same hand
quiz.e: Each map places Urithiru in a different spot, close to the mapmaker’s own lands but never in them.

quiz.q: What surprising thing does Pattern manage with the maps?
o: He picks out a few words of the Dawnchant
He spots which of the maps is a forgery
He redraws one of them from memory alone
He finds a hidden seal under the wax
quiz.e: He postulates a few words, including a form of Nohadon’s name, saying the scripts are derived from one another.

quiz.q: According to Jasnah’s note, what pervades the folktales in Among the Darkeyed?
o: Knights who guard a tower in the sky
A storm that never stops blowing
Shardblades that sing during battle
Instantaneous travel and the Oathgates
quiz.e: The note convinces Shallan that Jasnah hoped to find a passage to Urithiru on the Shattered Plains.

quiz.q: How has Shallan tried to reach her brothers?
o: She asked Navani to write to them
She sent two letters by different routes
She hired Vathah to ride out to Jah Keved
She had Sebarial send a courier
quiz.e: She sent a letter and a spanreed from Valath through a Tashikk information station, and a second letter from Northgrip, far from the fighting.

quiz.q: What does Vathah complain about as Shallan boards the coach?
o: He is bored with doing nothing
His men are being paid too little
Gaz keeps mocking him to the men
Sebarial’s guards treat them badly
quiz.e: He admits the men are happy, but all they do is sit around, collect their pay and go drinking.

quiz.q: What finally makes her illusion of black hair take hold?
o: Holding a ruby against her temple
Asking Pattern to speak the change
Sketching herself with dark hair first
Closing her eyes and holding her breath
quiz.e: Without a sketch the Light vanishes; after a quick drawing of herself with dark hair, the image takes.

quiz.q: How does Shallan discover she can end an illusion?
o: By tearing up the sketch it came from
By closing her eyes until it fades
By ordering Pattern to dismiss it
By breathing its Stormlight back in
quiz.e: With her hand inside the image of Sebarial, she sucks in a breath and the image dissolves into her skin.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan decide not to enhance her looks for Adolin?
o: Pattern tells her it would be dishonest
She couldn’t wear an illusion always
She has used up all her Stormlight
Navani has warned her against tricks
quiz.e: She wonders whether Adolin would want her or the lies, and knows she couldn’t keep an illusion up in married life.

chapters.title: No More Weakness
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: The structure of the body, as studied by artists and doctors.

Disagreement, especially open disagreement with authority.
Getting money from someone by threats or force.
Overindulgence, especially in food and drink.
A pile of wood for burning a body at a funeral.
Proud and looking down on others.
To pay off a debt; also, to make up for a fault.
Something meant to discourage people from doing something.
Wisely and carefully, with an eye to the future.
A Vorin priest or priestess; ardents also serve lords’ households as scholars and teachers.
Balat, now Father’s heir since Helaran was disinherited; Wikim, studious and often despairing; and Jushu, Wikim’s twin, who drinks and gambles.
In the previous flashback, Shallan arranged for Balat to meet Eylita Tavinar, and left mathematical problems that cheered Wikim.
At the fair, this neighbour, newly in the highprince’s favour, pressured Father into a badly lopsided trade deal.
Brightlord Lin Davar has grown violent. After Helaran’s threatening letter, he beat a maid nearly to death.
At the fair, a stranger bringing word of Helaran urged Shallan to “keep cutting at those thorns” and make a path for the light.

quiz.q: Who read Balat his latest letter from Eylita?
o: Wikim
Shallan
Malise
Jushu
quiz.e: Balat had Malise read it, saying Shallan was busy; Wikim teases him for being embarrassed.

quiz.q: How does Shallan finish “Love is like a Herdazian surgeon”?
o: You’d only want one after a blow to the head
Both cut much deeper than you would expect
Both will charge you twice the fair price
Neither one will ever wash his hands first
quiz.e: After a false start (“Both leave you uncomfortable?”), she says the only reason you’d want one is a sharp blow to the head.

quiz.q: What does Wikim give Shallan in a small pouch?
o: Spheres he won betting at the fair
Blackbane leaves he no longer needs
A ring that belonged to their mother
Seeds from Father’s ornamental garden
quiz.e: He has carried the poisonous leaves for most of a year and no longer feels he needs them; he thanks her, saying what she is doing is working.

quiz.q: Why have the men in old-style clothing come for Jushu?
o: He insulted their master at a feast
He stole a horse from their stables
He deserted from the highprince’s army
He ran up gambling debts he can’t pay
quiz.e: Jushu, meant to be riding the outer holdings, gambled with them; he promised Father would pay, and Father refuses.

quiz.q: What does Shallan accuse Father of doing with money they don’t have?
o: Bribing favor from supposed allies
Buying a Shardblade for Balat to carry
Paying for Helaran’s return home
Adding a new wing to the manor
quiz.e: The ledgers show huge debts. Father says he will make House Davar a force in the princedom.

quiz.q: What does Shallan offer the moneylender for Jushu?
o: Her sketchbook and her best gown
A letter promising that Father will pay
Her brothers’ knives and her necklace
Two of Father’s horses and a coach
quiz.e: Balat and Wikim hand over their knives, and she adds her aluminum necklace: thirty emerald broams, about half the debt.

quiz.q: What reason does Shallan give the moneylender to show Jushu pity?
o: Jushu once saved her from drowning
Jushu is the heir of House Davar
Their father is gravely ill at home
Jushu held her when Mother was killed
quiz.e: She says their mother was murdered, and that night Jushu held her as she cried. He frees Jushu and gives back the necklace.

quiz.q: What does Father tell Shallan when he comes to her room?
o: She will be sent to a convent at once
Others will suffer if she disobeys
Jushu is to be sent away for good
She is to be married within the year
quiz.e: After hurting the maid Minara, he says others create his anger, and he would not want to punish anyone else because of her.

chapters.title: Watching the World Transform
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A railing supported by a row of short posts, along a terrace or balcony.
A person who flatters powerful people to win their favour.
A large book or case of loose sheets, such as drawings or maps.
Unstoppable; impossible to calm or turn aside.
Hushed and secretive, as if sharing a private plot.
A piece of armour that protects the shin.
An old, well-known saying that expresses a general truth.
Based on observation or experiment rather than theory.
The system of methods used to do or study something.
A hunting animal at the top of its food chain, with no natural enemies.
To pass through the resting stage, often inside a case, between young and adult forms.
Moving from one region to another at certain times of life or of the year.

An air of mystery and allure that surrounds someone.
Jasnah arranged a causal, a provisional betrothal, between Shallan and Adolin Kholin. Dalinar has agreed to keep it in place for now.
The crude, plump highprince who has given Shallan a home in his warcamp, telling the other highprinces she is a distant relation.
Chasmfiends come up onto the plateaus of the Shattered Plains to form chrysalises. The Alethi race to kill them for their gemhearts, which Soulcasters use to make food.
In the last book, Sadeas abandoned Dalinar and Adolin to the Parshendi on the Tower plateau. Bridge Four rescued them, and Dalinar then traded his Shardblade to Sadeas for the bridgemen’s freedom.
Jasnah believed the Voidbringers were connected to the parshmen, the quiet servants found everywhere in Alethi society.

quiz.q: Why does the winehouse terrace make Shallan feel uneasy at first?
o: It hangs out over a deep chasm
It faces east, toward the Origin
It has no railing along its edge
It is crowded with Sadeas’s men
quiz.e: Terraces normally face away from the storms, but this one looks east toward the Origin, which makes her feel exposed.

quiz.q: What is in the oversized folio Adolin is browsing when Shallan arrives?
o: Battle maps of the Shattered Plains
Designs for a new suit of Shardplate
A list of the season’s highstorms
Fashions from Liafor and Azir
quiz.e: The glyphs, with women’s script beneath, label it as fashions out of Liafor and Azir.

quiz.q: How does Adolin confess he really chooses wine?
o: Mostly by its colour
By asking Renarin first
By the price on the list
By what the king drinks
quiz.e: He orders something that sounds important, but admits he is really just choosing based on colour.

quiz.q: What does Shallan ask Adolin in the middle of his story about the plateau run?
o: Whether his father’s greave was ever repaired
How many Parshendi he killed by himself
What he does if he needs to relieve himself
Why he didn’t simply jump back across
quiz.e: Instead of asking what happened next, she asks what he does if he needs to poop in his Shardplate.

quiz.q: Which creature’s chrysalis does Shallan say matches Adolin’s description of a chasmfiend’s?
o: A yu-nerig from the seas near Marabethia
A whitespine from the Unclaimed Hills
A santhid that trails ships at sea
A chull of the kind farmers raise
quiz.e: Adolin points to the chrysalis of a yu-nerig, an aquatic greatshell that only comes onto land to pupate.

quiz.q: What problem does Shallan see in the way the armies kill chasmfiends?
o: The gemhearts lose their Stormlight over time
The hunts draw the Parshendi closer to the camps
Their carcasses are poisoning the chasms
Killing the young could shrink their numbers
quiz.e: Greatshells breed slowly; killing over a hundred and fifty juveniles a year could make the population collapse.

quiz.q: How does Adolin react when Shallan asks about getting rid of the parshmen?
o: He says his father is already planning to do it
He calls it impossible and kingdom-breaking
He says Sadeas has suggested the same
He agrees the parshmen seem suspicious
quiz.e: He calls it impossible, “or really impossible,” and says it would break the kingdom in a heartbeat.

quiz.q: What does Shallan point out once the doors of the shelter are barred?
o: The storm was weaker than she had feared
Pattern had stayed out on the open terrace
They could have stayed out six seconds more
The parshmen had left Adolin’s guards outside
quiz.e: She counts six seconds between the doors closing and the storm hitting, and wishes they had stayed out longer.

Kaladin’s bridgemen, now Dalinar’s guard, protect the Kholin family, which includes following Adolin wherever he goes.
A Parshendi Shardbearer stopped Adolin on a plateau to ask to speak with Dalinar, and a messenger has since arranged a meeting.

quiz.q: According to Elit, what does his cousin plan to do about the duel?
o: Kill Adolin, then Elit for agreeing
Fight Adolin himself in Elit’s place
Ask the king to forbid the duel
Lend Elit his own Shardblade
quiz.e: Elit says his cousin plans to kill Adolin for challenging him, right after he kills Elit for accepting.

quiz.q: What does Adolin notice about the emeralds on Sadeas’s coat and ring?
o: They are fakes made out of painted glass
They were a gift from King Elhokar
They are uncut, fresh from a gemheart
They have been drained of Stormlight
quiz.e: The emeralds are uncut, won on a plateau run with Ruthar that Sadeas was not supposed to be on.

quiz.q: What does Sadeas reveal about his title of Highprince of Information?
o: He wants Adolin to serve as his deputy
He has recently renounced it
He plans to use it against Dalinar
The king has stripped it from him
quiz.e: Sadeas says he renounced the title and hints that the other highprinces agree none of them suit such appointments.

quiz.q: Why does Adolin stop himself from summoning his Blade against Sadeas?
o: His bridgemen guards hold his arm back
Sadeas is wearing his Shardplate
Shallan is still in the shelter with him
It would undermine the laws his father upholds
quiz.e: He wants to force Sadeas into the dueling ring instead, since killing him would undermine the codes Dalinar works to uphold.

quiz.q: What does Sadeas predict for himself and Adolin?
o: A firm alliance after a long civil war
A duel between them within the month
A marriage between their two houses
Exile for Adolin within the year
quiz.e: He predicts that in ten years or so, after an extended civil war between them, their alliance will be strong.

quiz.q: What do the glyphs scratched into the sitting-room floor say?
o: “Sixty-two days. Death follows.”
“Thirty-two days. Seek the center.”
“The Voidbringers come. Seek the tower.”
“Thirty days. Trust no highprince.”
quiz.e: A short Azish bridgeman reads them: “Thirty-two days. Seek the center.”

quiz.q: What points to Dalinar as the one who made the scratches?
o: Navani saw him kneeling there in the storm
His hands were found covered in stone dust
A bridgeman heard him scratching at the floor
His own knife lay blunted by his study door
quiz.e: His side knife was found blunted and flecked with stone just outside the study where he spent the highstorm alone.

quiz.q: When does Navani work out that the thirty-two days will end?
o: On the very first day of the new year
During the first highstorm after the Weeping ends
In the middle of the Weeping, before year’s end
On the anniversary of Gavilar’s death
quiz.e: She says it falls in the middle of the Weeping, two days ahead of the end of the year.

Adolin’s younger brother now has Shards of his own and has insisted on joining Bridge Four, wearing its uniform.
The Shin assassin who killed Gavilar struck again earlier in this book during a highstorm, and Kaladin fought him off.
After Gavilar’s murder, the highprinces swore a pact to punish the Parshendi, which is why the Alethi armies came to the Shattered Plains.
In the last chapter, new glyphs reading “Thirty-two days. Seek the center” were found scratched into the floor of Dalinar’s quarters.

quiz.q: What decision does Adolin announce at the morning planning meeting?
o: He will go to the meeting in Dalinar’s place
He will challenge Sadeas to a duel at once
He will stop dueling until the war ends
He will ask the king to cancel the meeting
quiz.e: He insists his father is too important to risk and that he will go in Dalinar’s place, borrowing Renarin’s Plate.

quiz.q: What does Adolin find strangest about the ride out?
o: Wearing armour that is not his own
Riding his father’s horse, Gallant
Leading the army without Renarin
Crossing on a mobile bridge again
quiz.e: The Plate soon feels like his own and he is used to leading; the strangest part is riding Gallant instead of Sureblood.

quiz.q: What is the strange rock mound at the center of the meeting plateau?
o: The worn ruin of an ancient Radiant tower
A Parshendi shrine carved from stone
A dead chasmfiend crusted over with crem
A cairn marking an old Alethi grave
quiz.e: Adolin realizes a chasmfiend died there centuries ago and slowly crusted over with crem, leaving a stone likeness.

quiz.q: How does Adolin try to keep Eshonai from realizing he is not Dalinar?
o: He lets his scribe do all of the speaking
He claims an illness has changed his voice
He stays mounted on Gallant the whole time
He keeps his helm on and deepens his voice
quiz.e: He pitches his voice down to match his father’s and hopes the helm will be enough to fool her.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai say when Adolin proposes terms of surrender?
o: That this is not the point at all
That her people will surrender soon
That she must ask her gods first
That only Elhokar can set terms
quiz.e: She laughs and says that is not the point at all; things have changed since she spoke to his son.

quiz.q: According to Eshonai, when will there be peace?
o: When the Alethi leave the Shattered Plains
When one of them is dead
When Gavilar’s killer is handed over
When the Weeping has come and gone
quiz.e: She says there will be peace “when one of us is dead,” and warns that they have changed the rules of the conflict.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai say Gavilar did wrong on the night of his death?
o: He insulted the Parshendi drummers
He tried to steal their Shardblades
He revealed his plans and bragged to them
He refused to sign their peace treaty
quiz.e: She says he should not have revealed his plans that night; he bragged, thinking they would welcome the return of their gods.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar ask of Adolin as he plans an assault across the Plains?
o: To guard Navani while the army is away
To make peace with Sadeas before the army marches
To lead the scouts toward the center first
To win high-profile duels against Sadeas’s side
quiz.e: He wants Adolin to win Shards in duels with as much fanfare as possible, focusing on the Shardbearers loyal to Sadeas.

Szeth, the Shin assassin, recently attacked the king’s palace. Kaladin fought him and watched him run along walls and ceilings, and he is determined to beat him next time.

The highlord Kaladin once served under, who betrayed him and had him branded and sold as a slave. Kaladin’s younger brother Tien died while they served in Amaram’s army. Amaram now lives in Sadeas’s warcamp.

Moash brought Kaladin to meet Graves and others who want King Elhokar dead so that Dalinar will rule. They asked Kaladin, now in charge of the King’s Guard, to give them an opening.

quiz.q: What happens if Shallan waits too long before using a sketch for a disguise?
o: The image comes out blurred, as if melted
The disguise drains Stormlight twice as fast
Pattern can no longer recognize the face
The disguise flickers whenever she speaks
quiz.e: She has found that a sketch works for about a day; after that the image she makes is blurred and sometimes looks melted.

quiz.q: Mistaking her for the maid, what task does the cook give Shallan?
o: Scrubbing the pots with the kitchen girls
Carrying curry up to the master’s room
Polishing mirrors for Stine in the study
Mending uniforms for Amaram’s guards
quiz.e: The cook, who has noticed the maid sneaking off, sends her to polish mirrors for Stine, who is cleaning Amaram’s flutes.

quiz.q: How does Shallan lure Amaram away from his locked room?
o: She says the king has sent for him at once
She says Hav stopped a messenger for him
She warns him of a fire in the kitchens
She says a guard caught a thief outside
quiz.e: Posing as the maid Telesh, she claims Hav stopped a messenger coming for Amaram, so he pockets his key and goes to see.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin find is the real trick to jumping between surfaces?
o: Timing each jump with the wind
Landing with his knees bent low
Keeping his eyes fixed on Syl
Overcoming his body’s fear
quiz.e: It isn’t landing, reflexes or timing: it is about fear, the panic his body feels every time down stops being down.

quiz.q: How does Amaram write the word “Parshendi” in his glyph notes?
o: He draws a small chasmfiend beside a glyph
He borrows letters from the women’s script
He uses glyphs for their sounds, underlined
He copies a cipher found in Jasnah’s work
quiz.e: Shallan realizes he strings glyphs together by their sounds (“Parap-shenesh-idi”) and underlines them when he does so.

quiz.q: Where does Amaram say his Shardblade and Plate came from?
o: A Parshendi Shardbearer he killed in battle
A red-haired Veden who tried to kill him
A gift from Sadeas for long and loyal service
A duel he won against a Thaylen champion
quiz.e: He says both belonged to an unnamed young Veden assassin with red hair. Shallan knows the Blade as her brother Helaran’s.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin turn back rather than go after Amaram that night?
o: Syl threatens to leave him if he goes on
Moash talks him out of it on the road
He sees guards posted around the manor
He won’t taint the joy of his first flight
quiz.e: After Syl’s “But tonight?”, he decides not to spoil the memory of his first true joy in ages, and says, “Not tonight.”

quiz.q: What does Shen tell Kaladin before he leaves?
o: That his real name is Rlain
That Moash cannot be trusted
That the Parshendi will attack
That he must go back to Sadeas
quiz.e: Shen says he must leave and cannot say why, then adds, “My name is not Shen. It is Rlain.”

Navani reacted with anger and grief when Shallan described the attack at sea in which Shallan believes Jasnah was killed.

quiz.q: How does Adolin turn aside Elit’s thrust at his faceplate?

He catches it on his raised left vambrace
He lets it slide along his hand and up
He knocks it down with his own Blade

quiz.q: How does Adolin finally defeat Elit?

He shatters Elit’s helm with a last blow
Elit yields after losing hold of his Blade
He drives his Blade through a Plate joint

quiz.q: What does Navani do when Shallan arrives in the staging room?

She invites Shallan to dine with her
She scolds Adolin for the dull duel
She leaves, her glyphward unfinished

quiz.q: Where did Shallan find the idea she thinks could help Adolin?

In King Gavilar’s biography
In Jasnah’s notes on dueling
In an old book of Alethi law

quiz.q: What does Adolin offer when Relis refuses to duel him?

To fight him without wearing any Shardplate
To give Relis the first strike for free
To let Relis pick both the day and the place
quiz.e: Thinking of Shallan’s “spectacular”, Adolin says he’ll fight Relis and whomever he brings together. Relis sets it for two days later.

quiz.q: Whom does Shallan ask Adolin about as the chapter ends?
o: Highprince Ruthar
Highprince Aladar
Highprince Sadeas
Highprince Yenev
quiz.e: Having heard Adolin’s plan, she sits beside him and asks what he knows of Highprince Yenev.

As Veil, Shallan told Mraize that the con artist Tyn had sent her as an intermediary instead of coming herself.
The scarred Ghostblood with a blowgun and a strange, masked companion. Through Veil, he ordered Tyn to investigate Amaram’s secrets and report back the next week.
Shallan slipped into it and found maps and glyph notes about the Voidbringers. Afterwards she realized Amaram’s Shardblade had been her brother Helaran’s, and that Amaram had killed him.

quiz.q: What does Shallan conclude about the Parshendi blowgun?
o: It was made to bring down chasmfiends
It was mainly meant as a weapon of war
It was used to feed a family, not for sport
It was a sacred tool used in their rites
quiz.e: She reasons it is for small game: a hunter who wants trophies seeks grand prey, but this is the weapon of a man feeding his family.

quiz.q: Why does Mraize at first think Tyn never even tried the task?
o: His people watching the house saw nothing
Tyn sent no word by spanreed all week
Amaram has doubled the guards at his door
Veil comes to the meeting empty-handed
quiz.e: He has people watching Amaram’s house, and later asks how Veil got in, since they watched the windows.

quiz.q: What does Shallan deliberately leave out of her pictures for Mraize?
o: The faces of Amaram’s guards
The layout of Amaram’s manor
The maps of the Shattered Plains
The actual writing on the walls
quiz.e: She draws the script as wiggly lines on purpose, keeping its details from the Ghostbloods, though she could have drawn it.

quiz.q: How does Mraize test Veil’s claim to draw from memory?
o: He has her sketch the pavilion with her eyes shut
He has her draw the man Jin after he walks off
He shows her a map, then burns it before her
He has her copy the masked woman’s carapace mask
quiz.e: He tells Jin to leave and Veil to draw him. Even a nervous sketch delights Mraize.

quiz.q: What does Mraize guess about Tyn?
o: That she has fled the warcamps
That she sold Veil out to Amaram
That she hides in Sebarial’s camp
That Veil herself has killed her
quiz.e: He asks, “You killed her, didn’t you?” Shallan blushes, and he is delighted that Tyn picked an apprentice too capable.

quiz.q: How does Shallan avoid leaving in her carriage?
o: She disguises herself as one of the Ghostbloods
She hides inside an illusion of a boulder
She slips into a nearby rocky cleft
She hides flat on top of the carriage roof
quiz.e: She makes an illusion of the boulder she drew for Mraize and hides in it, while Pattern tells the driver to leave as if she were inside.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan’s hiding place finally vanish?
o: The rain washes away the illusion
Pattern grows bored and wanders off
She has drained all her spheres dry
She falls asleep and loses her focus
quiz.e: Hours later the boulder dissolves into smoke: holding it without thinking, she had used up the Stormlight in every sphere.

quiz.q: What does Shallan find on her walk back to the warcamps?
o: Her coachman and his parshmen murdered
Bandits camped beside the road ahead
The Ghostbloods’ pavilion set ablaze
Adolin riding out to search for her
quiz.e: The carriage is half burned, the coachman’s throat cut and the parshmen dead; she blames herself.

chapters.title: The Rules of the Game
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Marked with a person’s initials, often as a decorative design.
A long, formal written work on a single subject.
How accurately a musician hits the right pitch of each note.
A long, angry speech of criticism or complaint.
Calm and casual, as if not especially interested.
A large building divided into rooms or flats for rent, usually crowded.
Completely astonished; too surprised to react.
Correct, polite behaviour according to accepted standards.
A collection of wild or unusual animals kept in cages for people to view.
Hidden beyond what is openly stated, as in an ulterior motive.
Someone who grabs any chance for personal gain, with little concern for principle.
A covered seat or litter carried on poles by bearers.
The jaws of an insect, crustacean or similar creature.
Long and winding, with many smooth curves.
A sheltered valley or cleft on Roshar, protected from the worst of the highstorms.
The King’s Wit, a sharp-tongued jester, met Kaladin in the last book, played a flute for him and left the flute with him.
After beating Elit, Adolin wagered six Shards on one bout against Relis, Ruthar’s son and the dueling champion.
After that duel, Shallan told Adolin she had remembered something from King Gavilar’s biography that could help him, if he won a duel in spectacular fashion.
Not long ago, Kaladin practised Lashing alone in the chasms at night, then flew high above the Shattered Plains with Syl.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin decide to guard Adolin himself today?
o: Adolin asked for him by name that morning
He fears Shallan could be an assassin
Dalinar ordered it after a new threat
The king had given him the day off
quiz.e: He doesn’t trust the foreign woman with a secret betrothal and no one to vouch for her; she could be an assassin, so Adolin gets “the best I have.”

quiz.q: What became of the flute Wit gave Kaladin?
o: It broke during a plateau run
He traded it to Rock for a meal
Syl hid it in his barracks room
He left it in Sadeas’s camp
quiz.e: When he gathered the remaining bridgemen from Sadeas’s camp he focused on people, not things, and forgot the flute among his possessions.

quiz.q: What does Shallan do when she recognizes Wit?
o: She hugs him tightly and thanks him
She slaps him for an old insult
She pretends not to know him at all
She orders him off the carriage
quiz.e: She lunges into an embrace, whispering that she always wanted to thank him and never had the chance. Adolin can’t believe she hugged Wit.

quiz.q: According to Ialai’s account, how did Sadeas get to kill Highprince Yenev?
o: He caught Yenev alone on a battlefield one night
He bribed the highjudge to name him champion
He won a showy duel and asked Gavilar a boon
He insulted Yenev at a royal wedding feast
quiz.e: At a tournament Sadeas won a spectacular duel; Gavilar offered him a boon, and Sadeas asked for Yenev’s “cowardly heart” on his sword, then killed him in a duel.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin at first say the plan wouldn’t really mean anything?
o: Sadeas would keep his title and authority
Duels are forbidden while the army is at war
Gavilar’s old laws have since been repealed
Adolin no longer holds any dueling rank
quiz.e: It’s just a game, he says: Adolin might win Sadeas’s Shards, but his title and authority would stay the same. Shallan answers that it’s about perception.

quiz.q: What does Shallan learn by grabbing the “devil rock” through the bars?
o: It has a poisonous sting
Its skin is cold and slimy
It cannot see out of its eyes
It is warm to the touch
quiz.e: It pulls away and puffs itself up, but she notes that it is warm to the touch: “Truly warm-blooded.”

quiz.q: What does Kaladin confess to Syl at the menagerie?
o: He wants to go back to being a surgeon
He has begun to trust Shallan Davar
He never felt so alive as in his bridge days
He regrets leaving Sadeas’s warcamp
quiz.e: His time as a bridgeman was the worst of his life, yet he never felt so alive as in those final weeks. Syl asks if he’s almost ready, and he says he is.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar announce about Amaram at the menagerie?
o: He is to take over from Kaladin as guard captain
He leads the newly refounded Knights Radiant
He will duel Sadeas on the king’s behalf
He has been named Elhokar’s new heir
quiz.e: Under the king’s direction Dalinar has refounded the Knights Radiant; Amaram was the first to speak the oaths and stands at their head, wearing a cloak with their double-eye symbol.

chapters.title: Whitespine Uncaged
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Showing disrespect toward God or sacred things.
Uncertain and dangerous; likely to fall or fail.
A group of attendants or advisers travelling with an important person.
Refusing to obey a superior’s orders.
A metal container holding burning coals or fire.
Unable to act or move normally, especially through injury.
A vivid example that teaches a lesson by being seen.
A piece of armour that protects the forearm.
A piece of armour that covers the shoulder.
To lose or give up something, often as the penalty for withdrawing or breaking a rule.
Extremely, often unreasonably, suspicious of others.
In a proud, commanding way that expects obedience.
A raised platform, often for a seat of honour.
Agreed rules or customs governing an activity.
A prayer written in glyphs and burned as an offering to the Almighty.
Moash took Kaladin to meet Graves, a lighteyed man whose group wants the king dead so Dalinar will take the throne. Kaladin told Moash not to meet with them again.
Adolin bet six Shards on a bout with Relis, set for two days later in the arena.
Relis is Highprince Ruthar’s son and the dueling champion. His cousin Elit lost the Plate Relis had given him to Adolin in their last duel.
The gruff swordmaster in Dalinar’s camp who trains Adolin.

quiz.q: Where does Kaladin order Moash to go, starting tomorrow?
o: To guard Brightness Navani every day
To train recruits alongside Teft
On a deep patrol toward New Natanan
Into Sadeas’s camp to watch Amaram
quiz.e: He wants Moash away when they move against Graves and his people. Moash admits he met them once more and insists that what they’re doing is right.

quiz.q: What does Adolin discover is missing just before he puts on his Plate?
o: His mother’s chain, his good-luck charm
The glyphward Shallan painted for him
His usual meal of chicken and curry
The breakaway cloak bearing his glyphpair
quiz.e: He ate two plates of chicken and spoke to his sword, but the chain isn’t in either pocket; Renarin sends a runner who won’t be back in time.

quiz.q: How does Sadeas justify Relis bringing three other Shardbearers?
o: The king himself approved the change
Adolin’s Plate is stronger than any of theirs
A champion may always choose the format
Adolin set no number when he challenged
quiz.e: Adolin said “I’ll fight you and whomever you bring” without naming a number, making it a full disadvantaged duel, and told the highjudge he understood.

quiz.q: What does Adolin take Zahel’s shouted advice to mean?
o: Keep his back pressed to the wall
Attack with fury so they hesitate
Yield before they can cripple him
Strike the man in the King’s Plate
quiz.e: “You’re not cornered . . . Show them why.” Adolin attacks furiously, giving them no time to respond, hoping to intimidate them into hesitating.

quiz.q: Why does Elhokar refuse to let Dalinar go down and fight?
o: He thinks Sadeas wants Dalinar killed there
He wants the duel to teach Adolin a lesson
He means to go down and fight there himself
The conventions forbid anyone from helping
quiz.e: When Sadeas goads Dalinar, Elhokar warns that Sadeas wants an “accident”: all four would attack Dalinar before he got into stance.

quiz.q: What does Relis threaten if Adolin surrenders or has the king end the bout?
o: Istow will award all the Kholin lands to Relis
Elit will keep the Plate he lost
Abrobadar’s sword might slip on Renarin
Jakamav will shame him in every camp
quiz.e: Abrobadar is keeping Renarin, who has no Plate, busy; if Adolin gives up, Abrobadar’s sword “might just slip.”

quiz.q: What reason does Istow give for refusing to call the fight?
o: The king has not asked her to end it
The crowd has paid to see a full bout
Sadeas has forbidden her to stop it
The duel’s terms have not been met
quiz.e: She says Adolin has neither surrendered nor been incapacitated, so the terms haven’t been met, and asks whether Dalinar has no respect for the law.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin ask of Dalinar before dropping into the arena?
o: To lend him the king’s Shardblade
To take care of his men if it goes badly
To keep Amaram well away from him
To forgive Moash for disobeying him
quiz.e: After whispering “Honor is dead,” Kaladin says he’ll see what he can do and asks Dalinar to take care of his men if it goes poorly, then vaults over the wall.

chapters.title: To Kill the Wind
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A gap in the wording of a rule or agreement that lets someone get around it.
Injured so badly that part of the body is permanently damaged.
The piece of armour that protects the forearm.
Not caring or not interested either way.
Something used to put pressure on a person and force them to do what you want.
Made unable to act, move or fight.
Melted by great heat into a glowing liquid.
Confused and unable to think clearly.
Made on the spot from whatever is at hand.
Requiring great effort; slow and hard.
To echo and shake with sound.
A favour or gift, especially one granted by a ruler.
Setting right a wrong, or payment for a wrong done.
To lose a contest or a right because of breaking a rule or giving up.

In the last book Kaladin killed a Shardbearer to save Amaram. Amaram had Kaladin’s squad murdered to keep the Shards, and branded Kaladin a slave. Dalinar, his old friend, asked Kaladin for proof and has since made Amaram the first of the refounded Knights Radiant.
From Ialai’s account of an old duel, Shallan suggested Adolin wow the crowd, earn a boon from the king, and use it to demand the Right of Challenge against Sadeas.
Adolin agreed to fight Relis “and whomever you bring”, so four Shardbearers came out: Relis in black, his cousin Elit with a hammer, Abrobadar in orange and Jakamav, Adolin’s friend, in green.
Renarin went onto the sands with a Blade but no Plate. No lighteyes would help, so Kaladin told Dalinar “Honor is dead” and jumped down himself, spear in hand.
Kaladin keeps his Stormlight hidden from the camp. It heals his wounds and lets him Lash himself, making him fall in any direction.

quiz.q: What does Shallan ask Pattern to do during the fight?
o: Distract the Shardbearer fighting Renarin
Whisper warnings to Adolin inside his helm
Find out which highprince bribed the judge
Fetch Dalinar down to the arena floor
quiz.e: She won’t meddle in Adolin’s fight, but sends Pattern to try to distract the Shardbearer facing Renarin so he isn’t maimed.

quiz.q: Why does Adolin ask Kaladin to keep an eye on Renarin?
o: Renarin had begged Kaladin to watch over him
The judge had threatened to disqualify him
The others might use him as leverage
Dalinar ordered Kaladin to guard him first
quiz.e: If things go badly for the three attacking Adolin, they might use his brother as leverage against them.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin knock Relis to the ground?
o: He sweeps his legs with the butt of his spear
He drops onto him from the top of the arena wall
He Lashes himself feet-first into Relis’s back
He throws sand through the eye slit of his helm
quiz.e: He Lashes himself toward Relis many times, so his kick hits like a long fall. It cracks Relis’s Plate and breaks Kaladin’s legs, which Stormlight heals.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin take from Elit after Elit yields?
o: His helm, worn on his hand as a shield
His hammer, to swing at Relis’s legs
His gauntlet, to help catch a Shardblade
His spheres, to refill his Stormlight
quiz.e: Shardplate fastens itself to its bearer, so the helm tightens around Kaladin’s wrist and he blocks Blades with it.

quiz.q: How does Adolin save Kaladin from Green Plate’s raised Blade?
o: He throws his own Shardblade across the arena
He hops onto Green Plate’s back and holds on
He calls on the judge to halt the bout at once
He shoves Relis into Green Plate from the side
quiz.e: Having beaten the man in orange, Adolin trudges over in nearly drained Plate and grapples Green Plate from behind; his Plate locks and both topple.

quiz.q: What happens when Kaladin catches Relis’s Shardblade?
o: Relis yields and kneels in the sand
The Blade shatters into molten light
Kaladin wrenches it from Relis’s grip
Relis drops it and flees, screaming
quiz.e: Kaladin hears a horrible scream; Relis drops the Blade, cries that he didn’t kill “you”, and runs into the preparation room, forfeiting.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin make Jakamav yield?
o: He threatens him with Relis’s Blade
He tears the helm off Jakamav’s head
He strikes his cracked breastplate
He presses a knife into a gap in his armor
quiz.e: With Adolin still holding Jakamav, Kaladin pushes his knife into an opening in the Plate and asks whether he will yield or be Kaladin’s second Shardbearer kill.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin demand as his boon?
o: To be raised to the rank of a lighteyed officer
A Right of Challenge against Amaram
Freedom for every bridgeman in the camps
That Sadeas be stripped of his Shardblade
quiz.e: He calls Amaram a murderer and demands to duel him. Amaram recognises him in horror, but the king orders Kaladin, not Amaram, arrested.

chapters.title: Never Again
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Saying false and damaging things about someone.
A person’s rank or position in society.
An official decision to forgive a crime and cancel its punishment.
A person controlled by someone else, like a doll worked by strings.
Someone who blames others for things they do themselves.
With the wrists or ankles locked in chains.
To make something seem less important by drawing attention away from it.
Small-minded; caring about minor things or personal grudges.
To quarrel noisily over unimportant things.
To speak with pauses and repeated sounds, from nerves or shock.
The flat sides of the head beside the eyes.
To gain an advantage over someone by being more clever or skilful.
A person who secretly passes on information.
After the duel, Adolin used the king’s boon to challenge Sadeas. Kaladin then demanded to duel Amaram, and the king ordered Kaladin’s arrest.
Kaladin earlier told Dalinar what Amaram did to him. Dalinar called Amaram one of the best men he knew and asked for proof.
Dalinar’s old Shardblade. In the last book he gave it to Sadeas in exchange for the bridgemen.
Highprince Sadeas betrayed Dalinar at the Tower. His wife, Ialai, works closely with him.

quiz.q: How has Sadeas answered Adolin’s challenge?
o: He has refused it as beneath his rank
He has agreed to duel in one year’s time
He has named a champion to fight for him
He has asked the king to forbid the duel
quiz.e: Adolin couldn’t pin the duel down, so Sadeas agreed to fight him in a year, when it likely won’t matter.

quiz.q: What punishment does Elhokar demand first?
o: Execution, the penalty for slander
A flogging in front of Bridge Four
Being sold back into slavery
Exile from the warcamps by night
quiz.e: He calls for execution, the law’s punishment for slandering a highlord; when Dalinar says he’d be an enemy, the king settles on prison.

quiz.q: What did Dalinar learn when he checked Kaladin’s claim?
o: Amaram’s records had been altered by scribes
Amaram had never served in Kaladin’s region
Witnesses say Amaram won his Blade recently
Amaram had been abroad during the battle
quiz.e: Seventeen witnesses said Amaram won his Shardblade only four months ago, long after Kaladin’s ledger says he was made a slave.

quiz.q: What question makes Dalinar hesitate?
o: Why Amaram didn’t fight to save his sons
Why the king wanted bridgemen as guards
Why Sadeas was allowed to leave the arena
Why the judge would not stop the duel
quiz.e: Kaladin asks why, if Amaram is so honorable, he didn’t help save Dalinar’s sons.

quiz.q: What does Sadeas tell Ialai to do?
o: Arrange a match to bind Adolin to them
Send a protest to the king’s court
Bribe the judges of the next duel
Use her spies to find a way to hurt Dalinar
quiz.e: She is to set every informant to find something to hurt Dalinar, and after that it will be time to use the assassins she has planted.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin tell Syl in his cell?
o: That he will break out before nightfall
That trusting lighteyes ends like this
That she should go and find Bridge Four
That Dalinar will free him before long
quiz.e: “This is what comes of trusting lighteyes,” he says. “Never again.”

chapters.label: Interlude I-9
chapters.title: Lift
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Round and swollen, like a bulb.
Something that sticks out from a surface.
A high-ranking government official or minister.
A person with the authority to judge or settle disputes.
A long pole weapon topped with an axe blade and a spike.
Twisting and curving gracefully, like a snake.
A ritual meant to drive an evil spirit out of a person or place.
Poor health caused by not eating enough, or not eating the right foods.
An object kept and honoured because it belonged to a holy or important person.
A private meeting of officials gathered to make a decision.
A short, thick club used as a weapon.
An officer in a royal household who attends on important people.
To hold something out for someone to take.
To formally demand the use of something, especially by an official.
A small crab-like creature common across Roshar.
A large nation in the west of Roshar. Sigzil, Bridge Four’s Azish member, speaks of its ruler as “the Prime”; the Alethi tend to call him the emperor.
Szeth has been killing kings and highprinces across the world. Early in this book, word reached the warcamps that the emperor of Azir was dead and Jah Keved was in turmoil.
Rare, priceless swords, each said to be worth a kingdom. A Shardbearer summons his Blade out of the air and dismisses it into mist.

quiz.q: Why does Lift insist that she is not twelve?
o: Her mother said she was only nine
Twelve is an unlucky number for an age
She has not seen twelve Weepings
Reshi never count years past ten
quiz.e: She says twelve is unlucky: if she can’t count an age on her fingers, it’s unlucky. Tigzikk counts her fingers as ten.

quiz.q: What does Lift insist on calling Wyndle, the vine spren with her?
o: Her pet Voidbringer
Her loyal honorspren
Her little cremling
Her lucky vinespren
quiz.e: She calls him her captured “pet Voidbringer”; he keeps protesting that he is a spren, not a Voidbringer.

quiz.q: How does Lift get through the thick window near the top of the dome?
o: She makes the frame Slick and slides it out
Wyndle grows through the latch and lifts it
She breaks the glass with her lucky sphere
She grows seeds into vines that pry it open
quiz.e: She throws seeds on the frame and makes them grow with her power; the vines crack the glass and pop the frame open.

quiz.q: What does Huqin’s crew actually mean to steal?
o: Spheres from the vizier quarters
Paintings from the long hallways
Fine clothing from the bedrooms
Jewelry from the Prime’s own rooms
quiz.e: Huqin says the clothes will sell for plenty; real riches are too well guarded, and a year or two of luxury is enough.

quiz.q: According to Gawx, how does someone become the new Prime?
o: By applying with forms and an essay
By winning a duel before the viziers
By being born into the last Prime’s line
By drawing lots among the scions
quiz.e: Viziers, scribes and arbiters may file the proper paperwork to apply, and the essay has to be really good. Even a clerk can apply.

quiz.q: What does Lift mean to do in the Prime’s quarters?
o: Steal the Prime’s ceremonial cap
Eat the important people’s dinner
Listen in on the viziers’ argument
Hide there until the palace empties
quiz.e: For two years she has sneaked into the hardest places to enter and eaten their dinners. Rich folk have the best food.

quiz.q: Why are the viziers struggling to choose a Prime?
o: The arbiters lost the applications
Two viziers both want the throne
The scions forbid any vote tonight
Nobody wants a job that means death
quiz.e: Two Primes were murdered within a week. Whoever they choose may be killed, so nobody wants the job; one calls it a death sentence.

quiz.q: How does Darkness stop Lift from using her power?
o: A small winged creature drains it
He shows her a gem that blinds her
His minion pours water on her hands
He binds her wrists in silver chains
quiz.e: He thrusts a bound, winged, cremling-like creature at her, and it drinks the glowing power out of her. He orders spheres kept from her.

quiz.q: Why does Darkness slap the minion who cut Gawx’s throat?
o: He let Lift slip free while doing it
He did it in front of the viziers
He lacked the paperwork to kill him
He used his Shardblade carelessly
quiz.e: Darkness says the minion had not done the proper paperwork in this kingdom to kill the boy: without the law, there is nothing.

quiz.q: Why do the viziers and scions declare Gawx the new Prime?
o: He knew every law in the codes
He returned to life before them
His uncle Huqin bribed the vote
He alone had applied in person
quiz.e: He was dead and came back. A scion calls the Regrowth a miracle, and they take it as a sign of a Prime who can survive the One All White.

chapters.label: Interlude I-10
chapters.title: Szeth
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: To think deeply about something for a long time.
To wait hidden, often with a threatening air.
A low wall along the edge of a roof or tower.
Very steep, almost straight up and down.
Forced to leave one’s homeland and not allowed back.
Quiet, focused thought, often as a spiritual practice.
Low hills at the base of a mountain range.
A gift given in worship or respect, as to a god.
An outcast among the Shin, bound to obey whoever holds his Oathstone.
The Shin assassin in white who killed King Gavilar. He hates the killing he is ordered to do but obeys, believing himself bound by his oath.
Earlier in this book, word came that the assassin had killed the king of Jah Keved, his heir and six highprinces. Then he attacked the Kholins.
When Szeth attacked Dalinar, Kaladin breathed in Stormlight and called himself a Windrunner. Szeth insisted that was impossible.
An ancient order of knights with strange powers. Most Alethi believe they betrayed mankind long ago.

quiz.q: Why does Szeth try to blink as little as possible?
o: The souls of his victims scream when he does
The thin mountain air has dried out his eyes
He fears missing an attack from the shadows
He is watching the sky for a coming storm
quiz.e: The souls of those he murdered lurk in shadows and scream whenever he shuts his eyes.

quiz.q: What is strange about the eastern side of the tower?
o: It is covered in carvings of the ten Heralds
It is sheer and flat, as if cut by a Blade
It has crumbled away into a heap of rubble
It is wound about by one spiral staircase
quiz.e: The east side is a sheer, flat face, as if sliced off by an enormous Shardblade, with glass windows facing the Origin.

quiz.q: What recent fight has shaken Szeth?
o: Losing a duel to a man in full Shardplate
Being driven off by a crowd of ardents
Facing a man who held Stormlight himself
Being wounded by a Parshendi warrior
quiz.e: He fought “an impossibility”: a man with Stormlight, who knew the storm within.

quiz.q: Why was Szeth banished from his homeland?
o: He refused to carry out a killing
He walked on the sacred stones
He stole a Shardblade from a shrine
He raised an alarm that was called false
quiz.e: He was banished for raising an alarm said to be false; they told him the Voidbringers and the powers of old were gone.

quiz.q: How do the villagers in the foothills treat Szeth?
o: They hide indoors until he has left
They set out spheres as offerings
They send riders to warn their lord
They beg him to rid them of bandits
quiz.e: They think him some kind of god and leave spheres for him, whose Light lets him travel on.

chapters.label: Interlude I-11
chapters.title: New Rhythms
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Something that gets in the way or slows progress.
To take smug pleasure in one’s own success or another’s misfortune.
Done openly and obviously, without trying to hide it.
To remove or wipe out completely.
Harsh, plain and impossible to miss.
To demand something loudly and insistently.
Certain to happen; impossible to avoid.
Practical and focused on results rather than ideas.
On the side sheltered from the wind.
Someone who openly disagrees with those in power.
A sudden, often violent seizure of power from a government.
To fix a feeling or idea firmly in someone’s mind over time.
