Chosen by the Five, Eshonai went into a highstorm with Venli’s captured spren and came out in stormform, with red eyes and a feeling of great power.
Eshonai’s sister, a scholar who has spent years studying the old songs. She claims enough listeners in stormform could summon a highstorm.
Meeting Adolin on a plateau, Eshonai told him there would be peace only when one side was dead, and that her people had changed the rules of the war.
Dalinar plans to march his whole army across the Plains during the Weeping, to bring the fight to the Parshendi.
Eshonai’s friend, a warform soldier who arranged the parley with the Alethi.

quiz.q: Why has Eshonai gone back to speaking in the old rhythms?
o: The new ones made some people nervous
The Five had forbidden the new rhythms
Venli told her to keep the new ones secret
The new ones could not be heard by others
quiz.e: At first she attuned the new rhythms often, but it made some people very nervous, so she forces herself to use the old ones.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai hear in one rhythm as she sits down?
o: The voices of the ancient listener gods
A song of Mourning sung by her mother
Something like her own voice screaming
Thunder from the next coming highstorm
quiz.e: It sounds like her own voice yelling at her in pain. Later she realises it is the Rhythm of Peace.

quiz.q: How many listeners does Eshonai want to take stormform?
o: Only the soldiers of her old division
The two hundred she has already picked
Every soldier, but none of the workers
Every single listener, of every form
quiz.e: Asked how many, she answers “All of us.” Davim hums to Amusement, thinking it a joke.

quiz.q: When does Eshonai plan to strike the Alethi with a storm?
o: While they sleep in their warcamps at night
While they cross the plateaus toward Narak
While they cut a gemheart from a chrysalis
While their highprinces meet for a feast
quiz.e: The humans will march together during the lull, exposed on the plateaus with no shelter; a highstorm then would destroy them.

quiz.q: What does Venli admit when Eshonai confronts her?
o: She had stolen her spren from the Five
She knew what the form would do to her
She had lied about summoning a storm
She had been meeting with the humans
quiz.e: Venli admits she knew exactly what stormform would do before she took it herself, but won’t say how she found out.

quiz.q: What does Eshonai do to stir the crowd below the spire?
o: Summons a tiny storm between her hands
Leaps from the top of the spire in Plate
Splits a boulder with her Shardblade
Leads them all in a song of Mourning
quiz.e: After claiming the Five would deny them the form, she conjures a miniature tempest of wind and red lightning, and the crowd sings to Awe.

quiz.q: Why won’t Eshonai have the dissenters killed yet?
o: Her own mother is among the group
The Five would turn the city on her
Many soldiers would resist the order
Venli still needs them to gather spren
quiz.e: She says many would resist; they must wait until all her soldiers are transformed, when they won’t object.

quiz.q: How do the dissenters escape?
o: They slip away dressed as stormforms
They are rescued by an Alethi patrol
They hide in the crowd at the center
They cut a bridge and climb into the chasms
quiz.e: Led by their guards under Thude, they cut down a bridge and used its ropes to climb into the chasms. Eshonai says the coming storm will kill them.

chapters.title: Fleet
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A break or relief from something unpleasant.
To tease or provoke someone in a mocking way.
A phrase or idea used so often that it has lost its force.
Broken up at intervals by something sharp or sudden.
Traditional stories and knowledge handed down over time.
Not discouraged or put off by difficulty or danger.
Acting without thinking about the risks.
Striking again and again, as strong wind or waves do.
The cost or damage that something causes over time.
A small crab-like creature, common all over Roshar.
After the duel in the arena, Kaladin accused Highlord Amaram of murder and demanded to duel him. The king had Kaladin locked up instead; Dalinar promised to get him free once Elhokar cooled down.
Moash has fallen in with men who plot against King Elhokar and believe the kingdom would be better off without him. Kaladin has met them; their leader, Graves, wants Kaladin to give them an opening.
The king’s sharp-tongued Wit, who dresses all in black. In the last book he told Kaladin a story and left him a flute, which Kaladin later left behind in Sadeas’s camp.
The great storms of Roshar sweep in from the east and weaken as they travel west. Shinovar, in the far west, barely feels them.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin think he might be able to do with a sphere on the wall?
o: Use it to signal his men outside
Draw its Stormlight into his cell
Bribe a guard to unlock the door
Smash it to light the lock’s gears
quiz.e: It is only a little farther than the Parshendi were when he drew Light from their gemstones.

quiz.q: How does Syl answer when Kaladin says breaking out would be against the law?
o: Spren are not bound by a king’s laws
She will not help him break any law
Laws don’t matter; what’s right does
Dalinar would rewrite the law for him
quiz.e: “I’m no highspren,” she says. “Laws don’t matter; what’s right matters.”

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin call Elhokar a terrible king?
o: He praised Kaladin, then would execute him
He has never fought on a single plateau
He keeps Dalinar out of his war councils
He doubled the taxes on the darkeyes
quiz.e: Elhokar first lauded him for protecting him, and now would execute him at a snap of his fingers. Kaladin decides Moash’s friends are right.

quiz.q: Why does Wit say he likes visiting people in prison?
o: The guards always pay him for his songs
Prisoners are the only ones who listen
He hopes to learn the secrets they keep
He can say anything and they can’t act
quiz.e: He can say whatever he wants to them, “and they can’t do anything about it.” He has come for a story.

quiz.q: Why does Wit change the animals in his children’s story?
o: Kaladin doesn’t know what a bunny rabbit is
Kaladin says it is far too childish for him
Syl laughs at the idea of a talking chick
The guards outside complain of the noise
quiz.e: Kaladin is puzzled by the chick and the “bunny rabbit,” so Wit swaps in wet slime and a seventeen-legged crab thing on a rainy day.

quiz.q: Whom had Fleet raced and beaten long before his race with the storm?
o: A Shin messenger
The king of Azir
The Herald Chan-a-rach
A Thaylen champion
quiz.e: Wit sings that in times long past Fleet raced the Herald Chan-a-rach, and won.

quiz.q: Which land does Kaladin name when Fleet faces his final mountains?
o: Jah Keved
Shinovar
Alethkar
Azir
quiz.e: After Azir’s plains, Kaladin whispers “Shinovar,” and Wit sings of the Misted Mountains guarding Shin.

quiz.q: In Wit’s ending, what happens after Fleet falls dead?
o: The storm buries him and the race is forgotten
Chan-a-rach carries his body to the sea
He wakes at dawn and walks the last mile
The storm halts there, and his soul races on
quiz.e: Kaladin says Fleet died. Wit agrees, but sings that the storm stopped at his body and his soul rose in the winds, forever free to race them.

chapters.title: Veil Walks
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: In an unsteady way that looks likely to fall.
Searched or groped about hurriedly with the hands.
A figure of speech that describes one thing as if it were another.
The ability to feel and be aware.
Saying the opposite of what you mean, to mock or amuse.
Placing two very different things side by side for contrast.
To recover from illness or exhaustion.
A long, distinct period of history.
A picture made from many small pieces of tile, stone or glass.
Smaller and dependent on a larger, more important place.
A raised platform, often for a throne or speaker.
Made up or invented, often to deceive.
She lives in Highprince Sebarial’s warcamp, keeping his accounts and reporting to his companion Palona, while being courted by Adolin Kholin.
Disguised, Shallan sneaked into Highlord Amaram’s rooms and copied his maps and notes about the Shattered Plains.
Jasnah believed the lost city of Urithiru could be reached from the Shattered Plains. Shallan has taken up her research.
The darkeyed woman Shallan disguises herself as with an illusion when dealing with the Ghostbloods.
Shallan can make illusions from Stormlight, usually by first drawing what she wants to create.

quiz.q: Where does Shallan argue that Stormseat, the old capital of Natanatan, really stood?
o: On the Shattered Plains
In the hills near Dawn’s Shadow
Under the city of Kholinar
On the shores of the Origin
quiz.e: The old map is wildly inaccurate, she says; Stormseat was on the Shattered Plains, not in the mountains the map points to.

quiz.q: What does Pattern find odd about Shallan tonight?
o: She has drawn nothing all day
She is awake during second moon
She refuses to answer Adolin
She is working without spheres
quiz.e: It is second moon, when she always sleeps, but tonight she can’t: her head surges with too many ideas.

quiz.q: Why did Shallan slip a page about Urithiru into her reports to Palona?
o: To prove that Jasnah’s notes are really hers
To warn Sebarial away from the Plains
So Sebarial might take her onto the Plains
To repay a favour to Sebarial’s scribes
quiz.e: If Sebarial thinks there is something valuable out there besides gemhearts, he might take her out with his armies in case Adolin’s promises fail.

quiz.q: What reason is Shallan given for Navani not meeting her?
o: She is busy with a new fabrial
She has gone back to Kholinar
She won’t see Sebarial’s people
She is caring for a sick Dalinar
quiz.e: The reply says Navani is busy caring for Dalinar, who has come down with a sickness and withdrawn for a few days.

quiz.q: Where did Pattern hear his joke about “the tip”?
o: From Vathah’s men
From Adolin’s officers
From Sebarial at dinner
From one of Jasnah’s books
quiz.e: Shallan guesses he heard it from Vathah’s men, and he admits it. He then explains it at length.

quiz.q: Why, Shallan realises, did no two maps agree on where Urithiru lay?
o: Mapmakers were forbidden to draw it
People reached it by Oathgate, not on foot
It moved each time a great highstorm passed
Jasnah’s rivals had altered the maps
quiz.e: Ten Oathgates linked the capitals of the Epoch Kingdoms to Urithiru; you went to the nearest city with one instead of walking.

quiz.q: What image does Shallan create without drawing it first?
o: Jasnah reading at her desk
Her father at the high table
Herself as a frightened girl
Her brother Helaran’s face
quiz.e: It is Shallan curled on the bed, unable to weep or laugh: the girl she believes she really is.

quiz.q: What happens when Shallan attaches the Veil illusion to Pattern?
o: It speaks aloud in Pattern’s own voice
It walks perfectly, even down stairs
It vanishes the instant he moves
It moves with him, but glides oddly
quiz.e: The image follows Pattern, but it glides like light reflected from a spoon rather than walking. She still counts it a victory.

chapters.title: Obedience
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Coaxed or persuaded with gentle urging.
Going far beyond what is usual or reasonable.
A natural layer of stone or ore found in the ground.
A noble who holds land from, and owes loyalty to, a higher lord.
The servant who manages a large household.
Tough and wrinkled, like old leather.
A building where dogs or similar animals are kept.
Something kept in reserve as protection against loss.
A sturdy, locked box for valuables.
A Vorin priest or priestess, who may be owned by a lord.
A large, loyal hunting animal kept like a dog.
Small spren that appear around someone who is hurt.
The lowest rank of lighteyed society.
Her father is Brightlord Lin Davar of Jah Keved. Her brothers at home are Balat, Wikim and Jushu; Helaran, the heir, left years ago.
She died when Shallan was a child. Her brothers believe their father killed her; Shallan insists he did not.
Shallan’s stepmother, her father’s second wife, not many years older than Shallan.
The daughter of Brightlord Tavinar, whom Balat cares for.

quiz.q: How does Father punish Shallan when she angers him?
o: He takes away her books
He beats others in her name
He locks her in the cellar
He sends her tutors away
quiz.e: He has proven he will not touch her; instead, he beats others in her name.

quiz.q: What discovery improves Father’s fortunes?
o: A gem cache in the old cellars
A royal pardon for his debts
A silver seam under the manor
A marble deposit on his lands
quiz.e: A new marble deposit gives him resources for his promises, bribes and deals.

quiz.q: Whom does Father suggest Balat consider instead of Eylita?
o: Sudi Valam, the highprince’s daughter
A younger sister of his wife Malise
The heir of a rich Thaylen merchant
A cousin of the lord of House Tavinar
quiz.e: He calls House Tavinar not ambitious enough and suggests Sudi Valam, the highprince’s daughter, who is in her fifties.

quiz.q: What does Father do after Balat calls him a murderer?
o: Strikes Balat across the face
Has Balat’s new pups killed
Sends Balat to Vedenar alone
Disowns Balat before the hall
quiz.e: He claims the axehound pups caught a sickness and sends a guard out with a sword to put them down.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan refuse to leave with Balat?
o: She is waiting for Helaran’s return
She fears life as a scribe in Vedenar
She believes someone must help Father
Eylita doesn’t want her coming along
quiz.e: Something awful has hold of Father; if they all leave, they give him to it. She also won’t leave Jushu and Wikim.

quiz.q: What does Shallan overhear Father order Rin to do?
o: Bring Balat back from the city
Have Eylita’s family thrown out
Spy on Malise and her letters
Kill Helaran and take his Blade
quiz.e: He wants Helaran’s head; the Shardblade will be Rin’s while he serves House Davar. Malise then confronts Father.

chapters.title: The One Who Killed Promises
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A place to stay or live.
A crusty growth that spreads over rocks and is hard to scrape off.
To shut someone out of a group or community.
A noble sworn to serve a higher lord.
A lighteyes of the tenth dahn, the lowest lighteyed rank.
To turn someone unfriendly or make them stop supporting you.
The stated reasons behind a decision.
Kaladin is locked up for challenging Highlord Amaram in front of the court. Wit visited him there and sang him the story of Fleet.

Moash told Kaladin his grandparents, silversmiths in Kholinar, died in the palace dungeons waiting for an inquest that Elhokar, then left in charge of the kingdom, never approved. A lighteyed rival of theirs was Elhokar’s friend.
Moash and a group led by a man named Graves want Elhokar removed, and asked Kaladin, who commands the King’s Guard, to give them an opening.
Dalinar made Kaladin, a darkeyes, captain of his guard, with Bridge Four protecting the Kholins and the king.

quiz.q: What happens to Kaladin’s cell at night?
o: Guards rattle the bars to keep him awake
Highstorm winds shake its walls all night
The spheres are taken, leaving him in dark
His bridgemen sing to him through a vent
quiz.e: They take the spheres away at night, and he imagines being buried deep under miles of stone.

quiz.q: What does Syl tell Kaladin she saw at the fight?
o: A Cryptic, a type of spren
A Shin assassin in white
An honorspren in the crowd
A Parshendi spy by the gate
quiz.e: There was a Cryptic there. She says they are looking for someone: soon he might not be alone.

quiz.q: How does Dalinar ask Kaladin to think of his imprisonment?
o: As a penance set by the ardents
As a duty to guard this room
As a siege he must wait out
As a lesson the king requires
quiz.e: If ordered to guard a room for a week, Kaladin would; so, “Guard this room.” Kaladin jokes he’ll protect the chamber pot.

quiz.q: Who, Dalinar says, led Elhokar into the silversmiths affair?
o: Highlord Meridas Amaram
Queen Aesudan herself
Highprince Torol Sadeas
Roshone, a lesser lord
quiz.e: Roshone owned silversmith shops and had Elhokar’s ear. Kaladin realises he is the citylord who ruined his family.

quiz.q: Why was Roshone exiled rather than made a tenner?
o: He was Sadeas’s man, with powerful cousins
He paid a heavy fine into the royal coffers
He had once saved Gavilar’s life in battle
The ardents of Kholinar begged for mercy
quiz.e: Harsher punishment would have alienated allies, so Elhokar argued for leniency, Gavilar agreed, and Dalinar relented.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin decide by the end of the chapter?
o: To break out of prison that night
To tell Dalinar all about Moash
To resign his post once released
That the king has to die
quiz.e: Dalinar has a blind spot about his nephew; for the good of the kingdom and of Dalinar, Kaladin decides the king has to die.

chapters.title: A Burning World
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A large, crowded building divided into rented rooms.
Long, leaf-like growths of a plant.
An enclosed seat carried on poles by bearers.
An animal or person being hunted.
Lacking proper respect for God or religion.
A building where people living under religious rules live and work.
The giving of help or care.
A dark outline seen against a lighter background.
A rank in darkeyed society; the higher nahns have more rights and standing.
As Veil, Shallan has been working her way into the Ghostbloods, a secret society whose leader, Mraize, keeps testing her. After her last visit to him, her coachman and parshmen were found dead.
A short figure in a mask of carapace pieces who has appeared among the Ghostbloods.
Alethi men do not read or write, so Adolin’s spanreed messages to Shallan are written for him by someone else.
Amaram’s notes, which Shallan copied, show him mapping the Shattered Plains and seeking to bring back the Voidbringers rather than fight them.

quiz.q: How has Shallan hidden herself to watch the tree?
o: Rented a top-floor room facing the street
Enlarged a rooftop shed with an illusion
Waited inside a parked palanquin
Climbed into the branches above it
quiz.e: An illusion expands the shed atop a tenement, giving her a hidden place to watch for five hours.

quiz.q: What has Adolin arranged for Shallan?
o: A seat at Dalinar’s war councils
A private meeting with Navani
A tour of the king’s palace
A scouting trip past a harvested chrysalis
quiz.e: Dalinar will bring her on a scouting mission that can pass a chrysalis a day or so after it was harvested.

quiz.q: What does Iyatil say about Mraize?
o: He is her student, not her master
He is her cousin from beyond Azir
He owes her a debt of blood
He is her captain in the hunt
quiz.e: “He is not my master. He is my student,” she says, and won’t say in what.

quiz.q: How does Shallan get the palanquin past the guards at Dalinar’s camp?
o: She shows them a pass forged by Mraize
She pretends to be one of Sebarial’s scribes
She shows her real face at the window
She bribes a gate supervisor in advance
quiz.e: She drops her disguise and pushes her own face out; the guards know Adolin’s betrothed and wave her through. Iyatil guesses she bribed them.

quiz.q: What story does Shallan tell the ardents?
o: Her mistress needs a physician
Her sister has a highstorm fever
Her brother has gone mad in battle
A Voidbringer inhabits her sister
quiz.e: She claims her masked “sister” is possessed by a Voidbringer, and Iyatil plays along, raving.

quiz.q: What does the madman say when Shallan asks who he is?
o: Bordin, Dalinar’s footman
Talenel’Elin, Stonesinew
Gadol, a soldier of Kholinar
Vev, a stonemason from Azir
quiz.e: He answers “Talenel’Elin. The one you call Stonesinew,” almost the name of a Herald, then goes back to his recitation.

quiz.q: What makes the madman leap up and seize Shallan?
o: She asks him where he comes from
Pattern speaks aloud in the dark
She breathes out Stormlight
She draws her Shardblade near him
quiz.e: As she breathes out Stormlight to remake the ardent disguise, he pins her to the wall and whispers, “One of Ishar’s Knights.”

quiz.q: Who is among the people heading for the madman’s door?
o: Highlord Amaram
Highprince Dalinar
Mraize himself
Adolin Kholin
quiz.e: Several people approach the door as she tries to slip out, and one of them is Amaram.

chapters.title: Treasures
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A grain grown and eaten on Roshar, often served steamed.
The clay-like sediment left by storm rains, which slowly hardens into stone.
A small shelled creature, like a tiny crab or beetle, found everywhere.
Of a sphere: drained of Stormlight, so that it no longer glows.
Burning slowly without flame; of a feeling, simmering under the surface.
The uniform worn by the servants or soldiers of a particular household.
A hidden store of valuable things.
Very freely and over and over, in great quantity.
A covered seat or small room carried on poles by bearers.
Quiet, careful movement meant to avoid being noticed.
An Alethi woman’s right hand, which she may leave uncovered.
After the duel, Kaladin called Amaram a murderer and demanded to duel him. The king had him arrested and, after calling for execution, settled on prison.
At the menagerie, Kaladin saw a listless captive whitespine, and Shallan remarked that such beasts don’t do well in captivity.
Shallan learned that Amaram won his Blade from a young red-haired Veden assassin. She knows it as the Blade of her brother Helaran.

Disguised as Veil, Shallan got into a locked room in the monastery of Dalinar’s warcamp while the masked Ghostblood Iyatil played her raving sister. The madman inside, brought to camp by Dalinar’s trusted servant Bordin, gave his name as Talenel’Elin.
Mraize had told the other Ghostbloods they could kill Veil if they feared her, as a test of whether she was clever enough to join them.

quiz.q: What has Kaladin begun to imagine himself as?
o: A chull hauling a cart in the rain
The whitespine caged in the menagerie
A skyeel kept in a cramped tub
A soldier left behind on a lost battlefield
quiz.e: He pictures himself as the menagerie’s whitespine: a predator in a cage, wilted and confused, as Shallan said they become in captivity.

quiz.q: What happens when Kaladin strains for the wall sphere a second time, after praying?
o: The sphere cracks and goes dark at once
Syl blocks him from taking it
A guard walks in and stops him
Its Light streams into his fingers
quiz.e: At first nothing happens. After he prays, the Light resists, then streams into his fingertips. Later a guard finds the dun sphere, puzzled.

quiz.q: How does Shallan hide when Amaram comes into the madman’s room?
o: She turns herself and her clothes pure black
She takes on the look of a grey-robed ardent
She builds a false wall across the corner
She crawls beneath the madman’s narrow bed
quiz.e: She rejects becoming an ardent as too slow and has no time for a false wall; she makes everything about herself black and presses into the darkest corner.

quiz.q: What does Amaram say after he sees the madman’s face?
o: He asks which Herald the man truly is
He promises to take him home to Kholinar
He tells Gavilar that they have done it
He begs forgiveness for Gavilar’s death
quiz.e: He calls the madman “Great Prince” and beautiful, then says, “Gavilar, we have done it.”

quiz.q: What treasure does Bordin say the madman once spoke of?
o: A whole cache of Shardblades
A vault of uncut gemhearts
A chest of ancient Shardplate
A hoard of infused spheres
quiz.e: Bordin says the madman spoke once of a cache of Blades; Amaram calls them the Honorblades and leaves at once to search, since the place is close.

quiz.q: What does Mraize require of Veil now that she is accepted?
o: A drawing of every member she meets
A Shardblade taken from Amaram’s house
A full report on Dalinar every week
A specific tattoo, as a sign of loyalty
quiz.e: He says the others won’t touch her now, and she must get a particular tattoo, placed anywhere, and prove it when they next meet. “Welcome to the Ghostbloods.”

chapters.title: The One Who Deserves It
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Existing as a permanent, built-in part of something.
An unfair leaning for or against something.
Favouring new ideas and social change.
To arrange into layers or ranks.
Serious discussion or debate on a subject.
Something pleasant that few people can afford or enjoy.
Filled with barely contained anger or turmoil.
Shyness and a lack of courage.
The edges of a roof that overhang the walls.
A thin, loosely woven cloth used to dress wounds.
A rigid strip bound to a broken limb to keep it still.
Acts of care, such as tending someone’s injuries.
A dog-like animal kept for hunting and as a pet, and bred in kennels.
In the earlier flashbacks, the head of House Davar grew colder and more violent. He would not strike Shallan; instead he beat others in her name.

In the last flashback, Shallan overheard her father tell Rin, captain of his new guards, to find Helaran in Valath and bring back his head. Her stepmother Malise confronted him, and a furious shouting match followed.
Balat refused to give up Eylita Tavinar, whom Father called too low for him. When Balat defied him, Father had Balat’s new axehound pups put down.
Shallan’s brother, a Shardbearer who left home years ago. Balat said he had met Helaran in secret, and that Helaran told him to watch over the family.
King Gavilar’s daughter, a famous scholar and author, who would later take Shallan as her ward.

quiz.q: According to the passage Shallan reads, what does Jasnah argue?
o: Women should be scholars before wives
Every woman’s place is set by her rank
Each woman must make her own role
Women must reclaim their ancient roles
quiz.e: Jasnah rejects defining a “place” for women at all: there is a role for each woman, which she must make for herself.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan think the guards are posted in the hallway?
o: To stop Malise from trying to flee
To keep Shallan shut away in her room
To watch for Helaran’s return
To guard her father’s strongbox
quiz.e: She doubts Father knows she overheard his order; the guards are there to see that Malise does not flee.

quiz.q: What does Shallan bring her father in the feast hall?
o: A bowl of his favorite spiced curry
A sealed letter sent from the highprince
A cup of chilled orange wine
His favorite: warm, spiced violet wine
quiz.e: She mixes his favorite, deep violet wine spiced with cinnamon and warmed, and finds his eyes free of darkness for once.

quiz.q: What crunches under Shallan’s feet as she reaches Balat?
o: Shards of a broken wine bottle
Claws pulled off of cremlings
Bones of the axehound pups
Dried husks of rockbud shells
quiz.e: The ground is littered with claws Balat has pulled from cremlings one after another; she shivers.

quiz.q: When does Shallan suggest that Balat should flee?
o: During the next highstorm
On the night of a great feast
While Father is away in Vedenar
As soon as Helaran sends men
quiz.e: Father plans another trip to Vedenar in a few months; Balat can leave then and get a head start, after they arrange by letter to meet Helaran.

quiz.q: What does Malise ask as Shallan is leaving?
o: Who he will hit, once she and Balat go
Whether Shallan will come away with them
Why Shallan never calls her Mother
Whether Helaran even knows of her
quiz.e: She wonders who he will hate and hit then: “Maybe you, finally? The one who actually deserves it?” Shallan whispers, “Maybe.”

chapters.title: Stormblessings
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Twisted or false versions of the truth.
An official release from the punishment for a crime.
On the side sheltered from the wind.
A ridiculous, pointless situation or pretence.
A young or minor prince; often said mockingly.
Rude and disrespectful, especially to someone of higher rank.
Boldly daring, sometimes to the point of rudeness.
The attendants and followers who accompany an important person.
The piece of armour that covers the shoulder.
When Adolin and Renarin’s fight against four Shardbearers turned against them, Kaladin leaped into the arena without armour. Together they won: Relis fled the ring and Jakamav yielded.
Kaladin then called Amaram a murderer and demanded to duel him, and the king had him imprisoned. In the confusion, Sadeas slipped out of Adolin’s challenge.
In the last book, Kaladin killed a Shardbearer to save Amaram and turned down the Shards. Amaram had Kaladin’s men killed, kept the Shards himself and had Kaladin branded a slave.
Moash took Kaladin to meet Graves, a lighteyed man whose group wants King Elhokar dead so that Dalinar will rule.

quiz.q: What does the jailer tell Kaladin as he opens the cell?
o: The king signed a pardon; he keeps his rank
He is to be exiled from the warcamps at dawn
Dalinar has paid a heavy fine for his release
He will be tried before the highprinces
quiz.e: The king signed a pardon that day, and they didn’t even strip his rank or position. “Guess you’re lucky.”

quiz.q: Why was Adolin also locked in the prison?
o: The king punished him for the duel
Sadeas had him arrested for slandering him
He shut himself in while Kaladin was held
He struck a highjudge after the duel
quiz.e: Adolin insisted on staying in a cell as long as Kaladin was there; that was the disturbance Kaladin heard early on.

quiz.q: Why does Adolin say he has always wondered about Amaram?
o: Amaram never seems to do anything wrong
Amaram once insulted Dalinar at a feast
Amaram cheated in a duel years ago
Amaram refused to fight beside Gavilar
quiz.e: Even Dalinar loses his temper and makes mistakes; Amaram’s spotless image smells to Adolin of someone working too hard on his reputation.

quiz.q: Besides the set offered to Kaladin, who gets a complete set of the new Shards?
o: Renarin Kholin
Highprince Hatham
Brightlord Teshav
General Khal
quiz.e: One full set goes to General Khal, two sets of Plate to lighteyed officers, and the last full set is for Kaladin.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin refuse the Shards for himself?
o: He thinks Adolin is mocking him
Blades have killed too many he loves
He hopes to win a set of Shards of his own
Dalinar ordered him not to accept
quiz.e: He can’t look at or touch a Blade without seeing blood. He wants the lives of people like him to change, not to become a lighteyes himself.

quiz.q: What has Rock been doing while Kaladin was in prison?
o: Cooking a fresh stew for every single day
Saving his best spices for a feast
Simmering one pot of stew for weeks
Shaving off his beard in protest
quiz.e: Teft explains he has kept a single “celebratory stew” simmering for weeks, tending it at night and letting nobody taste it.

quiz.q: How did Teft deal with the men’s talk of breaking Kaladin out?
o: He reported it to Dalinar
He beat some sense into them
He drew up the escape plan
He sent them to ask Adolin
quiz.e: He beat some sense into them: every good soldier spends a day or two locked up, and they hadn’t demoted Kaladin.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin tell Moash once they are alone?
o: To sell the Shards to a foreign king
To stay away from Graves’s group
To give the Shards back to Adolin
That he agrees with his friends’ plan
quiz.e: He says Moash’s friends are right and he will help them accomplish their task, because he thinks it is what Alethkar needs.

chapters.title: Spit and Bile
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A path that zigzags back and forth up or down a steep slope.
Fitted with pipes to carry water.
Decoration added to make something look attractive.
A formal written work that discusses a subject in depth.
Behaviour that follows accepted standards of politeness and decency.
A small remaining trace of something that once existed.
Poisonous; also spiteful and full of malice.
A calm, casual air of not caring.
An insulting word for a very stupid person.
A striking public display, especially one that draws stares.
To prove someone right or clear them of blame.
Too sacred or important to be questioned or interfered with.
During highstorms Dalinar lives through visions of the distant past, and Navani writes down what he says in them. By the end of the last book they had convinced him that the Almighty is dead.
Dalinar has no memory of his late wife; he cannot even hear her name when others say it.
Dalinar plans to march out onto the Shattered Plains to end the war, and is still seeking highprinces willing to go with him.

Dalinar refounded the Knights Radiant with Amaram at their head, wearing a cloak with their double-eye symbol. Kaladin asked why, if Amaram was so honourable, he did not help save Dalinar’s sons in the duel.
The King’s Wit, a black-clad jester whose job is to mock people. He recently visited Kaladin in prison and sang him the tale of Fleet, a runner who raced a storm.

quiz.q: What question led Rushu to the discovery Navani describes?
o: Why a Blade can be summoned with a dun gem
Why no two Shardblades weigh the same
Why some Blades have a cracked gemstone
Why Blades will not cut fabrial steel
quiz.e: Rushu asked why a Blade can be summoned and dismissed even when its gemstone is dun; an old fragment suggests gemstones were added only later, to let men bond Blades.

quiz.q: Why does Navani’s question about his late wife unsettle Dalinar?
o: He still blames Gavilar for her death
He cannot remember her at all
He has sworn never to speak of her
He fears Navani resents her memory
quiz.e: It isn’t a difficult question; he simply doesn’t remember his wife and can’t even hear her name, a hole he can go weeks without noticing.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar praise when he approaches Vamah?
o: The mercenary companies in his army
The rare liquor he brings to feasts
The discipline of his warcamp’s guard
The way he uses his light cavalry
quiz.e: He asks how Vamah decides when to risk an all-out cavalry assault, but Vamah is distracted by laughter across the island.

quiz.q: What are the papers being passed around the feast?
o: Forged orders written in Dalinar’s name
Navani’s records of his visions, altered
Copies of Kaladin’s charges on Amaram
Private letters from Dalinar to Navani
quiz.e: They are Navani’s accounts of his visions, with the tone changed to sound ridiculous and a mocking commentary added in another hand.

quiz.q: Why does Wit refuse to shake Amaram’s hand?
o: He fears Amaram means to strike him
He claims his own hands are filthy
He says Amaram’s hands only look clean
He never touches a man who bears a Blade
quiz.e: He doesn’t want “it” to rub off on him: whatever Amaram uses to make his hands look clean.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar promise the crowd from atop the food table?
o: To duel any man who mocks him again
To give up the command of his army
To find whoever stole Navani’s pages
To publish every vision he receives
quiz.e: He says what they read is true, that each new vision will be published for scholars to study, and that if they must laugh, they should look him in the eyes.

quiz.q: How does Wit answer when Dalinar asks whether he is a tyrant?
o: Yes, and one this world needs today
No; a tyrant would never ask that
Only in the eyes of Highprince Sadeas
Not yet, though he is close to it
quiz.e: Wit says softly that he is, but calls this an era for tyrants: a benevolent tyrant is better than weak rule.

quiz.q: Who does Wit say must not find him?
o: The Assassin in White
The Herald of War
The father of hatred
The Parshendi’s gods
quiz.e: He must go carefully, because if “the one you fight . . . the father of hatred” finds him, his soul would be shredded beyond repair.

chapters.title: Bridges
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: On the side sheltered from the wind.
Bold and resourceful; willing to try new things.
So surprised that you cannot speak or react.
Secretive, as if sharing a plot with someone.
Treating something complicated as if it were much simpler than it is.
To move something in small, locking steps, as a toothed gear does.
Able to bend and move easily; flexible.
A covered seat carried on poles by bearers.
Heavy, slow and awkward to move.
A regular fixed payment, such as an allowance.
Calm and casual, as if not really interested.
Layers of rock or other material laid down one on top of another.
Too annoying or arrogant to put up with.
When Kaladin came out of prison, Adolin let him decide who would get a full set of Shards Adolin had won in the arena. Kaladin gave them to Moash.
Moash and a group led by a man named Graves want King Elhokar dead. After his imprisonment, Kaladin told Moash that he now agreed with them.
The Shin assassin who killed Gavilar has attacked Elhokar’s palace and been driven off. Kaladin fought him there and survived a fall with him.
Dalinar’s son Renarin has been spending his time with Bridge Four, wearing their uniform.
Adolin arranged for Shallan to come along on one of Dalinar’s scouting missions so she could study a chasmfiend chrysalis that had already been harvested.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin believe Syl is keeping Stormlight from him?
o: His refusal to ride Dalinar’s horses
His promise to help Moash kill the king
His failure to save more of Bridge Four
His harsh words to Shallan at the feast
quiz.e: She tells him he is “making bad choices,” and he takes it to mean his promise to help assassinate the king.

quiz.q: What did the vaulter scout see out on the Plains?
o: A Parshendi army gathering at night
A chasmfiend climbing out of a chasm
Red lights over unexplored plateaus
A glowing man flying back and forth
quiz.e: He saw a glowing man flying over the Plains; Dalinar says it was the Assassin in White.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin tell Dalinar about Renarin?
o: Bridge Four suits a misfit like him
He ought to go back to Zahel’s lessons
He is too frail to carry a bridge yet
The men resent having a prince with them
quiz.e: Calling Renarin a misfit, awkward and alone, Kaladin says Bridge Four is probably the best place he could be.

quiz.q: What is the newest plan for killing the king, according to Moash?
o: Moash will strike him with his Blade
Poison will be slipped into his wine
Graves will shoot him with an arrow
Parshendi will ambush him on a run
quiz.e: Kaladin only has to lead the king to the right spot, and Graves, an excellent shot, will fell him with his own bow.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin advise Adolin about fighting the assassin?
o: Wait for the archers to wear him down
Fight him only from horseback
Pin him against a wall before striking
Strike straight for the head or spine
quiz.e: Kaladin saw the assassin heal a wound, so he tells Adolin not to try a weakening blow first but go right for the kill.

quiz.q: What does the rock Adolin slices open reveal?
o: White stone from a structure built long ago
A hollow core packed with uncut gemstones
Old Parshendi carvings of a chasmfiend
Fresh crem laid down only a year ago
quiz.e: The core is white, quarried-looking stone under centuries of crem, so a structure must once have stood there.

quiz.q: Why is Shallan angry with Kaladin?
o: He laughed at her for studying the moss on the rock
He told Adolin she was only playing at scholarship
He mocked Adolin in words meant to go over his head
He refused to let her ride ahead of the vanguard
quiz.e: She says he called Adolin obnoxious in a way he knew Adolin wouldn’t understand, to make a fool of a man who is trying to be nice.

quiz.q: Where has Kaladin seen the carpenter with the birthmark before?
o: Outside his prison cell
In Sadeas’s lumberyards
In the dueling arena
Among Amaram’s soldiers
quiz.e: It clicks just as the man reaches for a lever: he oversaw bridge construction in Sadeas’s lumberyards. He pulls the lever and the bridge collapses.

chapters.title: Nothing
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Strange and dreamlike, as if not quite real.
Apparently, or for the stated reason, though perhaps not the true one.
Untidy and messy in hair or clothing.
A very narrow, deep gorge cut into rock by running water.
A sudden, violent flood caused by heavy rain.
Believing in luck, omens or magic rather than reason.
To talk at length about unimportant things.
To talk foolishly and on and on.
To speak quickly and make little sense.
To make a gentle bubbling sound, or to babble.
To cheat someone out of money or rights.
The hard outer shell of an animal such as a crab or beetle.
Spren drawn to rot and infection in wounds.
As bridgemen in Sadeas’s army, Kaladin and Bridge Four spent long days in the chasms collecting gear from the dead. Highstorm rain turns those chasms into deadly floods.
Dalinar is preparing to march onto the Plains toward their unexplored center during the Weeping, the weeks of steady rain with no highstorms.
Coached by the con woman Tyn, Shallan once played a haughty foreigner and talked a soldier out of his boots on the road. That soldier was Kaladin, and he has been cold to her ever since.
After Kaladin accused Amaram of murder before the king, he was jailed for weeks. Adolin later joined him in prison by choice.
Shallan’s spren, a shifting pattern of lines that can ride on her dress and talk with her.

quiz.q: What gives Kaladin a breath of Stormlight as he falls?
o: He grabs a sphere from Shallan
He seizes Adolin’s Plate
Syl lets out a terrible scream
Dalinar shouts an order to him
quiz.e: He can’t draw Stormlight until Syl screams, a terrified, painful sound; then he gets a breath of it before hitting the ground.

quiz.q: What does Shallan say about the dead soldier whose spheres lit her way?
o: He was killed before he fell
He was one of her own guards
He held a map of the chasms
He still breathed when she came
quiz.e: His sphere pouch had ripped, and she shivers to say he had been killed by something before the fall.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin explain their survival to Shallan?
o: Vines on the walls broke their fall
They landed in a deep, soft bog
A rope caught them partway down
Windspren may have protected them
quiz.e: He cites folktales of windspren protecting people as they fall, hoping she won’t think of the stories of Kaladin Stormblessed.

quiz.q: When, by Shallan’s notes, is the next highstorm coming?
o: At dawn the day after tomorrow
Tomorrow night after first moonset
Later tonight, before midnight
In a week, on the next Lightday
quiz.e: She checks her pages: the last highstorm before the Weeping comes tomorrow night, just after first moonset.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan have no map with her?
o: Hers fell into a pool when she landed
She had been using Brightness Velat’s
Kaladin had thrown hers into the chasm
Adolin had kept it in his saddlebag
quiz.e: She didn’t bring her own; Brightness Velat has the maps, and Shallan was using hers.

quiz.q: What puzzles Shallan about the log bridging a pool?
o: It is carved with Parshendi glyphs
It is still covered in living moss
Someone had cut it with a Shardblade
Stumpweights shouldn’t grow out here
quiz.e: It’s too cold for stumpweights on this part of the Plains; a highstorm must have carried the trunk some four hundred miles.

quiz.q: What example does Kaladin give of Shallan toying with people beneath her?
o: Taking his boots while posing as someone else
Making her guards carry her through the chasms
Ordering Adolin to cut the moss for her sketch
Mocking the palanquin porters for being slow
quiz.e: He reminds her she stole his boots and bullied a darkeyed guard while pretending to be someone she wasn’t. She has no answer.

quiz.q: What makes Kaladin and Shallan run at the end of the chapter?
o: A roar of distant floodwater
Parshendi singing above them
A scraping like carapace on rock
Their last sphere going dark
quiz.e: After their shouting match, a scraping sound echoes closer and closer through the chasms, so they run from it.

chapters.title: From a Nightmare
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Richly fertile and full of growing life.
Long and winding, moving with smooth curves.
The jaws or biting mouthparts of an insect or crab-like creature.
The decaying flesh of dead animals, eaten by scavengers.
To pass through the resting, cocooned stage between larva and adult.
A prayer written out in glyphs, often burned as an offering.
The smallest unit of meaning in a language.
A person's look, manner or bearing, showing their mood.
In a hushed, knowing way, as if sharing a secret.
As it appears or is claimed, though perhaps not truly.
Someone who pretends to be another person in order to deceive.
No longer worth discussing, because it can make no practical difference.
A brand marking a slave as dangerous.
When the bridge collapsed during Dalinar’s expedition, Kaladin and Shallan fell to the chasm floor and survived. As he fell, Kaladin could not draw in Stormlight, and Syl let out a terrible scream.
Shallan’s notes say the next highstorm, the last before the Weeping, arrives the following night, just after first moonset. A storm’s floodwaters make the chasms deadly.
Shallan is betrothed to Adolin, and Kaladin guards the Kholin family. He has never trusted her, and their walk through the chasms began with a bitter argument about lighteyes.
Shallan believes Jasnah’s research shows that the parshmen are dangerous, and she has already asked Adolin how hard it would be to get them out of the warcamps.
The expedition was arranged so that Shallan could study a dead chasmfiend chrysalis, the shell a chasmfiend forms on a plateau, from which the armies race to harvest gemhearts.

quiz.q: How does Shallan finally lose the chasmfiend chasing them?
o: She leads them back to the fallen bodies
She hides them in a deep, cold pool
She drops their spheres down a side path
She has them climb a pile of debris
quiz.e: She leads them in a loop back to where the bridge fell; the beast stops to feed on the corpses of the fallen soldiers.

quiz.q: What else, according to Shallan, do the glowing arrow-shaped spren around the beast follow?
o: Highstorms
Whitespines
Skyeels
Greatshells
quiz.e: Shallan whispers that she has seen these spren before: they follow skyeels too.

quiz.q: What does Shallan sketch as a warm-up before drawing the chasmfiend?
o: Kaladin dressed as a bridgeman
The starspren in the sky above
The skeleton under the flowers
Their path as seen from above
quiz.e: She draws their route through the chasms as if viewed from above, more a picture than a map, then plays down how much she remembered.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin say Shallan had no need to come out to the chrysalis herself?
o: She could have had one towed back on a chull sled
A scribe could have sketched it for her at the site
Adolin had already sent her a full report of it
The Kholin library already held drawings of one
quiz.e: He points out that a chrysalis could have been hauled back on one of the chull sleds used for the wounded, so she must be after something more.

quiz.q: Why had Kaladin told his guards to stay close to Shallan and Adolin on the terrace?
o: He wanted to learn more about the Davar family
Dalinar had asked him to report on the courtship
He half suspected she meant to assassinate Adolin
He feared Sadeas’s spies would approach the pair
quiz.e: Kaladin admits that at the time he was half convinced she had come to assassinate Adolin, which is how his men overheard her talk of the parshmen.

quiz.q: If she got her way, what does Shallan say she would do about the parshmen?
o: Free them and pay them wages
Have them exiled
Put them to work in the mines
Have them executed
quiz.e: She would have them exiled. Kaladin replies that the lighteyes would then need more slaves, and honest men would end up branded.

quiz.q: By what does Shallan solemnly swear that she means no harm to Adolin’s family?
o: The memory of her late mother
The tenth name of the Almighty
The honour of House Davar
The Stormfather and the Heralds
quiz.e: She vows “by the tenth name of the Almighty” that she is sincere and wants only to prevent a disaster. Kaladin says he believes her.

quiz.q: What does the morning sun reveal at the end of the chapter?
o: The highstorm is coming early
They are almost back at camp
The chasmfiend is right behind
They have strayed south again
quiz.e: The sun rises over the wrong ridge: they are heading south instead of west, and Shallan asks for her satchel to draw it out.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A small group devoted to unusual and extreme religious beliefs.
A strange or improvised machine or device.
A scholar who studies and predicts the timing of highstorms.
Intensely painful or unbearably slow and frustrating.
Made of matching halves that mirror each other.
A tough cord of tissue joining muscle to bone.
A very small or inadequate amount of money.
A plant with wide, fanlike fronds that close up when disturbed.
A long, narrow crack or opening in rock.
Rubbish or debris that has been thrown or washed away.
The hard material that forms the shell of insects and crustaceans.
In a way meant to fend something off.
Bridge Four’s oldest member, who first noticed Kaladin drawing in Stormlight and knew old stories of the Knights Radiant.
Bridge Four’s educated Azish man, who is curious, precise and fond of asking questions.
Dalinar’s younger son, who has taken to wearing a Bridge Four uniform and serving alongside the bridgemen.
Kaladin and Shallan, stranded in the chasms after the bridge fell, are racing to walk back before the highstorm floods them. They have just learned they have drifted south off course.
Shallan can fix a scene in her mind by taking a “Memory” and later draw it in exact detail.

quiz.q: What did the Envisagers, the group Teft’s family belonged to, believe?
o: That the Heralds would reward those who fasted until death
That the Almighty would return to Roshar at the Weeping
That returning the Voidbringers would bring back the Radiants
That only a darkeyed king could unite the Alethi again
quiz.e: They thought if they could bring the Voidbringers back, the Knights Radiant would return too, and they put their own lives in danger to provoke powers.

quiz.q: What did Teft do about the Envisagers when he was a boy?
o: He ran away to join the army
He fled to a nearby town
He turned them in to the citylord
He burned down their meeting house
quiz.e: He turned them in. The citylord held a trial and had them all executed, and Teft later watched his father hang.

quiz.q: Why does Dalinar come to see the bridgemen keeping watch at the chasm?
o: To order them back to their barracks
To give them a new duty for the expedition
To ask Renarin to return to his rooms
To make sure they eat and avoid the storm
quiz.e: He has not come to order them away, only to see they care for themselves: no skipped meals, and no waiting out in a highstorm.

quiz.q: What does Shallan find odd about the plateaus near them?
o: They are taller than any she has seen
They match a mirrored group farther north
They do not appear on any of the maps
They are carved with ancient glyphs
quiz.e: The plateaus match a group farther north on the maps, exactly the same shape but mirrored, which leads her to realise the Plains form a pattern.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin say he knows the Shattered Plains are symmetrical?
o: Sigzil worked it out from maps
Dalinar’s scouts reported it
Syl flew high and told him so
He saw it in a dream
quiz.e: He says it came to him in a dream, where he saw the plateaus arranged in a wide symmetrical formation.

quiz.q: Whom does Shallan’s smile, after she speaks of being broken, remind Kaladin of?
o: His brother Tien
His mother Hesina
His friend Rock
His spren Syl
quiz.e: Seeing her smile despite her pain, Kaladin thinks that Tien always did that to him, even on the darkest day.

quiz.q: How do Kaladin and Shallan escape the chasmfiend’s charge?
o: They squeeze into a narrow fissure in the wall
They climb a tall heap of debris out of its reach
They dive into a deep pool and hold their breath
They hide behind the wreckage of a fallen bridge
quiz.e: Kaladin thrusts Shallan into a crack in the chasm wall, too small for the beast’s claw or leg to reach them.

quiz.q: What does Shallan do as Kaladin prepares to go out and face the beast?
o: She lights a sphere to blind the beast
She summons a Shardblade and offers it
She tears her skirt to make him a sling
She hands him her last infused spheres
quiz.e: Kaladin plans to lure the chasmfiend away so she can escape. She reaches over his shoulder, tells him to take “this,” and summons a Shardblade.

chapters.title: Selfish Reasons
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Droplets of water that form on a cold surface from moisture in the air.
The accepted rules of correct behaviour on formal occasions.
The hard outer shell of an animal such as a crab or beetle.
Floating wreckage or debris carried along by water.
A part of rock or growth that sticks up out of the ground.
A Rosharan plant that grows in stony, plate-like layers over rock.
The jaws or jaw-like mouthparts of an insect or crustacean.
The tough material that forms the shells of insects and crustaceans.
A thin fluid; used loosely for the blood of a strange creature.
The mouth or jaws of a large, hungry animal.
A tight band around a limb, used to stop heavy bleeding.
A show of boldness meant to impress others or hide fear.
The outward look of something; a rough version of it.
When a carpenter pulled a lever that dropped Dalinar’s bridge, Kaladin and Shallan fell into a chasm. They have been walking back toward the warcamps through the chasms.
The last highstorm before the Weeping is only hours away, and highstorms send floodwater surging through the chasms.
Since agreeing to help Moash’s plot against the king, Kaladin has had trouble drawing in Stormlight. He has not seen Syl since the fall.
A Shardblade kills living flesh rather than cutting it, but slices stone easily. Kaladin has never kept the Shards he won; most recently he gave a set to Moash.
A chasmfiend had trapped the two of them in a narrow crack. Kaladin chose to lure it away, and Shallan summoned a Shardblade for him.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin notice when his cheek brushes Shallan’s Shardblade?
o: The metal is burning hot against his skin
There is no screech in his mind at all
The Blade hums a low and steady note
Syl’s voice warns him to let it go
quiz.e: He hears none of the screech he heard when fighting beside Adolin, which he takes as a bad sign about his bond with Syl.

quiz.q: Why does Shallan ask Kaladin to lead the beast to the left?
o: That way leads straight to Dalinar
She has seen a way up to the plateau
Her spheres are hidden in that direction
She needs to get back to her satchel
quiz.e: Her satchel holds sketches showing the pattern of the Shattered Plains, which she needs to help Dalinar.

quiz.q: What happens when Kaladin grabs a sphere from a pool and tries to draw in its Light?
o: No power comes; he hears distant weeping
The sphere cracks and goes dark at once
Syl appears and lends him her strength
The Light rushes in and heals his leg
quiz.e: Straining for the Light, he hears weeping as if from far away, but no power enters him.

quiz.q: What appears beside Kaladin as the chasmfiend swings at him?
o: A glowing spearman from his dreams
A second chasmfiend, smaller and pale
A larger copy of Kaladin himself
Syl, grown to the size of a woman
quiz.e: A version of him half again as large stands with sword raised; the beast smashes it into a puff of Stormlight. It was one of Shallan’s illusions.

quiz.q: How does Kaladin finally kill the chasmfiend?
o: Cutting off its head with a single swing
Stabbing up through the roof of its mouth
Driving the Blade deep into its gemheart
Severing all the legs along one side
quiz.e: He stabbed through the roof of its mouth into the brain, and ended up with half his body inside its mouth.

quiz.q: How does the Shardblade give them a chance against the storm?
o: Cutting a tunnel into the next chasm
Slicing a raft from the beast’s shell
Felling vines to tie themselves down
Carving a hollow above the water line
quiz.e: Kaladin realises Shallan can cut stone; she carves handholds and a cubby high on the wall, above the water line.

quiz.q: What does Shallan’s Blade do as she struggles to cut higher?
o: It shrinks to the size of a big knife
It glows bright enough to light the wall
It vanishes and will not come back
It grows heavier with every cut made
quiz.e: The long Blade obligingly shrinks to a much shorter sword, really a big knife, and she thanks it.

quiz.q: What “selfish reason” does Shallan give for making Kaladin climb?

She wants his help with her satchel
She won’t be his last sight in a mess
She needs him to hold the light up
quiz.e: She won’t let his last sight be her in half a filthy dress, covered in purple blood, with her hair a mess.

Sail to Kharbranth to seek out Jasnah
Ride with Eylita to the highprince
Hide Malise away in a far village

To the guardhouse, to call for help
Out to the stables, to ready horses
Into Malise’s room, to warn her

He has joined the highprince’s guard
He has written to say he disowns them all
He is dead, killed in battle in Alethkar

Her stepmother Malise, dead
Wikim, hiding from Father
A stormshutter blown loose

He wounds Father deep in the chest
The sword pierces the coat and hits metal
He knocks the sword from Father’s hand
quiz.e: The blade barely misses, passing through Father’s coat and striking something metallic; Father is only grazed.

quiz.q: Why does Father collapse before he can strike Eylita?
o: Shallan put blackbane in his wine
Balat’s strike had cut too deep
Wikim struck him from behind
His heart gave out from all the rage
quiz.e: Shallan had poured him wine laced with the blackbane from the pouch Wikim gave her years before.

quiz.q: What does Jushu pull from Father’s coat pocket?
o: A letter from the highprince
A list of the new quarries
A purse of glowing spheres
A broken Soulcaster device
quiz.e: It is a Soulcaster of silvery chains and three gemstones, broken where Balat’s sword struck it.

quiz.q: What does Shallan whisper to her father at the very end?
o: A prayer for the Almighty’s mercy
The lullaby he sang to her
Her mother’s last words
A message for Helaran
quiz.e: Through tears she sings the lullaby he used to sing to her as a child when she was frightened.

chapters.title: Striding the Storm

quiz.q: How does Kaladin get up into the alcove as the water rises?

A burst of Stormlight lets him leap the gap
He wedges his spear in a crack to climb
Shallan heaves him up with sudden strength

quiz.q: What does a flash of lightning show in the floodwater?

The chasmfiend swimming toward them
Shallan’s satchel drifting off downstream
Bridge Four searching for them with ropes

quiz.q: Which name in Kaladin’s story makes Shallan gasp?

Sadeas
Tvlakv
Roshone
quiz.e: She gasps at the name of the slaver Tvlakv; she apparently knew him.

o: His days as a slave
Anything about Syl
The final bridge run
Rescuing Dalinar
quiz.e: He covers slavery, Bridge Four, the last bridge run and rescuing Dalinar, but says nothing of Syl; it hurts too much.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin realise as Shallan speaks of Helaran’s death?
o: Helaran must still be alive somewhere
Helaran once served in Sadeas’s army
Helaran was sold to the same slaver
He himself was the one who killed him
quiz.e: Shallan believes Amaram killed Helaran, but Kaladin realises Helaran was the Shardbearer he himself killed in Amaram’s army, something he has never told her.

quiz.q: What was Shallan’s plan when she first went to Jasnah?

Ask Jasnah to repair their Soulcaster
Study with Jasnah and never go home
Sell the family Soulcaster to Jasnah
quiz.e: She meant to swap the broken one for Jasnah’s working one; asking to have it fixed “would have been too rational.”

quiz.q: What does the Stormfather tell Kaladin about Syl?

She is hiding until he keeps his word
He has killed her; it cannot be fixed
She will return once he speaks the Words
quiz.e: The Stormfather says Kaladin has killed her, as men did before, and that he will not ride the winds again.

quiz.q: What does Kaladin find when the vision ends?
o: The sphere has crumbled into dust
The lost sphere is glowing again
The flood has taken Shallan’s satchel
His wounded leg is fully healed
quiz.e: The sphere Shallan dropped, which had gone dun, is now renewed and glowing.

Shallan’s spren, a Cryptic who speaks with a humming voice and is fascinated by lies.

Reach an accommodation with Sadeas
Let Amaram lead the march himself
Wait until the Weeping has ended

o: Shallan’s map of the chasms
A claw from the chasmfiend
A Shardblade from the chasms
The chasmfiend’s gemheart

Kaladin slew it with his spear
Bridge Four killed it in the chasms
The Parshendi left it behind there

She reads Navani’s private notes
Pattern listened and repeats it
She overhears them through a wall

They went to serve the Heralds
They all died in the Recreance
They chose new knights at once

quiz.q: What does Pattern say Shallan lacks in order to progress?

Words
Stormlight
Courage

quiz.q: Why does Shallan pull away from Adolin’s embrace?

He says the wedding must be delayed
He speaks of Kaladin with suspicion
He vows to protect her from all harm

quiz.q: What does Shallan urge Dalinar to do on the expedition?
o: Let Kaladin lead his guard again
Leave the parshmen behind in camp
Bring along all of Jasnah’s books
Make Adolin stay in the warcamp
quiz.e: Citing Jasnah’s belief that parshmen are dangerous, she asks him to march without them, and he agrees.

Her family bought the post for her

She lost a wager with another ardent

Barrels of wine meant for soldiers
The queen’s private stables

She would be sent to the warcamps
She would be sent away, quietly
She would be put on trial for theft

Why He allowed King Gavilar to be killed
Whether He truly sends the highstorms
Why He has sent no word to guide them

Painted the ten fools on its floor
Given away the queen’s food there
Burned a glyphward on the throne

They are quarreling among themselves

Once the Weeping has fully ended
After a final highstorm has passed
Only when the humans draw near

That the Shin want him to return
That Dalinar Kholin is now dead

o: Reading every single book in the palace library
Pointing out her mother’s logical fallacies
Refusing to set foot in the devotary
Correcting the royal scribes’ glyphs
quiz.e: Navani says Jasnah pointed out her logical fallacies when she tried to get her to bed on time.

quiz.q: What does Shallan tell Navani that Navani finds disturbing?
o: That Jasnah had planned to marry Amaram
That Jasnah could truly Soulcast unaided
That the Oathgate had already been found
That Sadeas’s men had sunk Jasnah’s ship
quiz.e: Shallan says Jasnah’s Soulcaster was a fake and that she was one of the Knights Radiant, swearing it on the tenth name of the Almighty.

quiz.q: When does Moash say the plotters will strike?
o: Once Dalinar is far out and committed
The very first night that the Weeping began
As soon as Kaladin’s leg has healed
On Lightday, when the countdown ends
quiz.e: They will wait until Dalinar is some distance away, maybe engaged with the enemy, so he won’t turn back when he hears.

quiz.q: How do the plotters plan to cover the killing?
o: Blame the whole attack on Sadeas’s soldiers
Make it look like the king fell drunk
Leave a Parshendi axe in the rooms
Claim the Assassin in White has been seen
quiz.e: Servants will be sent to hide as before, and everyone will believe the Shin assassin did it.

quiz.q: When Moash says Amaram is different because he’s a lighteyes, what does Kaladin reply?
o: That Graves is a lighteyes as well
That Shallan is lighteyed as well
That Moash is a lighteyes too now
That all lighteyes are murderers
quiz.e: Moash’s eyes have turned as light a tan as any Brightlord’s, the same color as Amaram’s. Moash is unsettled.

She weaves Stormlight into images, usually based on her own drawings.
Jasnah could Soulcast without a fabrial. Shallan has just told Navani this, and Navani found it disturbing.
During highstorms Dalinar sees scenes from the distant past. He has long feared they might be a sign of madness.
Dalinar named Amaram the first of his refounded Knights Radiant, then exposed him as a murderer and took away his cloak.
The deserter who once threatened Shallan on the road, now the leader of her guards.

quiz.q: How does Shallan’s drawing of Jasnah differ from her usual work?
o: It shows Jasnah as she was when just a young girl
It’s an interpretation, not an exact Memory
It was made as a gift to give to Navani
It was copied from an old court portrait
quiz.e: It re-creates Jasnah’s last night aboard ship from memory and imagination; Shallan is proud of capturing her contradictions.

quiz.q: Why does Pattern call creationspren useless?
o: They’re only drawn to someone else’s purpose
They copy shapes but cannot ever speak
They vanish as soon as the rain starts
They hide whenever Pattern comes near
quiz.e: Most spren have a purpose, he says; these merely flit around, watch and admire.

quiz.q: What did the artist Eleseth find after painting by red light for hours?
o: Her paintings came out redder with every hour
She could no longer see red at all
Her creationspren turned red as well
Her mind compensated and her colors balanced
quiz.e: At first she used too little red, but over hours her colors grew balanced; her mind adjusted to the light.

quiz.q: How does Dalinar react to Shallan’s illusion of Jasnah?
o: With tears, saying he is not mad after all
He draws his Blade, thinking it a hostile spren
He calls it a trick and storms outside
He orders her to show Adolin at once
quiz.e: An awespren bursts above him; he touches the image, his eyes fill with tears, and he says it is all true: “They’re returning.”

quiz.q: Why does Shallan refuse to be put in charge of the Radiants?
o: She thinks Adolin deserves the honor
Jasnah forbade her to lead anyone
She doesn’t yet know how to Soulcast
Her powers work best if nobody knows of them
quiz.e: If everyone is looking for her illusions, she says, she will never fool them. Dalinar is uneasy at “fool them.”

quiz.q: What does Dalinar say after Shallan refuses to be sent back?
o: That she’s as stubborn as Adolin
That she must obey him as a ward
That he sees Jasnah in her
That she’d make a fine general
quiz.e: He agrees to keep her secret, even from Navani, until she gives leave. Shallan takes it as a rare compliment.

quiz.q: What does Shallan find when she lifts the dead Parshendi’s eyelid?
o: The eye has a gemheart inside it
The eye beneath is entirely red
There is no eye there at all
The eye glows with Stormlight
quiz.e: She screams. Jasnah had a notebook of references to red eyes: the Voidbringers are here.

quiz.q: Who is the lone Parshendi sitting on the rock?
o: An envoy sent by Eshonai to parley
The scout who killed Bashin’s men
Shen, who once ran bridges with them
A parshman servant from Aladar’s camp
quiz.e: He calls to Skar and Leyten. Skar confirms it is Shen, changed, and that he wants to surrender to Dalinar.

chapters.title: Toward the Center
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

The parshman in Bridge Four whom Kaladin armed with a spear. Before vanishing, he told Kaladin, “My name is not Shen. It is Rlain.”
The Parshendi Shardbearer and warleader. On a plateau she told Adolin there would be peace only when one side was dead, and that her people had changed the rules.
Eshonai went out into a highstorm with a spren her sister had captured, and came out transformed, with red eyes and a feeling of great power.
Glyphs scratched in Dalinar’s quarters read “Thirty-two days. Seek the center.” The deadline falls in the middle of the Weeping.

quiz.q: Why has Dalinar put Teleb in charge of the prisoner?
o: Teleb captured him on the plateau
Teleb speaks the Parshendi tongue
Kaladin asked him to take on the duty himself
He dislikes how protective Bridge Four is
quiz.e: Dalinar doesn’t like how defensive the bridgemen are about him, though he invites Skar and Rock to the interrogation.

quiz.q: Why does Rlain answer Dalinar but none of the others?
o: Dalinar is his commanding officer
Dalinar has promised him his freedom
Dalinar once met Gavilar’s Parshendi
Dalinar holds a Shardblade to him
quiz.e: “You’re my commanding officer,” he says, and salutes like the other bridgemen.

quiz.q: How did Rlain hide among the parshmen?
o: He painted his skin to match theirs
He cut back his carapace every week
He took dullform, which looks like theirs
A spren disguised him with Stormlight
quiz.e: His people choose forms for the job required; dullform looks much like a parshman, and parshmen are rarely questioned.

quiz.q: What does Rlain say the red eyes mean?
o: A plague is killing the listeners
Their gods have returned
Eshonai has won a new Shardblade
The highstorms are about to fail
quiz.e: The gods are the souls of the ancient ones, he says; they hate humans, and the new form will bring something terrible.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar promise if Rlain leads them to his people?
o: To free every parshman in camp
To let him return home afterward
To make him a Shardbearer
To protect the noncombatants
quiz.e: Dalinar gives his word of honor that the noncombatants will be protected; Rlain is to describe the route to Shallan.

quiz.q: How long does Navani say remains until the countdown ends?
o: Three days
Thirty-two days
Two weeks
Ten days
quiz.e: Three days away, so Dalinar orders the armies to hasten their pace toward the center.

chapters.title: To Fight the Rain
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A short break from something hard or unpleasant.
Clay-like sediment left behind by storms, which hardens like stone over time.
The leading part of an advancing army.
A defended boundary around a position.
Short, clever and to the point.
To camp out in the open, as soldiers do.
Freedom to act as one wishes.
To attack an enemy again and again, wearing them down.
The special uniform or colours worn by a great household's servants.
Plain, strict living without comfort or luxury.
Proud and expecting to be obeyed.
Treating others as though they were beneath you.
Dalinar marched his army and those of Highprinces Aladar, Roion and Sebarial deep into the Shattered Plains, following Shallan’s maps. Kaladin, wounded in the chasms, stayed behind in the warcamp.
The quiet parshman of Bridge Four, whom the men called Shen, turned out to be a Parshendi spy named Rlain. Dalinar had him help Shallan map the route toward his people.
Following Jasnah’s research, Shallan hopes to find an Oathgate, an ancient pathway to Urithiru, in the ruined city of Stormseat at the heart of the Plains.
Numbers scrawled on walls during highstorms have been counting down the days toward something that will happen in the Weeping.
After Kaladin called Amaram a murderer and demanded a duel, Elhokar had him jailed. Kaladin has since told Moash he agrees with the plot to kill the king.

quiz.q: What does Shallan see in the distance from the top of the rock formation?
o: A Parshendi army drawn up in ranks
A great lake filling the chasms
A tall tower of pale white stone
A city coated in centuries of crem
quiz.e: Shadows in the misty rain, seen together, are unmistakably a city, covered over with centuries’ worth of crem.

quiz.q: What is wrong with the spyglass Gaz hands to Shallan?
o: It has fogged up on the inside
Its lens has a crack across it
Its brass tube is badly dented
Its far end is clogged with crem
quiz.e: It has fogged up at one end, and the fog is on the inside, so she can’t rub it clean.

quiz.q: What does Roion say he would do if he were the Parshendi?
o: Fall back into the stormlands and make the humans chase them
Form up as if to attack, then stall until the storms return
Strike at the supply lines and starve the army out slowly
Send envoys to talk of a truce while more troops arrive
quiz.e: He would make ready as if to attack but never do it, leaving the army stuck out there until the highstorms resumed.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar call Shallan once the highprinces have left?
o: His envoy to the Parshendi’s leaders
His chief scout for the inner plateaus
His backup plan, and perhaps their escape
His scribe to record the battle for the king
quiz.e: She is his backup plan: if the evil overwhelms them, her portal may be the only way out for the armies.

quiz.q: Why does Kaladin find himself smiling as he splashes through puddles?
o: He wears the boots Shallan stole from him
Lopen has tied an umbrella to his crutch
The rain has at last begun to let up
His leg has stopped hurting for the day
quiz.e: He smiles because he is wearing the boots Shallan stole, and thinks he never did believe she was a Horneater.

quiz.q: What does Elhokar ask of Kaladin?
o: To rejoin the King’s Guard under Moash
To carry a letter out to Dalinar’s army
To spy on the highprinces left in camp
To teach him how to be a hero to his men
quiz.e: Convinced Kaladin knows the secret of being a hero, he asks to be taught; he wants men to respect him as they did his father.

quiz.q: After saying Elhokar is a bad king, what does Kaladin suggest he do?
o: Lead the next battle in person
Step down for Alethkar’s sake
Ask Dalinar for daily counsel
Return to Kholinar to rule
quiz.e: Kaladin says he could do what is best for Alethkar and step down; Elhokar tells him not to overstep himself.

quiz.q: What does Elhokar say changed when Kaladin came?
o: Men began to cheer the king again
His nightmares grew much worse
The shadows he saw went away
Dalinar began to trust him more
quiz.e: He had seen shadows in mirrors and heard them whisper, but Kaladin frightened them; he hasn’t seen them since.

Bridge Four’s former parshman, revealed as a Parshendi spy, told Dalinar he believes everyone he loved has been destroyed and monsters left in their place.
Dalinar knows Shallan has powers like those of the Knights Radiant, though she insists she is not one yet.
Trapped in the chasms, Shallan realised that the plateaus of the Shattered Plains are laid out in a symmetrical, mirrored pattern.
A gruff, sarcastic ardent and swordmaster at the lighteyed training grounds, who teaches Adolin and agreed to give Kaladin lessons.
Moash and a man named Graves want King Elhokar dead. Their latest plan is for Kaladin to lead the king to a spot where Graves can shoot him.

quiz.q: Why does Dalinar wave away the umbrella offered to him?
o: He wants to feel which way the wind blows
It would mark him out as a target
If his men stand in the rain, so will he
Navani needs his hands free for fabrials
quiz.e: If his men had to stand in the rain, he would join them; he’d be soaked by the day’s end anyway.

quiz.q: What does Dalinar do when Aladar accuses him of leading them to slaughter?

Strips him of his command on the spot
Orders his guards to escort him away
Challenges him to a duel after the battle
quiz.e: Dalinar seizes Aladar’s jacket, tells him these are Voidbringers and they have a chance to stop them; Aladar leaves saluting.

quiz.q: What does Rlain say about the song the Parshendi begin to sing?
o: It is a lament for the listeners they lost
It calls on the Alethi to lay down arms
It is the song they sing before retreating
Its rhythm is one of destruction and power
quiz.e: He has never heard it, but calls it death, a rhythm of destruction, and begs Dalinar not to let them finish it.

quiz.q: Why have the ardents let the sparring grounds fill with rainwater?
o: To make a warm pool for bathing in
To wash the sand clean in the rain
To keep the crem from settling there
To stop anyone sparring in the Weeping
quiz.e: They stir the sand each day so the dirt floats away on the rain; Weeping rain carries no crem, so it’s good for washing.

quiz.q: What realisation brings Kaladin to his knees in the water?
o: The king is to Dalinar what Tien was to him
His spear skills have deserted him for good
Moash means to betray Dalinar as well
Zahel once served in Tien’s old army
quiz.e: Recalling the squadleader who sacrificed Tien to stay alive, he sees the king is Dalinar’s Tien: trying, but still failing.

quiz.q: What does Adolin find after the first flash throws him to the ground?
o: Skar and Drehy lying senseless nearby
His Shardblade has been knocked away
Sureblood dead, with a branching burn
A crater where the bridge once stood
quiz.e: Sureblood lies unmoving, a wide, jagged branching burn down his white coat, killed by the red lightning.

quiz.q: What does the newly arrived scout say is wrong with Shallan’s map?
o: The central plateau lies farther to the west
The chasms near the city are much narrower
Its eastern edge is mirrored the wrong way
One plateau is a circle, not long and thin
quiz.e: He says the plateau is a perfect circle with big gaps on either side, which wouldn’t match the pattern.

quiz.q: Whose voice does Dalinar recognise at the end of the chapter?
o: His dead brother Gavilar’s
The Almighty’s, from his visions
Rlain’s, speaking in rhythm
Eshonai’s, carried on the wind
quiz.e: A voice says it is sorry he has to die this way; he knows it from his visions as the voice of the Almighty.

chapters.title: For Glory Lit
chapters.intro: A few reminders from earlier in the series, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

Nervous and easily startled, especially of a horse.
Sorting the wounded by how urgently they need treatment.
Under attack and in serious difficulty.
